# Minerva Benefit Intelligence Strategy Evolution

**PDLC Phase:** Planning
**Authored Date:** 04/06/2026
**Cost Baseline:** Current $0.25-$0.27 per query → Target $0.08 per query (70% reduction)

---

## 📝 Executive Summary

Building on Minerva's strong agentic architecture, this strategic evolution acknowledges a critical business reality: **current per-query costs of $0.25-$0.27 threaten long-term profitability and scaling viability**. This cost-optimized strategy maintains all core capabilities—iterative plan data onboarding with intelligent quality management, formulary integration, and conversational AI excellence—while establishing a hard ceiling of **$0.08 per query** through aggressive architectural optimization, intelligent resource management, and operational efficiency improvements. This approach shifts from capability acceleration to sustainable unit economics, positioning Minerva for profitable conversational benefit intelligence at enterprise scale.

## 🎯 Strategic Context & Vision

* **Economic Reality:** Current operational costs of $0.25-$0.27 per query create unsustainable unit economics that will prevent profitable scaling regardless of capability sophistication
* **Cost Optimization Imperative:** Achieve 70% per-query cost reduction through architectural efficiency, intelligent resource allocation, and operational optimization while maintaining quality standards
* **Architectural Reality:** While the core Databricks platform enables powerful agentic processing, real-world profitability requires cost-efficient Self-Adapting systems that optimize computational resources without compromising accuracy
* **Paradigm Shift:** Traditional AI systems optimize for capability without considering unit economics. Our platform leverages Cost-Intelligent Self-Adapting Dynamic Baselines through Discovery (resource-efficient agent analysis), Verification (cost-aware human-in-the-loop processes), and Healing (cost-optimized automatic updates)
* **The Vision:** Deploy Minerva as a profitable conversational benefit intelligence platform with sub-second response times, intelligent context management, and cost-optimized Self-Adapting quality systems that maintain accuracy at <$0.08 per query

## 🚀 Key Architectural Evolution Areas

**Cost-Optimized Self-Adapting Framework:** Resource-efficient iterative plan data integration with cost-aware quality feedback loops, automated adjustment detection using optimized compute, and progressive accuracy improvements through cost-effective deployment cycles

**Efficient Multi-Source Intelligence:** Formulary data with cost-optimized ingestion pipelines, intelligent caching strategies, and resource-aware query routing that balances information quality with computational cost

**Cost-Efficient Conversational AI Foundation:** Optimized context window management, cost-aware conversation state persistence, sub-second response times through efficient architecture, and resource-optimized multi-turn capabilities

**Economic Learning Loop:** Cross-customer cost optimization patterns, resource-efficient dynamic baseline evolution, and deployment-specific cost management frameworks that improve unit economics with scale

## 📊 OKR Framework

### Objective (Qualitative)

**Transform Minerva into a cost-efficient conversational benefit intelligence platform with Self-Adapting dynamic baselines, multi-source intelligence capabilities, and enterprise-grade conversational AI performance achieving <$0.08 per query by Q1 2027**

### Key Results (Quantitative)

**KR1: Cost Optimization Excellence (Primary Priority)**

- **Q2 2026:** Establish baseline cost measurement and optimize core query processing to achieve $0.15 per query (44% reduction)
- **Q3 2026:** Implement resource-efficient architecture achieving $0.12 per query (55% reduction) while maintaining >95% accuracy
- **Q4 2026:** Deploy cost-intelligent scaling and optimization reaching $0.10 per query (63% reduction) across all customer environments
- **Q1 2027:** Achieve target $0.08 per query (70% reduction) with sustained quality and performance standards

**KR2: Cost-Aware Self-Adapting Plan Data Management**

- **Q2 2026:** Onboard all core plan types (IFP, SG, LG, Custom) with cost-optimized processing in partnership with Blue Shield of California
- **Q3 2026:** Establish cost-efficient iterative onboarding with 50% reduction in computational overhead for dynamic baseline improvement
- **Q4 2026:** Achieve automated plan data adjustment detection at 25% lower cost while maintaining 90% accuracy for data drift patterns
- **Q1 2027:** Sustain >99% plan data accuracy through cost-optimized Self-Adapting management across all customer environments

**KR3: Resource-Efficient Formulary Intelligence Capability**

- **Q2 2026:** Integrate formulary data with cost-optimized query logic achieving 40% processing efficiency improvement
- **Q3 2026:** Achieve >95% formulary query accuracy with intelligent cost-aware source selection and caching strategies
- **Q4 2026:** Implement cost-efficient cross-customer learning for formulary logic with 30% resource optimization

**KR4: Cost-Optimized Conversational AI Architecture**

- **Q2 2026:** Optimize context window achieving <1 second response times with 35% computational cost reduction
- **Q3 2026:** Implement cost-efficient conversation state management with 50% memory optimization
- **Q4 2026:** Deploy resource-optimized advanced memory architecture enabling 10+ turn conversations at 40% lower cost
- **Q1 2027:** Achieve conversational AI capability with <500ms average response time within $0.08 per query constraint

**KR5: Agent Experience & Adoption Excellence**

- **Q2 2026:** Deploy Low-Code/No-Code UI platform foundation with contextual interface reducing workflow disruption by 60%
- **Q3 2026:** Implement intelligent response architecture and real-time system feedback achieving >80% agent adoption and 45% parsing time reduction
- **Q4 2026:** Complete context-aware workflow integration and error handling framework reducing verification overhead by 50% and achieving >90% agent utilization
- **Q1 2027:** Sustain >95% agent satisfaction with cost-optimized UX achieving target adoption while maintaining $0.08 per query constraint

## 🔧 Strategic Capabilities Framework

### Capability 1: Cost-Intelligent Self-Adapting Data Quality Management

**Resource-Optimized Dynamic Baseline Framework**

- Cost-efficient customer-specific data quality baselines through optimized Discovery phase analysis
- Intelligent computational resource allocation for plan data inconsistency detection and pattern analysis
- Cost-aware iterative baseline refinement through efficient Verification processes and optimized Healing workflows
- Resource-efficient progressive accuracy improvement across deployment cycles with cost-intelligent pattern recognition

**Cost-Aware Quality Feedback Loop Architecture**

- Optimized real-time plan data quality scoring with efficient computational resource utilization
- Cost-intelligent automated flagging of plan modifications using efficient change detection algorithms
- Resource-optimized customer success team integration for complex plan interpretation edge cases
- Cost-efficient cross-customer learning repository with intelligent resource sharing and optimization

### Capability 2: Cost-Optimized Multi-Source Intelligence Engine

**Resource-Efficient Formulary Data Integration Architecture**

- Optimized external formulary data source connectors with intelligent caching and batch processing
- Cost-aware real-time formulary updates with efficient change monitoring and selective processing
- Resource-optimized medical necessity and prior authorization rule engine with intelligent rule caching
- Cost-efficient step therapy and alternative medication recommendation through optimized processing workflows

**Cost-Intelligent Query Routing Framework**

- Resource-optimized NLP-powered query classification with efficient model selection and caching strategies
- Cost-aware context-based source selection balancing information quality with computational overhead
- Optimized multi-source response synthesis with intelligent resource allocation for complex benefit scenarios
- Cost-efficient confidence scoring with optimized processing and intelligent result caching

### Capability 3: Cost-Optimized Advanced Conversational AI Foundation

**Resource-Efficient Context Window Optimization**

- Advanced cost-aware prompt compression reducing both token usage and computational overhead by 70%
- Intelligent cost-optimized context prioritization with efficient information ranking algorithms
- Resource-optimized dynamic context loading with cost-intelligent pre-loading and efficient caching strategies
- Cost-efficient sub-second response architecture with optimized parallel processing and resource sharing

**Cost-Aware Conversation State Management**

- Resource-optimized persistent conversation memory with intelligent storage optimization and efficient retrieval
- Cost-efficient member context preservation with optimized data compression and intelligent archiving
- Resource-optimized multi-turn conversation coherence with efficient reference resolution and context management
- Cost-intelligent personalized agent coaching with optimized analytics and efficient feedback processing

**Cost-Optimized Response Time Architecture**

- Resource-efficient parallel processing pipeline with intelligent load balancing and cost-aware resource allocation
- Cost-optimized predictive context loading with efficient pattern recognition and intelligent caching
- Resource-optimized edge computing integration with cost-effective data distribution and efficient processing
- Cost-intelligent advanced caching strategy with optimized storage utilization and efficient cache management

### Capability 4: Agent Experience & Adoption Excellence Framework

**Cost-Effective User Interface & Workflow Integration**

- Low-code/no-code UI platform enabling cost-efficient agent customization without development overhead
- Contextual panel architecture replacing disruptive full-screen interfaces with flexible, workflow-integrated design
- Cost-optimized Nexus integration supporting parallel verification workflows while maintaining resource efficiency
- Responsive interface design reducing training costs and support overhead through intuitive, adaptable user experience

**Intelligent Response Architecture & Information Management**

- Progressive disclosure framework reducing cognitive load while maintaining comprehensive information access
- Cost-aware response scoping matching information delivery to confirmed member intent and reducing unnecessary processing
- Visual hierarchy system distinguishing audit-complete scripts from contextual explanation, improving compliance efficiency
- Resource-optimized information selection balancing response completeness with cognitive load and processing cost

**Real-Time System Feedback & Agent Control Framework**

- Cost-efficient progress indication systems providing transparent processing visibility without resource overhead
- Intelligent user control mechanisms enabling query cancellation, rephrasing, and fallback actions with minimal cost impact
- System state visibility architecture communicating processing status and duration expectations through optimized feedback loops
- Resource-aware processing optimization maintaining responsive feedback while supporting cost targets

**Context-Aware Workflow & Error Recovery Integration**

- Seamless workflow integration enabling parallel verification and source transparency while maintaining cost efficiency
- Context preservation systems supporting audit trail requirements and compliance workflows through optimized data management
- Intelligent error handling with diagnostic states and guided recovery options reducing escalation costs and support overhead
- Cost-optimized fallback mechanisms ensuring service continuity while maintaining resource efficiency targets

## 🎟️ Implementation Themes

### Theme A: Unit Economics Excellence Over Feature Velocity

**Requirement 1:** Prioritize cost optimization in every architectural decision with mandatory cost impact assessment
**Requirement 2:** Establish comprehensive cost monitoring and alerting systems for real-time unit economics tracking
**Requirement 3:** Create cost-intelligent development workflows ensuring every feature contributes to cost reduction or revenue enhancement

### Theme B: Resource-Efficient Multi-Source Intelligence

**Requirement 1:** Complete formulary data integration with cost-optimized architecture by Q2 2026 end
**Requirement 2:** Achieve >90% source selection accuracy while reducing computational costs by 40%
**Requirement 3:** Implement cost-efficient formulary business rules with intelligent resource optimization

### Theme C: Cost-Optimized Conversational AI Excellence

**Requirement 1:** Achieve sub-second response times through cost-efficient architectural improvements
**Requirement 2:** Deploy cost-optimized context management enabling profitable multi-turn conversations
**Requirement 3:** Implement resource-efficient conversation intelligence with sustainable cost structure

### Theme D: Agent Experience & Adoption Excellence

**Requirement 1:** Deploy Low-Code/No-Code UI platform foundation by Q2 2026 end enabling cost-efficient agent customization and reducing training overhead
**Requirement 2:** Implement intelligent response architecture and real-time system feedback by Q3 2026 achieving >80% agent adoption rates
**Requirement 3:** Complete workflow integration and error handling frameworks by Q4 2026 enabling >90% agent utilization while maintaining cost targets

### Theme E: Profitable Enterprise Scaling

**Requirement 1:** Create deployment frameworks that reduce per-customer onboarding costs by 50%
**Requirement 2:** Establish cost-efficient cross-customer learning with optimized resource sharing
**Requirement 3:** Build cost-intelligent dynamic customization systems eliminating expensive custom development

## ⚠️ Risk & Mitigation Profile

**Enhanced Cost & Technical Risks:**

**Cost Reduction vs. Quality Trade-off:** Risk of accuracy degradation during aggressive cost optimization

- *Mitigation:* Comprehensive quality-cost balance framework with automated quality gates and cost monitoring at each optimization stage

**Resource Optimization Complexity:** Risk of over-optimization leading to system fragility or performance degradation

- *Mitigation:* Gradual optimization approach with comprehensive performance monitoring and automated rollback capabilities

**Cost Target Feasibility:** Risk of $0.08 target being technically unattainable while maintaining required quality standards

- *Mitigation:* Phased cost reduction approach with intermediate milestones, alternative architecture evaluation, and stakeholder expectation management

**New Cost-Specific Risk Areas:**

**Computational Resource Constraints:** Risk of resource optimization limiting system capacity during peak usage

- *Mitigation:* Intelligent auto-scaling with cost-aware resource allocation and peak demand prediction algorithms

**Cost Optimization Technical Debt:** Risk of short-term cost optimizations creating long-term technical debt and increased maintenance costs

- *Mitigation:* Architectural review process ensuring cost optimizations align with long-term technical strategy and maintainability

**Economic Model Sustainability:** Risk of cost reduction compromising revenue generation capabilities or customer satisfaction

- *Mitigation:* Revenue per query tracking, customer satisfaction monitoring, and economic impact assessment for all cost optimization decisions

**New UX & Adoption-Specific Risk Areas:**

**UX Development vs. Cost Optimization Trade-off:** Risk of UX improvement investments delaying or compromising primary cost reduction objectives

- *Mitigation:* Integrated development approach ensuring UX PRDs directly support cost optimization through improved adoption and reduced support overhead

**Agent Adoption During Transition:** Risk of decreased agent utilization during interface changes and training periods

- *Mitigation:* Phased rollout with parallel legacy support, comprehensive change management, and continuous agent feedback integration

**Low-Code Platform Complexity:** Risk of low-code/no-code customization creating system complexity that increases maintenance costs

- *Mitigation:* Structured customization framework with guardrails, automated testing for custom configurations, and controlled flexibility boundaries

## 🏥 Health Metrics

**Cost Optimization Excellence (Primary KPIs):**

- Per-query cost tracking with real-time monitoring and automated alerting for cost threshold breaches
- Cost reduction trajectory must show consistent progress toward $0.08 target with <5% monthly variance
- Resource utilization efficiency must improve by >10% quarterly while maintaining quality standards

**Cost-Aware Quality Excellence:**

- Customer-specific accuracy improvement maintaining >98% while reducing computational costs by 50%
- Plan data quality detection accuracy >90% achieved at 60% lower computational cost than baseline
- Cross-customer learning application must reduce per-customer costs while maintaining accuracy

**Resource-Efficient Performance:**

- Formulary query response accuracy >95% achieved at 40% lower processing cost than current baseline
- Intelligent query routing accuracy >90% with 35% reduction in computational overhead
- Multi-source response synthesis coherence >98% achieved at 45% lower resource cost

**Cost-Optimized Conversational AI Performance:**

- Average response time <500ms for 95th percentile achieved within $0.08 per query cost constraint
- Multi-turn conversation coherence >95% for 10+ turn sessions at 40% lower resource cost
- Conversation context accuracy >98% achieved with 50% memory optimization compared to baseline

**Agent Experience & Adoption Excellence (Critical Success Enabler):**

- Agent workflow disruption reduction trajectory showing consistent improvement toward 60% reduction target
- Interface customization adoption must exceed 80% within 30 days of Low-Code platform deployment
- Agent satisfaction scores >4.0/5 for system predictability and >4.5/5 for information clarity consistency
- Agent utilization progression: Q2: >40%, Q3: >70%, Q4: >90% sustained adoption rates
- Support ticket volume for UI/UX issues must decrease by 50% following each major UX improvement deployment

**Economic Health Metrics:**

- Unit economics trending toward profitability with clear cost reduction trajectory
- Customer lifetime value to acquisition cost ratio improvement through reduced operational expenses
- Resource efficiency gains translating to sustainable competitive pricing advantages

## 🗓️ Milestone Timeline

### Q2 2026

- Achieve $0.15 per query through core architecture optimization and initial resource efficiency improvements
- Complete cost-optimized expansion of all plan types with resource-efficient processing workflows
- Implement cost-aware formulary data integration with intelligent caching and batch processing
- Deploy cost-intelligent agentic plan analysis with optimized computational resource allocation
- **UX Foundation:** Deploy Low-Code/No-Code UI platform foundation with contextual panel architecture reducing workflow disruption by 60%

### Q3 2026

- Achieve $0.12 per query through advanced optimization and resource-efficient architecture deployment
- Implement cost-optimized conversation intelligence with efficient context management
- Establish resource-efficient conversation state management and optimized multi-turn capability
- Deploy cost-aware HITL baseline validation with optimized workflow efficiency
- **UX Intelligence:** Complete intelligent response architecture and real-time system feedback achieving >80% agent adoption and 45% parsing time reduction

### Q4 2026

- Achieve $0.10 per query through comprehensive cost optimization and efficient scaling architecture
- Onboard new customers with cost-optimized deployment and reduced onboarding computational overhead
- Implement resource-efficient cross-customer learning with intelligent cost sharing frameworks
- Establish cost-intelligent predictive quality management and optimized formulary business rules
- **UX Integration:** Deploy context-aware workflow integration and error handling framework reducing verification overhead by 50% and achieving >90% agent utilization

### Q1 2027

- Achieve target $0.08 per query through final optimization phase and efficient operational excellence
- Deploy cost-optimized advanced conversation coaching with resource-efficient personalization
- Complete additional customer onboarding with cost-intelligent dynamic deployment acceleration
- Validate profitable conversational AI excellence with sustainable cost-optimized operations model
- **UX Excellence:** Sustain >95% agent satisfaction with cost-optimized UX achieving target adoption while maintaining $0.08 per query constraint

## 💡 Innovation Opportunities

**Cost-Intelligent Predictive Guidance:** Leverage cost-optimized conversational intelligence to provide cost-effective member guidance and benefit optimization recommendations

**Resource-Efficient Formulary Intelligence:** Integrate cost-aware drug pricing optimization, generic alternatives, and therapeutic equivalency through efficient formulary processing

**Cost-Optimized Cross-Platform Intelligence:** Export cost-efficient conversational AI capabilities to other channels with optimized resource sharing

**Economic Regulatory Intelligence:** Implement cost-aware regulatory update detection with optimized impact assessment and efficient compliance processing

## 🔄 Success Criteria

**Cost Excellence:** Achieve $0.08 per query hard cap while maintaining all quality and performance standards established in capabilities framework

**Resource Optimization:** Each customer deployment must demonstrate measurable cost efficiency improvements that compound across the customer base

**Profitable Multi-Source Intelligence:** Formulary capabilities must provide differentiated value while operating within cost constraints and contributing to unit economics

**Sustainable Conversational Performance:** True multi-turn benefit consultations must be enabled with maintained accuracy, sub-second performance, and profitable cost structure

**Agent Experience & Adoption Excellence:** Achieve and sustain >90% agent utilization through cost-effective UX optimization that directly supports cost reduction objectives rather than adding overhead

**Economic Sustainability:** Platform must demonstrate clear path to profitability with industry-leading cost efficiency and sustainable competitive advantages enabled by high agent adoption rates

---

*This cost-optimized strategy recognizes that capability without profitability creates unsustainable business models. By establishing a hard $0.08 per query cost ceiling while maintaining quality, Minerva will achieve market-leading unit economics that enable sustainable growth, competitive pricing, and long-term platform viability in the conversational benefit intelligence market.*

# 🧩 Project Name: Sierra AI Conversational Agent for BCBS Customer Service

**PDLC Phase:** Implementation
**Authored Date:** March 16, 2026
**Status:** READY FOR REVIEW
**Template:** Feature-1-Pager-PRD
**Time Box:** 12 - 16 weeks

## 🎯 Problem Statement

BCBS customer service representatives handle thousands of routine inquiries daily about claims status, member benefits, FEP eligibility, and provider information, leading to high operational costs, inconsistent service quality, and longer wait times for members seeking immediate assistance.

**Impact:** High volume routine inquiries consume 60-70% of agent capacity, resulting in increased operational costs ($2M+ annually), member dissatisfaction due to wait times, and limited agent availability for complex issue resolution.

## 💡 Proposed Solution

Deploy Sierra AI's conversational AI agent integrated with BCBS systems (Facets, member databases) to handle routine customer inquiries through voice and chat channels, providing instant, accurate responses for claims status, benefits verification, FEP eligibility, and provider searches while seamlessly escalating complex issues to human agents.

## 👥 Target Users

**Primary Users:**

* **BCBS Members:** Health plan members seeking information about claims, benefits, eligibility, and provider networks through phone and digital channels
* **FEP Members:** Federal Employee Program participants needing specialized eligibility and benefits information
* **Customer Service Representatives:** Agents who will handle escalated complex inquiries and oversee AI performance

**Secondary Users:**

* **Healthcare Providers:** Medical professionals and their staff verifying patient eligibility and benefits information
* **BCBS Operations Team:** Staff monitoring AI performance, training models, and managing system integration
* **Compliance Team:** Personnel ensuring regulatory compliance and audit trail maintenance

## ✅ Success Metrics

* Increase automated query resolution rate from 0% to 75% for routine inquiries within 90 days
* Reduce average member wait time from 8 minutes to 2 minutes for handled query types 
* Achieve 90%+ accuracy rate for claims status, benefits, and eligibility responses
* Maintain 85%+ customer satisfaction score for AI-handled interactions
* Reduce operational costs by 40% for targeted inquiry categories

## 📦 Scope

**Phase 1 - Core Implementation:**
* Claims status inquiry automation using Facets integration via API endpoints
* Member benefits verification for standard and FEP plans
* Provider network search and verification capabilities
* Voice IVR integration for phone channel
* Chat integration for digital channels
* Real-time escalation to human agents for complex queries

**Phase 1 - Technical Components:**
* Sierra AI conversational engine deployment
* API integration with existing BCBS systems (Facets, member databases)
* SFTP secure data exchange setup
* Compliance logging and audit trail implementation
* Performance monitoring and analytics dashboard

## 🚫 Out-of-Scope

* Claims processing or adjudication functionality
* Member enrollment or plan changes
* Provider credentialing or network management
* Mobile app native integration (web-based only)
* Prior authorization processing
* Appeals and grievance handling
* Payment processing or billing inquiries

## 🏁 Definition of Done

* [ ] Sierra AI agent deployed to production with 99.5% uptime capability
* [ ] Claims inquiry API integration tested with real member data achieving <2 second response time
* [ ] Member benefits verification working for all standard and FEP plan types
* [ ] Voice IVR integration handling minimum 1000 concurrent calls
* [ ] Chat integration deployed across BCBS digital properties
* [ ] Escalation workflows tested with 100% successful handoff to human agents
* [ ] Compliance logging capturing all required audit information per regulatory requirements
* [ ] Performance monitoring dashboard operational with real-time metrics
* [ ] User acceptance testing completed with 90%+ task completion rate across all use cases
* [ ] Security and compliance review passed including PHI/PII protection validation
* [ ] Training completed for all customer service representatives on AI oversight procedures
* [ ] Pilot results documentation showing achievement of success metrics baseline

---

**T:** Requirements validated against Sierra pilot documentation and use case scenarios  
**C:** PRD created following mandatory PM Template Selection rules per UCAF Section 3  
**O:** PM-M3 Plan phase completed with comprehensive feature scope and success criteria defined

# Sierra AI FEP Implementation Plan

**Project:** Sierra AI Conversational Agent - FEP Enhanced Implementation  
**Date:** April 9, 2026  
**Document Version:** 1.0  
**Plan Owner:** Product Management  
**Implementation Period:** April 2026 - July 2026 (90 days)

---

## 📋 Executive Summary

This implementation plan builds upon the successful Sierra AI pilot (1,469 conversations, 4.06 CSAT) to deliver enhanced FEP capabilities with 75% automation rate, <2 minute handle times, and >4.5 CSAT for FEP members. The plan leverages pilot learnings and addresses federal compliance requirements through a phased 90-day approach.

**Key Success Factors from Pilot:**
- Strong 24/7 operational foundation established
- 30% containment rate provides optimization baseline  
- Successful 1m 48s GA interactions demonstrate efficiency potential
- 62.5% increase in member engagement validates approach

---

## 🚀 Implementation Phases

### 📅 Phase 1: Foundation & Integration (Days 1-30)

#### **Week 1-2: Technical Foundation**

**🔧 Core System Integration**
- **Facets API Enhancement**
  - Extend existing claims integration for FEP-specific data
  - Implement real-time eligibility verification (<2 sec response)
  - Add FEP member identification and validation
  - *Owner:* IT Integration Team | *Completion:* Day 10

- **OPM System Connectivity**
  - Establish secure connection to OPM eligibility systems
  - Implement federal employee verification workflows
  - Configure data synchronization schedules
  - *Owner:* IT Security Team | *Completion:* Day 14

**🛡️ Federal Compliance Setup**
- **Business Associate Agreements**
  - Execute federal BAAs with Sierra AI and sub-vendors
  - Complete HIPAA compliance validation
  - Implement audit trail requirements
  - *Owner:* Legal & Compliance | *Completion:* Day 7

- **Security Configuration**
  - Deploy FISMA-compliant security controls
  - Implement multi-factor authentication for federal data
  - Configure encrypted data transmission protocols
  - *Owner:* IT Security | *Completion:* Day 12

#### **Week 3-4: FEP Workflow Development**

**🤖 AI Model Enhancement**
- **FEP-Specific Training**
  - Develop FEP conversation flows based on pilot insights
  - Train AI on federal employee scenarios and terminology
  - Implement FEP-specific intent recognition patterns
  - *Owner:* Sierra AI Team | *Completion:* Day 21

- **Provider Directory Integration**
  - Integrate FEP provider network database
  - Implement real-time provider status verification
  - Configure provider search and verification APIs
  - *Owner:* Provider Relations + IT | *Completion:* Day 28

**📊 Phase 1 Success Criteria**
- [ ] Facets integration tested with 98%+ accuracy
- [ ] OPM connectivity operational with <2 sec response
- [ ] Federal compliance validation completed
- [ ] FEP conversation flows developed and unit tested

---

### 📅 Phase 2: Enhancement & Testing (Days 31-60)

#### **Week 5-6: Advanced Capabilities**

**🎯 Intelligent Automation**
- **Enhanced Intent Recognition**
  - Deploy advanced NLP models trained on 1,469 pilot conversations
  - Implement context-aware response generation
  - Configure automated escalation triggers
  - *Target:* Increase containment from 30% to 50%
  - *Owner:* Sierra AI + BSC Analytics | *Completion:* Day 42

- **Dynamic Provider Verification**
  - Real-time provider network status checking
  - Automated provider directory updates
  - Provider quality score integration
  - *Owner:* Provider Relations Team | *Completion:* Day 45

#### **Week 7-8: Quality & Performance Optimization**

**⚡ Performance Tuning**
- **Handle Time Optimization**
  - Leverage successful 1m 48s GA interaction patterns
  - Optimize response times based on pilot data analysis
  - Implement streamlined escalation procedures
  - *Target:* Reduce handle time from 13+ min to <5 min
  - *Owner:* Operations Excellence Team | *Completion:* Day 52

- **Customer Experience Enhancement**
  - Implement feedback loops from 4.06 CSAT baseline
  - Deploy personalized response capabilities
  - Configure satisfaction tracking and real-time adjustment
  - *Target:* Improve CSAT from 4.06 to >4.2
  - *Owner:* Customer Experience Team | *Completion:* Day 56

#### **Week 9: Comprehensive Testing**

**🧪 End-to-End Validation**
- **FEP Integration Testing**
  - Test complete FEP member journey scenarios
  - Validate eligibility verification accuracy (>98%)
  - Confirm provider directory functionality
  - *Owner:* QA + FEP Operations | *Completion:* Day 60

**📊 Phase 2 Success Criteria**
- [ ] 50%+ automation rate achieved in test environment
- [ ] Handle time reduced to <5 minutes average
- [ ] CSAT scores >4.2 in user acceptance testing
- [ ] 98%+ accuracy in FEP eligibility verification

---

### 📅 Phase 3: Production & Optimization (Days 61-90)

#### **Week 10-11: Production Deployment**

**🚀 Staged Rollout**
- **Pilot Production (25% Traffic)**
  - Deploy to limited FEP member segment
  - Monitor performance metrics in real-time
  - Implement immediate feedback and adjustment cycles
  - *Owen:* Operations Team | *Completion:* Day 70

- **Gradual Scale-Up (100% Traffic)**
  - Progressive increase to full FEP member base
  - Continuous performance monitoring and optimization
  - Real-time adjustment based on member feedback
  - *Owner:* Operations + Product Team | *Completion:* Day 75

#### **Week 12-13: Excellence Achievement**

**🎯 Target Performance Achievement**
- **Automation Excellence**
  - Achieve 75% automation rate for FEP interactions
  - Optimize containment strategies based on production data
  - Implement advanced AI learning from real interactions
  - *Owner:* Sierra AI + Analytics | *Completion:* Day 82

- **Customer Satisfaction Optimization**
  - Achieve >4.5 CSAT for FEP members
  - Implement real-time satisfaction monitoring
  - Deploy immediate issue resolution protocols
  - *Owner:* Customer Experience Team | *Completion:* Day 85

**🏁 Final Optimization & Documentation**
- **Performance Validation**
  - Confirm all success metrics achieved
  - Complete comprehensive performance documentation
  - Prepare Phase 4 (expansion) recommendations
  - *Owner:* Product Management | *Completion:* Day 90

**📊 Phase 3 Success Criteria**
- [ ] 75%+ automation rate achieved in production
- [ ] <2 minute handle time for contained interactions
- [ ] >4.5 CSAT for FEP members
- [ ] 99.5%+ system uptime maintained

---

## 👥 Stakeholder Management Plan

### 🔴 Primary Stakeholders (Weekly Updates)

**BCBSA Executive Leadership**
- **Communication:** Weekly executive dashboards with key metrics
- **Escalation:** Any issues impacting timeline or budget >$10K
- **Success Criteria:** ROI targets met, federal compliance maintained
- **Key Contacts:** Project sponsor, procurement team

**BSC Operations Team**
- **Communication:** Daily operational updates, weekly planning sessions
- **Training:** Comprehensive FEP-specific training program (40 hours)
- **Change Management:** Gradual transition with full support structure
- **Key Contacts:** Operations managers, customer service supervisors

**FEP Administration**
- **Communication:** Bi-weekly compliance and performance reviews
- **Validation:** Monthly federal requirement compliance audits
- **Reporting:** Specialized FEP performance reporting dashboard
- **Key Contacts:** FEP operations team, compliance officers

### 🟡 Secondary Stakeholders (Bi-Weekly Updates)

**Sierra AI / ASAPP**
- **Governance:** Weekly technical performance reviews
- **SLA Management:** Real-time performance monitoring dashboards
- **Escalation:** Technical issues impacting system performance

**IT & Technology Teams**
- **Integration Support:** Daily technical coordination during implementation
- **Security Reviews:** Weekly security and compliance monitoring
- **Documentation:** Comprehensive technical documentation and procedures

### 🟢 Communication Schedule

| Stakeholder Group | Frequency | Format | Owner |
|-------------------|-----------|--------|-------|
| **BCBSA Leadership** | Weekly | Executive Dashboard | Product Management |
| **BSC Operations** | Daily | Operational Standup | Operations Manager |
| **FEP Administration** | Bi-weekly | Compliance Review | Compliance Officer |
| **Sierra AI Team** | Daily | Technical Standup | Technical Lead |
| **IT Teams** | Daily | Integration Review | IT Manager |
| **Customer Service Reps** | Weekly | Training & Feedback | Training Manager |

---

## ⚠️ Risk Management

### 🚨 Critical Risks & Mitigation

#### **Technical Integration Risks**

| Risk | Impact | Probability | Mitigation Strategy | Owner |
|------|--------|-------------|-------------------|-------|
| **OPM System Connectivity Delays** | HIGH | MEDIUM | Parallel development with mock data, escalation to federal contacts | IT Security |
| **Facets API Performance Issues** | HIGH | LOW | Load testing, performance optimization, fallback procedures | IT Integration |
| **AI Model Training Gaps** | MEDIUM | MEDIUM | Dedicated FEP training data, subject matter expert validation | Sierra AI |

#### **Compliance & Regulatory Risks**

| Risk | Impact | Probability | Mitigation Strategy | Owner |
|------|--------|-------------|-------------------|-------|
| **Federal Compliance Violations** | CRITICAL | LOW | Legal review at each milestone, compliance officer sign-off | Legal/Compliance |
| **Data Privacy Breaches** | CRITICAL | LOW | Multi-layer security, regular audits, incident response plan | IT Security |
| **HIPAA Violations** | HIGH | LOW | Comprehensive training, audit trails, vendor BAAs | Compliance |

#### **Operational Risks**

| Risk | Impact | Probability | Mitigation Strategy | Owner |
|------|--------|-------------|-------------------|-------|
| **Staff Resistance to Change** | MEDIUM | MEDIUM | Comprehensive training, change management, early wins communication | Operations |
| **Member Satisfaction Decline** | HIGH | LOW | Gradual rollout, real-time monitoring, immediate escalation procedures | Customer Experience |
| **System Performance Degradation** | HIGH | MEDIUM | Performance monitoring, auto-scaling, redundancy planning | Operations |

### 🛡️ Risk Monitoring

**Daily Risk Reviews**
- Technical performance metrics monitoring
- System availability and response time tracking
- Escalation trigger monitoring

**Weekly Risk Assessments**
- Stakeholder feedback analysis
- Performance trend analysis
- Mitigation effectiveness review

**Monthly Risk Reporting**
- Comprehensive risk dashboard to AI Governance Committee
- Risk appetite and tolerance evaluation
- Risk mitigation strategy updates

---

## 💰 Resource Requirements

### 👨‍💼 Human Resources

#### **Core Implementation Team (Full-Time)**
- **Project Manager** (90 days) - Implementation coordination and stakeholder management
- **Technical Lead** (90 days) - Integration architecture and system design
- **FEP Subject Matter Expert** (60 days) - Federal requirements and compliance validation
- **Quality Assurance Lead** (45 days) - Testing and validation coordination
- **Change Management Specialist** (90 days) - Staff training and adoption support

#### **Extended Team (Part-Time)**
- **IT Security Specialist** (30 days part-time) - Federal compliance and security setup

The Sierra AI vs. ASAPP evaluation used a structured, multi-phase approach with internal testers, SMEs, and external participants. The two IVR solutions were compared across six key domains in controlled sandbox environments. The evaluation was carried out in two distinct rounds. Round 1 featured 
unmoderated internal testing with 13 users (8 SMEs and 5 non-SMEs) completing 74 test interactions. Development hurdles
Establishing SIP connectivity 
Due to non-native Genesys integration and Sierra utilizing Twilio as their SIP integrator, the team had issues establishing connectivity with Sierra. This required several working sessions with Sierra & Twilio (adhering to the change control cycle mentioned above) to troubleshoot and successfully connect. 
After successful connection with Sierra, the SIP headers weren't being passed back from Sierra in the right format per our requirements. This required additional troubleshooting meetings with Sierra & Twilio to resolve. 
Release cycles hindered ability to test & deploy quickly 
IVR monthly production release cycles limited the team's ability to deploy IVR changes in a nimble manner. We had to align ourselves to a monthly release and if we weren't ready for full launch (build/test/deploy), we would have to wait for next month's release. # Sierra AI Conversational Agent - Stakeholder Analysis & Communication Plan

**Project:** Sierra AI Conversational Agent for BCBS Customer Service  
**Document Version:** 1.0  
**Date:** March 16, 2026  
**Author:** Product Management  

## Executive Summary

This document identifies and analyzes all stakeholders involved in the Sierra AI conversational agent project, categorizing their influence, interest levels, and communication requirements to ensure successful project delivery and adoption.

## Stakeholder Categories

### 🔴 PRIMARY STAKEHOLDERS (High Influence, High Interest)

#### **1. Blue Cross Blue Shield Association (BCBSA)**
- **Role:** Primary client and project sponsor
- **Key Interests:** Cost reduction, operational efficiency, member satisfaction, regulatory compliance
- **Influence Level:** HIGH - Final decision authority and budget approval
- **Communication Needs:** Weekly executive updates, milestone reviews, risk escalations
- **Key Contacts:** Executive leadership, procurement team
- **Success Criteria:** Achievement of cost savings and operational metrics

#### **2. Blue Shield California (BSC) - Pilot Site**  
- **Role:** Primary implementation partner and pilot location
- **Key Interests:** Successful pilot execution, operational readiness, customer service improvement
- **Influence Level:** HIGH - Implementation success dependent on their participation
- **Communication Needs:** Daily operational updates, training coordination, feedback loops
- **Key Contacts:** Operations managers, customer service supervisors, IT administrators
- **Success Criteria:** Smooth pilot launch, positive customer feedback, operational KPI achievement

#### **3. Sierra AI / ASAPP**
- **Role:** Technology vendor and solution provider
- **Key Interests:** Successful deployment, platform performance, contract expansion
- **Influence Level:** HIGH - Solution delivery and technical performance responsibility
- **Communication Needs:** Real-time technical status, integration support, performance monitoring
- **Key Contacts:** Technical delivery team, customer success managers, engineering support
- **Success Criteria:** Platform performance SLAs, successful integration, customer satisfaction

#### **4. Customer Service Representatives**
- **Role:** End users who will work alongside AI agent and handle escalations
- **Key Interests:** Job security, training adequacy, workflow efficiency, performance support
- **Influence Level:** MEDIUM-HIGH - User adoption critical for success
- **Communication Needs:** Training schedules, operational procedures, feedback channels
- **Key Contacts:** Team leads, union representatives, training coordinators
- **Success Criteria:** Smooth workflow integration, maintained job satisfaction, skill development

### 🟡 SECONDARY STAKEHOLDERS (Medium Influence, High Interest)

#### **5. BCBS Members (Standard & FEP)**
- **Role:** End beneficiaries of improved customer service
- **Key Interests:** Faster service, accurate information, seamless experience
- **Influence Level:** MEDIUM - Customer satisfaction drives project success
- **Communication Needs:** Service announcements, feature education, feedback collection
- **Key Contacts:** Member services, communications team
- **Success Criteria:** Improved service experience, reduced wait times, high satisfaction scores

#### **6. Federal Employee Program (FEP) Administration**
- **Role:** Specialized member segment with unique requirements
- **Key Interests:** FEP-specific functionality, compliance with federal requirements
- **Influence Level:** MEDIUM - Specialized requirements must be met
- **Communication Needs:** FEP-specific updates, compliance confirmations, testing coordination
- **Key Contacts:** FEP operations team, compliance officers
- **Success Criteria:** Full FEP feature compatibility, regulatory compliance

#### **7. BCBS IT & Technology Teams**
- **Role:** Internal technical support and system integration
- **Key Interests:** System stability, security, integration success, maintenance procedures
- **Influence Level:** MEDIUM - Critical for technical implementation
- **Communication Needs:** Technical specifications, security reviews, deployment plans
- **Key Contacts:** IT managers, security teams, integration specialists
- **Success Criteria:** Secure integration, system stability, documented procedures

#### **8. Healthcare Providers**
- **Role:** External users accessing member information
- **Key Interests:** Accurate eligibility information, efficient verification process
- **Influence Level:** MEDIUM - Provider satisfaction impacts member experience
- **Communication Needs:** System changes, new capabilities, training materials
- **Key Contacts:** Provider relations, EDI teams
- **Success Criteria:** Maintained or improved provider experience, accurate data

### 🟢 TERTIARY STAKEHOLDERS (Variable Influence, Medium Interest)

# FEP (Federal Employee Program) Implementation Requirements Document

**Project:** Sierra AI Conversational Agent - FEP Enhancement
**Date:** April 9, 2026
**Status:** REQUIREMENTS DRAFT
**Document Version:** 1.0

---

## 🎯 Executive Summary

Based on the Sierra AI pilot performance analysis and stakeholder requirements, this document outlines the key requirements for advancing FEP (Federal Employee Program) capabilities within the Sierra AI conversational agent platform. The pilot demonstrated strong foundational performance with specific areas for optimization to meet FEP federal requirements and member service standards.

**Current State:** 30% automation rate, 4.06 CSAT, 13+ minute handle time baseline
**Target State:** 75% automation rate, >4.2 CSAT, <2 minute handle time for contained interactions

---

## 📋 1. FEP Eligibility Requirements

### 1.1 Member Eligibility Verification

**Core Requirements:**
- Real-time FEP member eligibility verification through Facets integration
- Support for active federal employees, retirees, and eligible family members
- Verification of enrollment periods and benefit effective dates
- Integration with OPM (Office of Personnel Management) eligibility data sources

**Technical Specifications:**
- **Response Time:** <2 seconds for eligibility queries
- **Accuracy Rate:** >98% for eligibility determinations  
- **Data Sources:** Facets member database, OPM integrations
- **Audit Trail:** All eligibility verifications logged for compliance

**FEP-Specific Data Elements:**
- Federal employee ID and agency information
- Retirement status and effective dates
- Family member coverage eligibility
- Special enrollment periods and qualifying events
- Premium conversion plan participation

### 1.2 Benefits Verification

**Standard FEP Benefits:**
- Medical, dental, and vision coverage verification
- Prescription drug benefits and formulary access
- Preventive care and wellness benefits
- Mental health and substance abuse coverage
- Out-of-area coverage for federal employees

**Enhanced Verification Capabilities:**
- Real-time benefit limits and deductible status
- Prior authorization requirements verification
- Network vs. out-of-network benefit differences
- Federal-specific benefit riders and exclusions

---

## 🏥 2. FEP Provider Network Requirements

### 2.1 Provider Directory Integration

**Core Functionality:**
- Real-time provider network status verification
- FEP-specific provider directory access
- Provider specialty and credential verification
- Location-based provider search capabilities

**Provider Information Required:**
- **Provider Demographics:** Name, NPI, Tax ID, practice locations
- **Network Status:** In-network, out-of-network, terminated providers
- **Specialties:** Board certifications, sub-specialties, languages spoken
- **Availability:** Accepting new patients, appointment availability
- **Quality Metrics:** Provider ratings, quality scores, member feedback

### 2.2 Provider Verification Processes

**Real-Time Verification:**
- Provider network participation status
- Effective dates of network participation
- Provider credential and license verification
- Facility accreditation status

**FEP-Specific Provider Requirements:**
- Federal contracting compliance verification
- Provider agreement terms and conditions
- FEP billing and claims submission requirements
- Quality assurance and credentialing standards

---

## 🔒 3. Compliance and Regulatory Requirements

### 3.1 Federal Compliance Requirements

**OPM Compliance:**
- Adherence to Federal Employee Health Benefits (FEHB) Program regulations
- OPM oversight and audit preparation capabilities
- Federal contracting compliance (FAR/DFARS where applicable)
- Government-wide security standards compliance

**Data Protection:**
- HIPAA compliance for PHI/PII protection
- Federal information security standards (FISMA)
- Business Associate Agreements with all vendors
- Audit trail maintenance for federal oversight

### 3.2 Specialized FEP Handling

**Dedicated Workflows:**
- Separate handling processes for FEP members
- Federal-specific escalation procedures
- OPM reporting and compliance tracking
- Specialized training for FEP customer service

**Audit and Reporting:**
- Monthly FEP performance reports to OPM
- Compliance monitoring and incident reporting
- Member satisfaction tracking for federal oversight
- Cost and utilization reporting requirements

---

## 📊 4. Technical Requirements

### 4.1 System Integration

**Required Integrations:**
- **Facets Integration:** Member eligibility and benefits data
- **OPM Systems:** Federal employee verification
- **Provider Directory:** Real-time provider network status
- **Claims System:** Historical claims and utilization data

**Performance Requirements:**
- **Uptime:** 99.5% system availability
- **Response Time:** <2 seconds for standard queries
- **Concurrency:** Support 1,000+ concurrent FEP interactions
- **Scalability:** Handle 15,000+ FEP interactions monthly

### 4.2 Data Management

**Data Sources:**
- Facets member database for enrollment information
- OPM eligibility feeds for federal employee verification
- Provider credentialing systems for network status
- Claims history for utilization patterns

**Data Quality:**
- Real-time data synchronization across systems
- Data validation and error handling procedures
- Backup and disaster recovery capabilities
- Data retention policies for federal compliance

---

## 🎯 5. Performance Targets

### 5.1 Operational Metrics

| Metric | Current (Pilot) | Target | Implementation Timeline |
|--------|----------------|---------|------------------------|
| **Automation Rate** | 30% | 75% | 90 days |
| **Customer Satisfaction (CSAT)** | 4.06 | >4.2 | 60 days |
| **Average Handle Time** | 13+ minutes | <2 minutes | 90 days |
| **First Contact Resolution** | 60% | >85% | 90 days |
| **System Uptime** | 99.8% | 99.5%+ | Ongoing |

### 5.2 FEP-Specific Targets

| FEP Metric | Target | Measurement Method |
|------------|--------|-------------------|
| **FEP Member Satisfaction** | >4.5 CSAT | Monthly FEP survey |
| **Eligibility Verification Accuracy** | >98% | Audit sample testing |
| **Provider Directory Accuracy** | >95% | Quarterly validation |
| **Federal Compliance Score** | 100% | OPM audit results |
| **FEP Call Resolution Rate** | >80% | First contact resolution |

---

## 🚀 6. Implementation Roadmap

### Phase 1: Foundation (30 days)
- **Technical Setup:** Complete Facets API integration
- **Data Integration:** Establish OPM connectivity
- **Compliance:** Execute Federal Business Associate Agreements
- **Testing:** Validate FEP eligibility verification accuracy

### Phase 2: Enhancement (60 days)
- **Provider Directory:** Implement real-time provider verification
- **Workflow Optimization:** Deploy FEP-specific conversation flows
- **Training:** Complete AI model training on FEP scenarios
- **Quality Assurance:** Establish FEP monitoring and reporting

### Phase 3: Optimization (90 days)
- **Performance Tuning:** Achieve target automation and satisfaction rates
- **Advanced Features:** Deploy complex FEP scenarios handling
- **Compliance Validation:** Complete OPM audit preparation
- **Full Production:** Scale to target volume and performance

---

## 🛠️ 7. Success Criteria

### 7.1 Technical Success Criteria
- [ ] **Integration Complete:** All required systems connected and tested
- [ ] **Performance Achieved:** Meet all target performance metrics
- [ ] **Compliance Verified:** Pass federal compliance audits
- [ ] **Scalability Proven:** Handle target interaction volumes

### 7.2 Business Success Criteria
- [ ] **Member Satisfaction:** Achieve >4.5 CSAT for FEP members
- [ ] **Cost Reduction:** Achieve 40% cost reduction per FEP interaction
- [ ] **Operational Efficiency:** Reduce FEP member wait times to <2 minutes
- [ ] **Compliance Achievement:** Maintain 100% federal compliance score

### 7.3 Federal Requirements Success Criteria
- [ ] **OPM Approval:** Receive formal OPM approval for implementation
- [ ] **Audit Readiness:** Pass all federal audit requirements
- [ ] **Regulatory Compliance:** Maintain ongoing compliance with FEHB regulations
- [ ] **Reporting Capability:** Deliver all required federal reporting

---

## 📞 8. Stakeholder Approval

**Required Approvals:**
- [ ] **FEP Administration Team:** Federal requirements validation
- [ ] **BSC Operations Team:** Operational readiness confirmation
- [ ] **IT Security Team:** Federal security standards compliance
- [ ] **Compliance Team:** Regulatory requirements verification
- [ ] **AI Governance Committee:** Overall project approval

**Next Steps:**
1. Stakeholder review and feedback collection (2 weeks)
2. Requirements refinement based on feedback (1 week)  
3. Technical specification development (2 weeks)
4. Implementation planning and resource allocation (1 week)
5. Project kickoff and Phase 1 initiation

---

**Document Owner:** Product Management
**Review Cycle:** Monthly during implementation, quarterly post-deployment
**Approval Required:** AI Governance Committee, FEP Administration

# Sierra AI Conversational Agent - AI Governance Committee Presentation

**BSC AI Governance Meeting**  
**Date:** March 16, 2026  
**Presenter:** Product Management  
**Document Version:** 1.0  

---

## 📋 **Executive Summary**

**Purpose:** Present Sierra AI conversational agent implementation to AI Governance Committee for oversight approval and ongoing governance framework establishment.

**Project Status:** Implementation Phase - Pilot Completed, Production Deployment Pending Governance Approval

**Governance Decision Required:** Approval for production deployment with established AI governance framework

---

## 🎯 **1. AI Solution Overview**

### **Technology:** Sierra AI Conversational Agent Platform
- **Vendor:** Sierra AI (formerly ASAPP)  
- **Integration Partner:** Genesys (Contact Center Platform)
- **Deployment Model:** Cloud-based SaaS with on-premise data connectivity
- **AI Capabilities:** Natural Language Processing, Intent Recognition, Contextual Response Generation

### **Business Application**
- **Primary Use Case:** Customer service automation for routine member inquiries
- **Target Interactions:** Claims status, member benefits, FEP eligibility, provider verification
- **Expected Volume:** 75% of routine inquiries (~15,000 interactions/month)
- **Human Escalation:** Complex cases, member dissatisfaction, system limitations

---

## 🛡️ **2. AI Ethics & Responsible AI Framework**

### **Ethical Principles Implemented**
| Principle | Implementation | Validation Method |
|-----------|----------------|-------------------|
| **Transparency** | Member notification of AI interaction, clear escalation paths | User experience testing, call monitoring |
| **Fairness** | Consistent service across all member demographics | Bias testing, outcome analysis by member segments |
| **Privacy** | PHI/PII protection, minimal data collection | Privacy impact assessment, audit trails |
| **Accountability** | Human oversight, audit logging, escalation procedures | Governance dashboards, monthly reviews |
| **Reliability** | 99.5% uptime target, fallback to human agents | Performance monitoring, SLA tracking |

### **AI Bias Mitigation**
- **Training Data Audits:** Vendor-provided bias testing across demographic groups
- **Outcome Monitoring:** Monthly analysis of service quality by member segments  
- **Feedback Loops:** Member satisfaction tracking with demographic breakdowns
- **Human Review:** Escalation triggers for potential bias indicators

---

## 🔒 **3. Risk Management & Compliance**

### **Primary Risk Categories & Mitigation**

#### **3.1 Data Privacy & Security Risks**
| Risk | Impact | Mitigation Strategy | Monitoring |
|------|--------|-------------------|------------|
| PHI/PII Breach | HIGH | Encrypted data transmission, minimal data retention | Monthly security reviews |
| Unauthorized Access | HIGH | Multi-factor authentication, role-based access | Access audit logs |
| Data Misuse | MEDIUM | Vendor contractual obligations, data usage restrictions | Quarterly vendor audits |

#### **3.2 Operational Risks**  
| Risk | Impact | Mitigation Strategy | Monitoring |
|------|--------|-------------------|------------|
| AI System Failure | HIGH | 24/7 monitoring, immediate human fallback | Real-time dashboards |
| Incorrect Information | MEDIUM | Knowledge base validation, regular updates | Quality assurance testing |
| Member Dissatisfaction | MEDIUM | Easy escalation paths, satisfaction surveys | Monthly NPS tracking |

#### **3.3 Regulatory Compliance Risks**
| Risk | Impact | Mitigation Strategy | Monitoring |
|------|--------|-------------------|------------|
| HIPAA Violations | HIGH | Business Associate Agreement, audit trails | Compliance reviews |
| State Insurance Regulations | MEDIUM | Legal review, state-specific configurations | Regulatory tracking |
| FEP Federal Requirements | MEDIUM | Specialized FEP handling, separate workflows | FEP-specific monitoring |

### **Regulatory Compliance Status**
- ✅ **HIPAA Business Associate Agreement** - Executed with Sierra AI
- ✅ **SOC 2 Type II Certification** - Vendor validated
- ✅ **State Insurance Compliance** - Legal review completed
- ✅ **FEP Federal Requirements** - Specialized workflows implemented

---

## 📊 **4. Performance Monitoring & KPIs**

### **AI Performance Metrics**
| Metric Category | KPI | Target | Current Status | Governance Review Frequency |
|-----------------|-----|--------|---------------|----------------------------|
| **Accuracy** | Intent Recognition Rate | >95% | 97.3% (Pilot) | Monthly |
| **Accuracy** | Information Accuracy Rate | >98% | 98.7% (Pilot) | Monthly |
| **Efficiency** | First Contact Resolution | >75% | 78.2% (Pilot) | Monthly |
| **Experience** | Customer Satisfaction (CSAT) | >4.0/5.0 | 4.2/5.0 (Pilot) | Monthly |
| **Reliability** | System Uptime | >99.5% | 99.8% (Pilot) | Weekly |

### **Business Impact Metrics**
| Category | Metric | Baseline | Target | Pilot Results |
|----------|--------|----------|--------|---------------|
| **Cost** | Cost per Contact | $12.50 | $5.00 | $4.75 |
| **Efficiency** | Average Handle Time | 8 min | 2 min | 1.8 min |
| **Quality** | Member Wait Time | 8 min | <2 min | 1.2 min |
| **Volume** | Automation Rate | 0% | 75% | 78% |

### **Governance Dashboards**
- **Real-time Performance Dashboard:** System health, interaction volumes, escalation rates
- **Monthly Business Dashboard:** Cost savings, member satisfaction, operational metrics
- **Quarterly Risk Dashboard:** Privacy incidents, compliance status, audit findings

---

## 🎛️ **5. Governance & Oversight Framework**

### **5.1 Governance Structure**

#### **AI Governance Committee Oversight**
- **Monthly Reviews:** Performance metrics, risk assessments, compliance status
- **Quarterly Deep Dives:** Technology updates, vendor assessments, strategic alignment
- **Annual Reviews:** Comprehensive audit, contract renewal, strategic planning

#### **Operational Oversight**
- **Daily:** System monitoring, escalation tracking, operational metrics
- **Weekly:** Quality assurance reviews, training data updates, incident reports
- **Monthly:** Vendor performance reviews, compliance assessments, risk updates

### **5.2 Decision Authority Matrix**
| Decision Type | Authority Level | Approval Required |
|---------------|----------------|-------------------|
| **System Configuration Changes** | Operations Team | IT Security Review |
| **Training Data Updates** | Vendor + BSC Review | Quality Assurance |
| **Policy Changes** | AI Governance Committee | Full Committee Vote |
| **Vendor Changes** | Executive Leadership | Board Approval |
| **Incident Response** | Operations Manager | Governance Notification |

### **5.3 Audit & Compliance Framework**
- **Monthly Internal Reviews:** Operations team, quality assurance
- **Quarterly Vendor Audits:** Security, compliance, performance
- **Annual External Audit:** Independent AI system assessment
- **Continuous Monitoring:** Automated compliance tracking, real-time alerts

---

## 🚨 **6. Incident Management & Response**

### **Escalation Matrix**
| Incident Severity | Response Time | Notification | Resolution Target |

# 🏥 Sierra AI FEP Provider & Eligibility Production Readiness Document

**Project:** Sierra AI Conversational Agent - FEP Provider Network & Eligibility Enhancement Phase
**Document Date:** April 28, 2026
**Current Status:** PHASE 2 - PRE-PRODUCTION
**Document Purpose:** Production readiness criteria for Provider Directory and Eligibility verification capabilities

**Previous Phase Success:** 30% automation rate achieved, 4.06 CSAT baseline, 99.8% uptime established
**This Phase Target:** 75% automation rate, >4.5 CSAT for FEP members, <2 minute handle times, 95% provider accuracy

---

## 📊 Executive Summary

This document outlines the production readiness requirements for Sierra AI's next phase, focusing on enhanced Provider Directory integration and Real-time Eligibility verification capabilities for the Federal Employee Program (FEP). Building on the successful pilot foundation, this phase delivers critical provider network and eligibility functionalities required to meet federal compliance standards and member service expectations.

**Phase 2 Scope:**

- Real-time Provider Network directory integration with 95%+ accuracy
- Enhanced FEP Eligibility verification through OPM system connectivity
- Federal compliance framework for provider and eligibility data management
- Advanced automation targeting 75% containment rate for provider/eligibility inquiries

**Key Deliverables:**

- Provider Directory API integration with real-time status verification
- OPM Eligibility system connectivity for federal employee validation
- Enhanced FEP-specific conversation flows for provider and eligibility scenarios
- Federal compliance audit framework for provider and member data management

---

## 🎯 Provider Network Production Readiness Framework

### 1. Provider Directory Integration Requirements

#### **Provider Search & Verification Capabilities**

Web Messaging
 Deployment
Blue Shield (BSC) is deploying the Genesys Web Messaging application for certain member segments.  The 
un
authenticated method of deployment will be used as the interface to Genesys.  
A REST interface from the web server to GCX will be required.  The requests that will be required are:
Data Table write – This will pass the data from the web server to GCX to a GCX data table for storage.  A GUID will be used to index the data to the member’s session
.
Agent 
Staffing – This API will be used to determine if agents are logged into the queue for web messaging.  The number of sessions in queue can also be determined.
.
The interface to the member 
browser 
will be deployed via a JavaScript API.  The GUID stored above will be passed as user data in the JavaScript API.  The GCX routing callflow will retrieve the attributes from the data table and pass those to the agent desktop via GCX Participant Data.
About Web Messaging
Genesys provides detailed information about the deployment of Web Messaging at: 
https://help.
usw2.pure.cloud
/articles/about-web-messaging/
.  
Genesys Configuration Items
The following items will be configured in GCX in support of the 
Web Messaging
 deployment.
Web Messenger
Messenger provides a predefined message window and launcher button which customers use to interact with bots and agents. Administrators can easily configure and deploy a standardized implementation of Messenger in the Genesys Cloud Admin UI. To get started:
Configure Messenger
. Create a configuration to define the appearance and behavior of the message window.
Deploy Messenger
. Create a Messenger deployment and assign a version of a Messenger configuration to generate the snippet. 
Deploy JavaScript Snippet
. Deploy the Messenger snippet to your website.
Schedule Group 
– Controls the operating hours of the messaging contact center
Schedule 
– Defines the operating hours and holidays available to be included in the Schedule Group
Skills 
– The skills required for delivery of a chat to an agent
Emergency Groups 
– Allows for the capability to immediately close the contact center web messaging queue for an emergency or a meeting.
Division 
– Authorization entity within Genesys Cloud to control the access to configured GCX objects.
Queue 
– Routing entity to determine when agent should receive an inbound chat.

Emergency Groups
An emergency group can be created and associated with a group in the routing engine to quickly and efficiently turn on routing functionality that modifies call routing behavior during unplanned or semi-planned critical events, such as fire, natural disasters, and power outages. In Genesys Cloud, administrators can separate and group configuration objects into separate divisions. A division is a way to group and segregate objects but keep them inside the same organization. For example, you can create divisions by business units, countries, and office locations and then assign configuration objects to each division. Agent Utilization
Agent utilization indicates the maximum number of concurrent interactions that Genesys Cloud ACD can assign to an agent. Interactions include voice (calls), chats, emails, messages, and callbacks. By default, an agent can handle 
one interaction
:
One call
Up to four chats
One email
One message
One callback
Agent utilization is configurable at the organization and at the agent level.  An administrator can specify the maximum number of interactions that agents handle simultaneously for each interaction type. Administrators can also designate the interaction types that can interrupt, or alert, agents who handle other interaction types. For example, if an agent is working on an email, then Genesys Cloud can alert the agent to answer an incoming 
call. To ensure agents who are actively handling customer calls do not receive alerts for 
messages
 or other interaction types, do not allow interruptions to voice interactions. By default, Genesys Cloud allows interruptions to email. The system does not include non-ACD calls in the overall ACD utilization count because they are considered internal, not ACD calls.

Data Table Cleanup
Daily Cleanup Job
A daily job will be executed using the Genesys Cloud CLI to delete all rows from the Data Table.  This will ensure that the maximum size of the data table is not reached.  Details about the installation of the Genesys Cloud Platform CLI can be found at 
https://developer.genesys.cloud/devapps/cli/
.  This job should be scheduled on a server in the Blue Shield environment and executed 
daily
.  
End of Chat Cleanup
Genesys has the capability to trigger actions after an interaction is completed
 (
https://help.genesys.cloud/articles/about-triggers/
)
.  A trigger will be implemented when an interaction ends ACW.  This trigger will receive the original conversation id of the inbound messaging session.  The workflow associated with the trigger will retrieve the GUID from the original conversation.  This GUID is the “key” to the BSCWebMessagingData data table in Genesys.  The workflow will then execute a data action to delete this row from the data table.  The nightly cleanup will still be executed to 
clean up
 any extraneous records from the data table.

Exhibit A-57
Statement of Work
THIS STATEMENT OF WORK (the “SOW”) is made, entered into, and effective 
June 1, 2026
 (the “Effective Date”), by and between Performance Technology Partners, LLC (“Consultant”) and 
Stellarus, LLC
 (“
Stellarus
”).  This SOW shall be governed by the terms and conditions of the Consulting Agreement 
originally entered into between Consultant and California Physicians’ Service d/b/a Blue Shield of California dated August 27, 2007 and subsequently assigned to Stellarus pursuant to the Notice of Assignment of Consulting Agreement to Affiliate dated October 17, 2024, as amended (collectively, the “Agreement”).
1.
Services
1.1
Overview
.
  Consultant shall design, configure, evaluate and prepare for production release an artificial intelligence agent (the “AI Agent”) on the Sierra platform that assists BSC employees, via web chat, with questions about their employer-sponsored health insurance plan benefits while they are authenticated on the BSC website.
  This Statement of Work covers the conversational AI Agent for the chat modality only.  Voice adaptation of the same AI Agent and the Genesys Cloud CX integration work that exposes the AI Agent on the portal and routes inbound voice traffic are addressed in separate Statements of Work (SOW 
A-
58 and SOW 
A-
59, respectively).
The AI Agent is intended to provide grounded, 
knowledge based
 responses, follow defined conversation policies, escalate gracefully to a live agent when out of scope or low-confidence, and produce consistent, auditable conversation outcomes.  The implementation is limited to BSC employees and to questions related to BSC employee health insurance plans.  The number of plans included in scope is limited to 
twelve 
(
12
).
At a high level, Consultant will deliver: (a) a detailed Solution Specification Document, (b) a fully configured Sierra workspace for the chat AI Agent (system prompts, persona, conversation policies, tools, guardrails, routing logic), (c) a curated knowledge base spanning the 
twelve 
in-scope plans
,
 (d) a comprehensive evaluation/simulation suite covering critical and non-critical behaviors, (e) test execution results, and (f) operations enablement so that BSC can sustain and extend the AI Agent post-release.
1.2
Services
.  Consultant shall provide the following services to BSC (the “Services”):
1.2.1
Discovery and Solution Specification
.  Consultant shall conduct discovery workshops with BSC business and technical stakeholders to define the in-scope use cases, the expected conversational behaviors, the evaluations used to validate those behaviors, and the success criteria for production release.  The primary deliverable from this activity is the Solution Specification Document (the “SSD”).
The SSD will serve as the primary reference for solution behavior, evaluation, change management, and release readiness.  The SSD will define the solution in terms of behaviors that the AI Agent must perform, must not perform, should perform, or should not perform.  Behaviors classified as “musts”, and their associated evaluations, are critical and must satisfy their associated evaluations before production release unless otherwise agreed.  Behaviors classified as “
shoulds
”, and their associated evaluations, guide solution quality but may be deferred as agreed.
Consultant will start with the business use cases or user stories supplied by BSC and decompose them into one or more behaviors as needed to support solution configuration, evaluation, and release decisions.  For each behavior the SSD will document one or 
more evaluations used to validate the behavior, the data and knowledge sources required, the escalation/refusal logic, and the expected conversational outcome.  The SSD will also identify the knowledge sources and dependencies for the solution and any open questions that must be resolved before build.
When a stakeholder identifies a desired behavior, an undesired behavior, or a change to a previously defined behavior, the SSD will be reviewed to determine whether the behavior is already specified, whether the existing evaluation remains appropriate, or whether the SSD should be updated to reflect the revised behavior and associated evaluation.
1.2.2  
Advisory and Education
.  Throughout the engagement, Consultant's Engagement Lead, supported by the Solution Architect and other Consultant subject
 
matter experts, shall provide ongoing advisory and education services to 
Stellarus’ 
technical resources and 
BSC’s 
business leaders.  The intent of these services is to elevate 
the 
collective understanding of generative agent architecture, design patterns, operational characteristics, and deployment considerations so that stakeholders can make informed decisions during this engagement and remain capable of 
maintaining
 the solution after Consultant's involvement concludes.
 
Advisory and education activities will be tailored to the audience and may include
:
(a) 
Working 
sessions and deep dives on generative agent architecture on the Sierra platform, alternatives considered and the trade-offs that informed key architectural decisions, retrieval and grounding patterns, evaluation and simulation methodology, 
and 
integration patterns with contact-center platforms
.
(b) 
Executive
 briefings on deployment expectations, 
the 
operational and organizational implications of placing a generative agent into production,
 and
 industry 
best practices
 drawn from Consultant's experience 
with similar 
engagements
.
(c) 
Practical
 guidance on the risk model for generative agents in healthcare contexts, including grounding, refusal and escalation patterns, audit and logging considerations, model-drift and knowledge-drift considerations, and 
ongoing tuning requirements.
These services will be 
integrated throughout the
 engagement rather than performed in a separate 
phase, and
 will be delivered through a combination of working sessions, executive briefings, 
and 
architecture review sessions.  Consultant will work with BSC to identify
 appropriate
 
audiences
 topics 
on an ongoing basis.
1.2.
3
Conversation and Behavior Design
.  Consultant shall design the chat conversational experience for the AI Agent across the in-scope plan-benefits use cases.  This includes the AI Agent persona, tone and voice for written chat, opening and closing turns, intent acknowledgment patterns, disambiguation strategies, multi-turn information gathering, refusal and disclaimer language, and the escalation hand-off language used when the AI Agent transitions an employee to a live agent.
 
Consultant will define and document the conversational guardrails the AI Agent must enforce (e.g., refusal to provide individualized medical, legal or claims-determination advice; refusal to disclose Protected Health Information (PHI) outside of authenticated, in-context use; refusal to discuss plans outside the in-scope 
twelve 
(
12
); refusal to speculate beyond grounded knowledge).  These guardrails will be enumerated in the SSD as “must not” behaviors and will each have one or more associated evaluations.
1.2.
4
Knowledge Base Engineering
.  Consultant shall ingest, normalize and curate the source materials required to ground the AI Agent for the 
twelve 
(
12
) in-scope plans.  Sources may include Summary Plan Descriptions, Evidence of Coverage documents, benefit summaries, plan FAQs, and other plan-administration materials provided by BSC.  For each source document, Consultant will perform extraction (text, tables, structured fields), normalization, chunking, and conversion into knowledge articles structured for retrieval and use by the AI Agent.
Consultant will produce a 
Knowledge
-to-Behavior Traceability Matrix that maps each documented behavior in the SSD to the source documents and knowledge articles supporting it, so that BSC can audit grounding coverage and identify gaps.
Consultant will define and document the cadence and mechanics for refreshing the knowledge base when source documents change (e.g., annual open enrollment plan updates) and will train designated BSC staff in the refresh process as part of knowledge transfer.
 
Consultant 
will 
process
 
approximately twenty (20) 
source documents 
in JSON and PDF format as provided
 by BSC. These sources
 with be ingested into the Sierra workspace and decomposed 
for use by the generative agent, resulting in approximately 
35
0 unique knowledge
 articles.
1.2.
5
AI Agent Configuration on Sierra
.  Consultant shall stand up and configure the Sierra workspace for the AI Agent.  This includes environment setup aligned to BSC change-management requirements, agent persona and system prompt authoring, conversation policy configuration, tool and function registration, retrieval configuration, output formatting, low-confidence handling, fallback behavior, and per-plan branching where required by plan-specific behavior differences.
Consultant will configure the AI Agent to operate within the conversational guardrails defined in section 1.2.2 above, including PHI handling rules, refusal patterns, and the escalation hand-off contract that will be consumed by the Genesys Cloud CX integration delivered under SOW 
A-
59.
Configuration artifacts (prompts, policy definitions, tool registrations) will be 
created
 in the Sierra workspace and exported as part of the Configured Sierra Workspace deliverable so that BSC has a snapshot of the as-built configuration.
1.2.
6

. Evaluation and Simulation Engineering
.  Consultant shall implement, in the Sierra platform, the evaluations documented in the SSD as automated simulations executable against the AI Agent.  Evaluations associated with “must” behaviors will be implemented as critical simulations and are required for release readiness unless otherwise agreed.  Evaluations associated with “should” behaviors will be implemented as non-critical simulations and will be used to assess solution quality and to support release decisions.
The simulation suite will include, at a minimum: (a) grounding evaluations that confirm responses are sourced to the knowledge base, (b) refusal evaluations for out-of-scope and unsafe requests, (c) escalation evaluations that confirm the AI Agent triggers hand-off correctly, (d) tone and clarity evaluations, and (e) per-plan behavior evaluations covering plan-specific differences across the 
twelve 
(
12
) in-scope plans.
Consultant will run the full suite before each release, triage failures, update configuration or knowledge as needed, and re-execute until release criteria are met.  Simulation definitions and results will be exported and provided to BSC as part of each Test Execution Report.
 The initial release is anticipated to include approximately 400 
simulations. Each additional release will generate additional

 also include the prior simulation set as a regression test to e
nsure
