Pre-Production Testing
.  In addition to the automated simulation suite, Consultant shall support a structured pre-production testing phase including a User Acceptance Testing (UAT) cycle with BSC business stakeholders.  Consultant will triage defects, propose remediations, implement remediations to the AI Agent configuration or knowledge base, and re-test.
Consultant will also support an optional limited pilot with a small population of BSC employees prior to broad release, if BSC elects to pilot.  Pilot scope, population, and entry/exit criteria will be defined jointly during specification.
BSC is responsible for performing and signing off on User Acceptance Testing.  Consultant will provide test scripts, defect-triage support and remediation during this phase.
 
Acceptance is based on 100% pass rate for critical scenarios, characterized as “must do” and “must not do” with 95% accuracy for other scenarios as measured by 
the Sierra instrumentation tools
, in alignment with the process for other implementations at BSC.
Target first-token latency ≤ 2 seconds for chat, ≤ 1.5 seconds for voice; end-of-turn target ≤ 6 seconds chat, ≤ 4 seconds voice. 
Targets assume nominal performance of the Sierra platform, 
GCX, 
the underlying LLM inference layer, and BSC-provided web services

Use Case Summary 
Use Case Definition 
 
The initial implementation will focus on a text-based chat experience designed to support 
members with plan-related questions and self-service needs.  
 
The primary use case for the solution is member benefits look-up across Employee Medical, 
Specialty, and Pharmacy plans. The implementation will support multiple plan types, including 
four PPO plans, four HMO plans, one Medicare plan, one PPO Dental plan, and two PPO Vision 
service plans. The goal is to provide members with fast, conversational access to plan benefit 
information within a guided digital experience. 
 
For unsupported or out-of-scope requests, the chat experience will not transfer directly to a live 
agent. Instead, the only supported escalation path will be the ability for members to request a 
callback for follow-up assistance. 
 
Future Channel/Feature expansion: Speak-to-Chat and Inbound Voice  
 
Future planned use cases include: Eligibility verification, Claims status and information, 
Accumulator balances, Billing information, Provider and facility look-ups, Symptom checker 
support, Medication cost inquiries by medication name.

Exhibit A-58
Statement of Work
THIS STATEMENT OF WORK (the “SOW”) is made, entered into, and effective 
June 1, 2026
 (the “Effective Date”), by and between Performance Technology Partners, LLC (“Consultant”) and 
Stellarus, LLC
 (“
Stellarus
”).  This SOW shall be governed by the terms and conditions of the Consulting Agreement 
originally entered into between Consultant and California Physicians’ Service d/b/a Blue Shield of California dated August 27, 2007 and subsequently assigned to Stellarus pursuant to the Notice of Assignment of Consulting Agreement to Affiliate dated October 17, 2024, as amended (collectively, the “Agreement”).
1.
Services
1.1
Overview
.  Consultant shall extend the AI Agent originally developed for chat under SOW A-57 to support inbound voice interactions through the same generative AI Agent on the Sierra platform.  This Statement of Work covers all modifications, adaptations and additions to the AI Agent that are required for it to operate effectively in the voice modality.  The integration work that routes inbound voice calls from the BSC IVR through Genesys Cloud CX (“GCX”) into the AI Agent, and the corresponding live-agent transfer behavior, is addressed under SOW A-59.
Voice adaptation is non-trivial.  The same AI Agent reasoning core can be reused, but the conversational design, response length and style, knowledge framing, disclaimer pattern, error/disfluency handling, and evaluations all change materially in a voice context.  In addition, the AI Agent must interoperate with speech recognition (ASR) and speech synthesis (TTS), must support barge-in and interruption, must tolerate misrecognitions, and must produce conversational turns appropriately scoped for spoken delivery.
At a high level, Consultant will deliver: (a) a Voice SSD Addendum to the chat SSD produced under SOW A-57, (b) updated Sierra workspace configuration encoding voice-specific behaviors and persona, (c) voice-adapted knowledge content where existing knowledge requires reframing for spoken delivery, (d) a pronunciation lexicon and 
custom dictionary
 for benefit-specific terminology, (e) a voice-specific evaluation/simulation suite, (f) test execution results, and (g) operations enablement for the voice modality.
1.2
Services
.  Consultant shall provide the following services to BSC (the “Services”):
1.2.1
Voice Solution Specification Addendum
.  Consultant shall produce a Voice Solution Specification Addendum (the “Voice SSD Addendum”) to the chat SSD produced under SOW A-57.  The Voice SSD Addendum will document the additional and modified behaviors required for the AI Agent in voice, the corresponding evaluations, the speech-input and speech-output behaviors, the barge-in and interruption policy, the silence and no-input timeout policy, the misrecognition recovery policy, and the voice escalation contract that will be consumed by the GCX integration delivered under SOW A-59.
Where a chat behavior translates without change to voice, the Voice SSD Addendum will reference the chat SSD; where it must change for voice, the Voice SSD Addendum will define the voice-specific version, classified as “must,” “must not,” “should,” or “should not,” and the associated evaluations.
The Voice SSD Addendum will define the audio quality, latency budget, and turn-taking expectations the AI Agent must meet.
1.2.2
Voice Persona, Prompt and Tone Adaptation
.  Consultant shall adapt the AI Agent persona for spoken delivery.  This includes voice persona definition, system-prompt adjustments to instruct the AI Agent to produce response turns that read well aloud (shorter sentences, no bulleted lists, no markdown, no URLs), spoken disclaimers, spoken citations (e.g., “according to your 2026 PPO plan summary”), and revised refusal and escalation language tuned for voice.
1.2.3
Speech I/O Tuning
.  Consultant shall tune the speech-input (ASR) and speech-output (TTS) characteristics of the voice AI Agent.  ASR tuning includes assembling a domain vocabulary and phrase list of benefit-specific terminology (plan names, network names, benefit categories, common acronyms)
 and 
authoring a pronunciation lexicon for proper nouns and acronyms that are routinely misrecognized or mispronounced.
1.2.4
Voice-Specific Behavior Configuration
.  Consultant shall configure the voice-specific behaviors documented in the Voice SSD Addendum.  This includes barge-in handling (when an employee speaks over the AI Agent), no-input and no-match recovery, misrecognition recovery (e.g., re-prompts and disambiguation), confirmation strategy for high-stakes information (e.g., before transferring), conversational repair, and graceful fall-through to a live-agent transfer when the AI Agent cannot continue.
Consultant shall configure the in-flight filler/holding pattern for the AI Agent so that the employee perceives responsiveness while back-end tool calls or retrievals are in progress.
1.2.5
Voice Knowledge Adaptation
.  Consultant shall review the existing chat knowledge base produced under SOW A-57 and adapt content where the chat presentation is not appropriate for voice.  
1.2.6
Audio Connector Agent-Side Configuration
.  Consultant shall perform the AI Agent–side configuration required to interoperate with the Sierra Genesys Audio Connector that connects voice traffic to the AI Agent.  This includes session initiation parameters, metadata mapping (e.g., authenticated employee identifier, plan identifier, IVR collected data), session lifecycle handling, and the escalation contract used to surface the AI Agent’s voice transfer signal to GCX.
The Sierra Genesys Audio Connector itself is a Sierra-supplied integration, and Sierra is responsible for that connector.  The GCX-side configuration that consumes the Audio Connector is in scope under SOW A-59.
1.2.7
Voice Evaluation and Simulation Engineering
.  Consultant shall implement voice-specific evaluations as simulations in the Sierra platform, including but not limited to: (a) audio-input simulations covering accented speech, background noise, and varying speaking rates within the limits supported by the platform, (b) misrecognition-recovery evaluations, (c) barge-in evaluations, (
d
) voice-specific refusal and escalation evaluations, and (
e
) regression coverage of every chat “must” behavior to confirm parity in voice.
Evaluations associated with voice “must” behaviors will be implemented as critical simulations and are required for release readiness unless otherwise agreed.  Evaluations associated with voice “should” behaviors will be implemented as non-critical simulations and will support release decisions.
1.2.8
Voice Pre-Production Testing
.  Consultant shall support a voice-specific User Acceptance Testing (UAT) cycle with BSC stakeholders.  Consultant will triage defects, propose 
remediations, implement remediations to the AI Agent configuration or knowledge base, and re-test.
BSC is responsible for performing and signing off on voice User Acceptance Testing.  Consultant will provide voice test scripts, evidence packages including representative call recordings (subject to applicable privacy and consent requirements), defect-triage support and remediation during this phase.
1.2.9
Knowledge Transfer and Enablement
.  Consultant shall produce a Voice Operations Guide Addendum (the “Voice Operations Guide Addendum”) to the Operations Guide produced under SOW A-57.  The Voice Operations Guide Addendum will describe how to administer voice-specific behaviors, the pronunciation lexicon, the SSML library, voice persona and prompt updates, voice simulation authoring and execution, and incident triage procedures specific to voice.  Consultant shall conduct live knowledge transfer sessions covering the Voice Operations Guide Addendum with the BSC operations team.
1.2.10 
Release Readiness
, 
Production Cutover Support
, and Hypercare
.  Consultant shall produce a Production Release Readiness Report documenting the state of all critical simulations, outstanding defects, residual risks, recommended go/no-go decision, and the cutover plan.  Consultant shall support the production cutover activities defined in the cutover plan, including configuration promotion, smoke testing, and hyper-care support.
1.2.10.1  Consultant will provide 
hypercare
 support for a period of 2 business weeks following the production release of the Deliverables under this SOW (the "Hypercare Period"). The Hypercare Period may be extended at BSC's request through a written change order at scope and fees to be agreed by the parties.
1.2.10.2  Hypercare support will be provided during BSC business hours, Monday through Friday excluding BSC-observed holidays, with on-call engineering response for Severity 1 (Critical) incidents outside of business hours. All other severity levels are worked during business hours.
1.2.10.3  BSC will report issues through a jointly agreed channel (designated email alias, shared messaging channel, or ticketing tool) confirmed during cutover planning. The Engagement Lead and Project Manager will serve as primary points of escalation for BSC. Solution performance will be monitored through a combination of established reporting dashboards within Sierra and GCX, survey results, manual review of session transcripts by Consultant and BSC, and qualitative feedback from contact center representatives.
1.2.10.4  Issues identified during the Hypercare Period will be classified jointly by BSC and Consultant using the following definitions:
Severity
Definition
1 - Critical
The agent is unavailable or non-responsive for all or a large subset of users; the retrieval or knowledge layer has failed; or the agent is generating harmful, false, or non-compliant outputs at scale.
2 - High
A core agent capability is significantly impaired including persistent retrieval failures, inability to complete a primary use case, or systematic hallucination on a defined topic.
3 - Medium
Agent behavior is degraded in a limited or non-core way, including inconsistent grounding or stale knowledge content, and a workaround exists or the issue occurs only under specific conditions.
4 - Low
Minor issue, knowledge base content correction, prompt or instruction adjustment, or non-urgent refinement of an existing agent behavior.
1.2.10.5  Consultant commits to the following acknowledgment, working, and communication commitments during the Hypercare Period:
Severity
Initial Response
Working Commitment
Status Updates
1 - Critical
Within 1 business hour
Continuous engineering effort until the issue is resolved or a stable workaround is in place
Every 2 hours
2 - High

Engineering effort during business hours, not paused while the issue is open
Daily
3 - Medium
Within 1 business day

hypercare
 backlog and worked during business hours based on impact
Daily
4 - Low
Within 3 business days

hypercare
 backlog as agreed
Weekly
1.2.10.6  The parties acknowledge that the time required to resolve an issue with the AI Agent and the associated integrations is driven by the root cause, complexity, and dependency on third-party platforms (including Sierra and Genesys Cloud CX), BSC IT infrastructure, and BSC-provided web services. Consultant commits to the acknowledgment, working commitment, and status update cadence above, and 
does not commit to a specific resolution deadline
. For each open issue, Consultant will maintain open communication and proactively escalate to the Engagement Lead and the BSC Operations Owner when the estimate changes materially or when root cause is identified to lie outside Consultant's scope of work.  
Where the root cause of an issue is determined to lie within a third-party platform (Sierra, Genesys Cloud CX), BSC IT infrastructure, or BSC-provided web services, Consultant's responsibility during 
hypercare
 is limited to triage, root-cause identification, coordination with the responsible party, 
and 
ongoing communication with BSC.
1.2.10.7  
Hypercare is limited to defect remediation against the Deliverables accepted under this SOW. The following are expressly out of scope of 
hypercare
 and, if requested, will be handled through written change orders:
New use cases, new intents, new conversation flows, or new behaviors not documented in the SSD
New plans or material revisions to in-scope plans during the Hypercare Period
New integrations, or material changes to in-scope integrations
Routine or scheduled knowledge-
base
 refresh (including annual open enrollment updates)
Knowledge updates resulting from changes to BSC source materials provided after acceptance
Performance tuning beyond the targets documented in the SSD
Enhancement requests of any classification
  
1.2.1
2
  
Project Management
.  Consultant shall provide project management for Services, including but not limited to the following:
1.2.1
2
.1
  
Serve as the primary contact for all questions and issues related to Consultant’s Services hereunder.
1.2.1
2
.2
  
Create and maintain a project plan (the “Project Plan”) and provide a weekly status report (the “Weekly Status Report”) of Consultant’s project progress, staff management, risks, and issues.
1.2.1
2

Maintain a risk and issue log and a decision log, updated weekly and reviewed in the weekly status meeting.
1.2.1
2

BSC will appoint a single point of contact responsible for all communications and project management among all Customer parties (staff, vendors, consultants) and for the escalation and resolution of any issues for BSC.
1.2.1

The participation and commitment of BSC’s project team during the project, including assigned tasks to BSC team members, will be a key to project success.
1.2.1

1.2.1

All Services, materials and communications are assumed to be delivered in English, unless otherwise specifically noted.
1.3
Consultant Personnel
.  Consultant shall ensure that its personnel assigned to perform services under this SOW have the necessary qualifications, competence and experience required to provide the Service and Deliverables.  If BSC, at its sole discretion, is not satisfied with the performance of any Consultant personnel, BSC shall notify Consultant and Consultant shall promptly furnish replacement personnel.  BSC 
retains the right at all times
 to end the assignment of any personnel Consultant provides under this SOW.
1.4
Term
.  Consultant shall begin providing the Services under this SOW on the Effective Date and Consultant will complete all Services and provide all Deliverables no later than 
September 30
th
, 2026. 
Unless otherwise terminated earlier pursuant to the terms of the Agreement, this SOW will terminate on completion of all Services, including final acceptance of all Deliverables.
1.5
Key BSC Roles
.
  The participation and commitment of BSC’s project team will be a key to project success.  BSC will provide qualified business and technical resources versed in BSC’s applications and systems during the project as needed.  The following key customer roles shall be filled by BSC:
1.5.1
Project Sponsor
.  The Project Sponsor shall be able to articulate the project vision, identify and provide needed resources and funding, and oversee the successful deployment and adoption of the voice modality.
1.5.2
Benefits Subject Matter Experts
.  BSC shall provide one or more Benefits SMEs who will validate voice-adapted knowledge content, listen to representative call recordings and AI Agent renderings, and sign off on plan-specific spoken behaviors.
1.5.3
Compliance and Privacy Reviewer
.  BSC shall provide a Compliance and Privacy Reviewer responsible for reviewing voice-specific disclaimer language, call recording, consent, and any privacy-relevant logging or transcript storage configuration prior to production release.
1.5.4
Telecommunications Administrator
.  The Telecommunications Administrator is responsible for administering the telecommunications environment at BSC and serving as the point of contact for any telecommunications or contact-center infrastructure questions affecting the 
voice
 AI Agent.
1.5.5
IVR Developer
.  The IVR Developer is responsible for the BSC IVR configuration; they will participate in design sessions related to IVR-collected metadata that is passed to the voice AI Agent, even though the IVR-to-GCX integration itself is delivered under SOW A-59.
1.5.6
Operations Owner
.  BSC shall designate the same Operations Owner identified under SOW A-57 to receive voice-specific knowledge transfer and to be the operational owner of the voice AI Agent post-release.
1.6
Assumptions and Dependencies
.  This SOW is predicated on the following assumptions and dependencies.  If any of 
these change
 materially, Consultant may request a change to scope, schedule, and/or fees pursuant to the Agreement:
1.6.1
Dependency on SOW A-57
.  This SOW depends on the AI Agent foundation delivered under SOW A-57.  Activities under this SOW will be sequenced against the chat SSD, knowledge base, simulation suite, and Sierra workspace produced under SOW A-57.
1.6.2
Dependency on SOW A-59
.  End-to-end voice testing requires the inbound voice routing and Audio Connector configuration delivered under SOW A-59.  Consultant will agree the cross-SOW integration test schedule with BSC.
1.6.3
Plan Scope
.  The voice AI Agent will cover the same eight (8) BSC employee health plans in scope under SOW A-57.
1.6.4
Language
.  The voice AI Agent will be developed, evaluated and operated in English only.
1.6.5
Speech Stack
.  Voice I/O will be provided through the Sierra Genesys Audio Connector and the underlying speech stack supported by Sierra.  Replacement or addition of alternate speech stacks is out of scope for this SOW.
1.6.6
Call Recording and Consent
.  Recording of calls, retention of recordings, and consent disclosures are BSC responsibilities outside the AI Agent itself; Consultant will configure 
the AI Agent to honor any required consent or disclosure language documented in the Voice SSD Addendum.
1.7
Out of Scope
.  Without limiting any other terms of this SOW, the following are expressly out of scope under this SOW:
1.7.1
IVR-to-GCX Routing
.  Modifications to the BSC IVR call flow and the routing of inbound voice calls from the BSC IVR into GCX are out of scope and are addressed under SOW A-59.
1.7.2
GCX Voice Routing, Callback and Warm Transfer
.  Configuration of GCX inbound voice routing, callback queues, warm transfer flows, live-agent queues, and reporting is out of scope and is addressed under SOW A-59.
1.7.3
New Chat Functionality
.  New chat behaviors, new chat knowledge, or chat-only enhancements are out of scope under this SOW (such work would be sequenced under SOW A-57 or a successor SOW).
1.7.4
Replacement of Speech Stack
.  Procurement or replacement of the underlying speech stack (ASR/TTS providers) is out of scope.
1.7.5
Voice Biometrics or Authentication
.  Voice biometric identification or voice-based authentication is out of scope.  The voice AI Agent will rely on authentication performed upstream by the BSC IVR / GCX path.
1.8
Staffing Plan

Consultant
 for the duration of the engagement and reviewed with BSC in the weekly status meetings.

.  Strategic advisor to BSC’s Project Sponsor and steering committee, ensuring the engagement aligns with enterprise AI strategy, contact-center transformation, and broader organizational initiatives.
1.8.2
Project Manager
.  Single point of accountability for delivery of the voice adaptation, including coordination with SOW A-57 (chat AI Agent) and SOW A-59 (integration) workstreams.
1.8.3

.  Owns the Voice SSD Addendum, voice persona and prompt strategy, latency budget, evaluation strategy and release-readiness criteria for the voice modality.
1.8.4

1.8.5
Speech / Linguistics Engineer
.  Owns the pronunciation lexicon and SSML library, ASR vocabulary and phrase lists, TTS voice selection and tuning, and the validation of spoken renderings of representative content.
1.8.6
AI Agent Engineer (Voice)
.  Configures voice-specific behaviors in the Sierra workspace and performs the Audio Connector agent-side configuration.
1.8.7
Evaluation Engineer (Voice)
.  Designs and implements voice-specific simulations including audio-input simulations, barge-in, recovery, latency and regression suites; runs evaluations against release candidates and produces Voice Test Execution Reports.
1.8.8
Quality / Test Lead
.  Coordinates voice SIT/UAT with BSC, manages defect triage, owns the Voice Production Release Readiness Report.

word/document.xml
Exhibit A-58
Statement of Work
THIS STATEMENT OF WORK (the “SOW”) is made, entered into, and effective 
June 1, 2026
 (the “Effective Date”), by and between Performance Technology Partners, LLC (“Consultant”) and 
Stellarus, LLC
 (“
Stellarus
”).  This SOW shall be governed by the terms and conditions of the Consulting Agreement 
originally entered into between Consultant and California Physicians’ Service d/b/a Blue Shield of California dated August 27, 2007 and subsequently assigned to Stellarus pursuant to the Notice of Assignment of Consulting Agreement to Affiliate dated October 17, 2024, as amended (collectively, the “Agreement”).
1.
Services
1.1
Overview
.  Consultant shall extend the AI Agent originally developed for chat under SOW A-57 to support inbound voice interactions through the same generative AI Agent on the Sierra platform.  This Statement of Work covers all modifications, adaptations and additions to the AI Agent that are required for it to operate effectively in the voice modality.  The integration work that routes inbound voice calls from the BSC IVR through Genesys Cloud CX (“GCX”) into the AI Agent, and the corresponding live-agent transfer behavior, is addressed under SOW A-59.
Voice adaptation is non-trivial.  The same AI Agent reasoning core can be reused, but the conversational design, response length and style, knowledge framing, disclaimer pattern, error/disfluency handling, and evaluations all change materially in a voice context.  In addition, the AI Agent must interoperate with speech recognition (ASR) and speech synthesis (TTS), must support barge-in and interruption, must tolerate misrecognitions, and must produce conversational turns appropriately scoped for spoken delivery.
At a high level, Consultant will deliver: (a) a Voice SSD Addendum to the chat SSD produced under SOW A-57, (b) updated Sierra workspace configuration encoding voice-specific behaviors and persona, (c) voice-adapted knowledge content where existing knowledge requires reframing for spoken delivery, (d) a pronunciation lexicon and 
custom dictionary
 for benefit-specific terminology, (e) a voice-specific evaluation/simulation suite, (f) test execution results, and (g) operations enablement for the voice modality.
1.2
Services
.  Consultant shall provide the following services to BSC (the “Services”):
1.2.1
Voice Solution Specification Addendum
.  Consultant shall produce a Voice Solution Specification Addendum (the “Voice SSD Addendum”) to the chat SSD produced under SOW A-57.  The Voice SSD Addendum will document the additional and modified behaviors required for the AI Agent in voice, the corresponding evaluations, the speech-input and speech-output behaviors, the barge-in and interruption policy, the silence and no-input timeout policy, the misrecognition recovery policy, and the voice escalation contract that will be consumed by the GCX integration delivered under SOW A-59.
Where a chat behavior translates without change to voice, the Voice SSD Addendum will reference the chat SSD; where it must change for voice, the Voice SSD Addendum will define the voice-specific version, classified as “must,” “must not,” “should,” or “should not,” and the associated evaluations.
The Voice SSD Addendum will define the audio quality, latency budget, and turn-taking expectations the AI Agent must meet.
1.2.2
Voice Persona, Prompt and Tone Adaptation
.  Consultant shall adapt the AI Agent persona for spoken delivery.  This includes voice persona definition, system-prompt adjustments to instruct the AI Agent to produce response turns that read well aloud (shorter sentences, no bulleted lists, no markdown, no URLs), spoken disclaimers, spoken citations (e.g., “according to your 2026 PPO plan summary”), and revised refusal and escalation language tuned for voice.
1.2.3
Speech I/O Tuning
.  Consultant shall tune the speech-input (ASR) and speech-output (TTS) characteristics of the voice AI Agent.  ASR tuning includes assembling a domain vocabulary and phrase list of benefit-specific terminology (plan names, network names, benefit categories, common acronyms)
 and 
authoring a pronunciation lexicon for proper nouns and acronyms that are routinely misrecognized or mispronounced.
1.2.4
Voice-Specific Behavior Configuration
.  Consultant shall configure the voice-specific behaviors documented in the Voice SSD Addendum.  This includes barge-in handling (when an employee speaks over the AI Agent), no-input and no-match recovery, misrecognition recovery (e.g., re-prompts and disambiguation), confirmation strategy for high-stakes information (e.g., before transferring), conversational repair, and graceful fall-through to a live-agent transfer when the AI Agent cannot continue.
Consultant shall configure the in-flight filler/holding pattern for the AI Agent so that the employee perceives responsiveness while back-end tool calls or retrievals are in progress.
1.2.5
Voice Knowledge Adaptation
.  Consultant shall review the existing chat knowledge base produced under SOW A-57 and adapt content where the chat presentation is not appropriate for voice.  
1.2.6
Audio Connector Agent-Side Configuration
.  Consultant shall perform the AI Agent–side configuration required to interoperate with the Sierra Genesys Audio Connector that connects voice traffic to the AI Agent.  This includes session initiation parameters, metadata mapping (e.g., authenticated employee identifier, plan identifier, IVR collected data), session lifecycle handling, and the escalation contract used to surface the AI Agent’s voice transfer signal to GCX.
The Sierra Genesys Audio Connector itself is a Sierra-supplied integration, and Sierra is responsible for that connector.  The GCX-side configuration that consumes the Audio Connector is in scope under SOW A-59.
1.2.7
Voice Evaluation and Simulation Engineering
.  Consultant shall implement voice-specific evaluations as simulations in the Sierra platform, including but not limited to: (a) audio-input simulations covering accented speech, background noise, and varying speaking rates within the limits supported by the platform, (b) misrecognition-recovery evaluations, (c) barge-in evaluations, (
d
) voice-specific refusal and escalation evaluations, and (
e
) regression coverage of every chat “must” behavior to confirm parity in voice.

Exhibit A-59
Statement of Work
THIS STATEMENT OF WORK (the “SOW”) is made, entered into, and effective 
June 1, 2026
 (the “Effective Date”), by and between Performance Technology Partners, LLC (“Consultant”) and 
Stellarus, LLC
 (“
Stellarus
”).  This SOW shall be governed by the terms and conditions of the Consulting Agreement 
originally entered into between Consultant and California Physicians’ Service d/b/a Blue Shield of California dated August 27, 2007 and subsequently assigned to Stellarus pursuant to the Notice of Assignment of Consulting Agreement to Affiliate dated October 17, 2024, as amended (collectively, the “Agreement”).
1.
     
Services
1.1
Overview
.
  Consultant shall design, configure and prepare for production release the Genesys Cloud CX (“GCX”) integration work required to expose the AI Agent to BSC employees through the BSC web portal and through the existing inbound telephony channel, and to handle escalation from the AI Agent to a live agent.  This Statement of Work covers all GCX-side configuration and integration work.  The AI Agent itself (the conversational reasoning core, prompts, knowledge base, evaluations and operations enablement) is delivered under SOW 
A-
57 for chat and SOW 
A-
58 for voice.
The integration work in this SOW falls into three principal areas: (1) exposing the chat experience on the BSC employee portal via Genesys Cloud Messaging and connecting that chat channel to the AI Agent on Sierra through the Sierra Genesys Bot Connector; (2) routing inbound voice calls collected by the BSC IVR into GCX and from GCX into the voice AI Agent through the Sierra Genesys Audio Connector, including the passing of IVR-collected metadata; and (3) implementing the escalation paths from the AI Agent to a live agent, including chat-to-voice callback during business hours and warm transfer with conversation context.
At a high level, Consultant will deliver: (a) an Integration Specification Document and end-to-end Solution Architecture Diagram, (b) the configured Genesys Cloud Messaging deployment on the BSC employee portal, (c) GCX Architect flows for inbound chat routing and bot connection, (d) GCX Architect flows for inbound voice routing and Audio Connector connection, (e) a GCX callback flow for chat-to-voice escalation, (f) a warm transfer flow with live-agent context handoff, (g) reporting and analytics dashboards, (h) an end-to-end test plan and results
.
1.2
Services
. 
 Consultant shall provide the following services to BSC (the “Services”):
1.2.1
Integration Specification
.  Consultant shall produce an Integration Specification Document (the “Integration SSD”) that defines the end-to-end design for chat and voice routing, identifying every interface between systems (BSC portal, Genesys Cloud Messaging, GCX inbound chat, Sierra Genesys Bot Connector, AI Agent on Sierra, BSC IVR, GCX inbound voice, Sierra Genesys Audio Connector, live-agent desktop), the payloads exchanged at each interface, the routing rules, the authentication and authorization model, the escalation contracts consumed from the AI Agent, the disposition and wrap-up conventions, and the data-retention and logging behavior.
The Integration SSD will be paired with an end-to-end Solution Architecture Diagram showing the systems, the interfaces, the data and control flows for chat, the data and control flows for voice, and the escalation paths.  The Integration SSD will identify all configuration that is BSC-owned versus 
Consultant
-owned and the change-control process for each.
1.2.2
Portal Web Messaging Deployment
.
  Consultant shall configure and deploy the Genesys Cloud Messaging chat experience on the BSC employee portal.  This includes the Messenger configuration, the portal-side embed script provided to the BSC web team for inclusion in the portal, the authentication handshake so that the AI Agent receives the authenticated employee context (employee identifier, plan identifier, any other portal-provided context), and the launch behavior (entry points, business hours behavior, holiday behavior).
Consultant will work with the BSC Web Developer on the embed mechanics and will provide a documented embed integration package suitable for inclusion in the portal release.
1.2.3
GCX Inbound Chat Routing and Bot Connector Integration
.
  Consultant shall design and configure the GCX Architect inbound message flow that receives portal-originated chat sessions, validates the inbound payload, applies routing rules, and connects the session to the AI Agent on Sierra through the Sierra Genesys Bot Connector.  Consultant shall configure the Bot Connector integration on the GCX side, including the authentication parameters, session-initiation payload, session-update payload, and the disposition contract returned to GCX.
Consultant shall configure the GCX skill, queue and routing logic required to handle escalation from the AI Agent to live agents during business hours, including business-hours and holiday schedules, queue overflow behavior, and after-hours behavior.
1.2.4
IVR-to-GCX Inbound Voice Routing
.  Consultant shall design and configure the inbound voice routing that transfers calls from the existing BSC IVR into GCX along with the relevant IVR-collected metadata (such as authenticated employee identifier, plan identifier, intent or menu selection, and any other agreed metadata).  Consultant shall work with the BSC IVR Developer and Telecommunications Administrator to specify the IVR-to-GCX handoff interface (e.g., SIP REFER with custom headers, UUI data, or other agreed mechanism) and the metadata mapping into GCX participant data.
Consultant shall configure the GCX Architect inbound voice flow that receives the transferred call, validates the inbound metadata, applies the routing rules, and connects the call to the voice AI Agent through the Sierra Genesys Audio Connector.
The BSC IVR application code itself is BSC-owned; Consultant will work with the BSC IVR Developer to specify the IVR-side changes required to perform the handoff and to populate the metadata, but the implementation and deployment of those IVR changes is performed by BSC.
1.2.5
GCX Audio Connector Integration for Voice AI Agent
.  Consultant shall configure the GCX-side Audio Connector integration that connects an inbound voice call to the voice AI Agent on Sierra.  This includes session initiation, the metadata payload, the disposition / escalation contract returned to GCX, and the GCX behavior on each disposition (continue, transfer to live agent, schedule callback, end call).
The Sierra Genesys Audio Connector itself is a Sierra-supplied integration; the AI Agent–side configuration is performed under SOW 
A-
58.
1.2.6
Chat-to-Voice Callback Configuration
.  Consultant shall configure the GCX callback functionality used to transition an employee from web chat to a voice call with a live agent during business hours when the AI Agent cannot complete the request in chat.  This includes the callback request capture in the chat session, the GCX callback queue, 
expected-wait-time messaging, callback retry behavior, and the live-agent screen-pop on callback delivery showing the originating chat transcript summary.
Consultant shall configure the after-hours behavior for callback requests (e.g., offer next-business-day callback windows or queue for the next business day, per BSC policy documented in the Integration SSD).
1.2.7
Warm Transfer and Live Agent Context Handoff
.  
Consultant shall configure the warm-transfer flow that hands an employee from the AI Agent to a live agent, in both chat and voice, when the AI Agent signals the need for escalation.  Consultant shall configure the live-agent screen-pop / context payload so that the receiving live agent has the conversation summary, the employee identifier, the plan identifier, the reason for escalation, and a transcript link.
Consultant shall configure the GCX disposition / wrap-up codes used to capture the outcome of the live-agent interaction following an AI Agent escalation, to support reporting in section 1.2.8 below.
Consultant will coordinate with BSC on any agent-desktop-side changes required to render the context payload; changes to BSC live-agent desktop tooling beyond consumption of the agreed context payload are out of scope.
1.2.8
Reporting, Analytics and Dashboards
. 
 Consultant shall configure 
native 
GCX reporting and at least one operational dashboard covering the AI Agent traffic for both chat and voice.
 Custom report development is not included in this scope of work.
  
1.2.9
End-to-End Integration Testing
.  
Consultant shall produce and execute an End-to-End Integration Test Plan covering all integration paths.  The test plan will cover happy paths, business-hours and after-hours behavior, disposition handling, escalation context handoff, and negative cases including connector failure, AI Agent timeout, and queue overflow.
Consultant will coordinate execution with the SOW 
A-
57 (chat AI Agent) and SOW 
A-
58 (voice AI Agent) workstreams and will report integration defects to the appropriate workstream for remediation.  BSC is responsible for performing and signing off on integration User Acceptance Testing; Consultant will provide test scripts, test data, evidence packages and defect-triage support.
1.2.10
 
Production Cutover
.  Consultant shall produce a Production Cutover Plan covering the staged rollout of portal Messaging, IVR-to-GCX routing, callback, and warm transfer.
Consultant shall support the production cutover activities defined in the cutover plan, including configuration promotion, smoke testing, and hyper-care support during the first two bus
i
ness weeks following production release.
1.2.11
 
Project Management
.  Consultant shall provide project management for Services, including but not limited to the following:
1.2.11.1
 
Serve as the primary contact for all questions and issues related to Consultant’s Services hereunder.
1.2.11.2
 
Create and maintain a project plan (the “Project Plan”) and provide a weekly status report (the “Weekly Status Report”) of Consultant’s project progress, staff management, risks, and issues, including coordination touchpoints with the SOW 57 and SOW 58 workstreams.
1.2.11.3
 
Maintain a risk and issue log and a decision log, updated weekly and reviewed in the weekly status meeting.
1.2.11.4
 
BSC will appoint a single point of contact responsible for all communications and project management among all Customer parties (staff, vendors, consultants) and for the escalation and resolution of any issues for BSC.
1.2.11.5
 
The participation and commitment of BSC’s project team during the project, including assigned tasks to BSC team members, will be a key to project success.
1.2.11.6
 
BSC will provide qualified development engineering/programming resources versed in Customer’s application(s) during any development/integration portion of this project as needed.
1.2.11.7
 
All Services, materials and communications are assumed to be delivered in English, unless otherwise specifically noted.
1.3
Consultant Personnel
.  Consultant shall
 ensure that its personnel assigned to perform services under this SOW have the necessary qualifications, competence and experience required to provide the Service and Deliverables.  If BSC, at its sole discretion, is not satisfied with the performance of any Consultant personnel, BSC shall notify Consultant and Consultant shall promptly furnish replacement personnel.  BSC 
retains the right at all times
 to end the assignment 
of any personnel Consultant provides under this SOW.
1.4
Term
.
  Consultant shall begin providing the Services under this SOW on the Effective Date and Consultant will complete all Services and provide all Deliverables no later than
 
September 30
th
, 2026
.  Unless otherwise terminated earlier pursuant to the terms of the Agreement, this SOW will terminate on completion of all Services, including final acceptance of all Deliverables.
1.5
Key BSC Roles
.  The participation and commitment of BSC’s project team will be a key to project success.  BSC
 will provide qualified business and technical resources versed in BSC’s applications and systems during the project as needed.  The following key customer roles shall be filled by BSC:
1.5.1
Project Sponsor
.
  The Project Sponsor shall be able to articulate the project vision, identify and provide needed resources and funding, and oversee the successful deployment and adoption of the integration.
1.5.2
Web Developer
.  The Web Developer is responsible for embedding the Genesys Cloud Messenger in the BSC employee portal.  They will participate in design sessions and serve as the point of contact for any portal-side issues.
1.5.3
IT Administrator
.  The IT Administrator is responsible for providing infrastructure and network connectivity between BSC systems, GCX and Sierra, ensuring that the network connectivity is robust, and serving as the point of contact for any infrastructure or network issues.
1.5.4
Telecommunications Administrator
.  The Telecommunications Administrator is responsible for administering the telecommunications environment at BSC and for the SIP / IVR-to-GCX handoff configuration on the BSC telephony 
side, and
 serves as the point of contact for any telecommunications or contact-center infrastructure changes or issues.
1.5.5
IVR Developer
.  The IVR Developer is responsible for the BSC IVR application, including any IVR changes required to perform the handoff to GCX and to populate the IVR-
collected metadata defined in the Integration SSD.  They will participate in design sessions, provide the call-flow documentation as part of design, and serve as the point of contact for any IVR issues.
1.5.6
Contact Center Operations Lead
.  BSC shall designate a Contact Center Operations Lead who will own the live-agent queues, schedules, dispositions, and wrap-up codes affected by the integration, and who will participate in the design of escalation, callback and warm-transfer behavior.
1.6

.  This SOW is predicated on the following assumptions and dependencies.  If any of

Consultant
 personnel working in BSC’s San Francisco office (except for travel to BSC locations outside of the greater Bay Area) are not reimbursable.

BSC 
will not
 reimburse for the following expenses:  Limousine service, parking tickets, moving violations, or additional automobile insurance.

 personnel who use their personal car to perform services for BSC at locations other than their BSC assigned office.  Consultant personnel may submit expenses for the miles 
in excess of

are considered to be
 part of Consultant’s overhead costs and are not eligible for reimbursement.

Other Requirements:

Exhibit A-59
Statement of Work
THIS STATEMENT OF WORK (the “SOW”) is made, entered into, and effective 
June 1, 2026
 (the “Effective Date”), by and between Performance Technology Partners, LLC (“Consultant”) and 
Stellarus, LLC
 (“
Stellarus
”).  This SOW shall be governed by the terms and conditions of the Consulting Agreement 
originally entered into between Consultant and California Physicians’ Service d/b/a Blue Shield of California dated August 27, 2007 and subsequently assigned to Stellarus pursuant to the Notice of Assignment of Consulting Agreement to Affiliate dated October 17, 2024, as amended (collectively, the “Agreement”).
1.
     
Services
1.1
Overview
.
  Consultant shall design, configure and prepare for production release the Genesys Cloud CX (“GCX”) integration work required to expose the AI Agent to BSC employees through the BSC web portal and through the existing inbound telephony channel, and to handle escalation from the AI Agent to a live agent.  This Statement of Work covers all GCX-side configuration and integration work.  The AI Agent itself (the conversational reasoning core, prompts, knowledge base, evaluations and operations enablement) is delivered under SOW 
A-
57 for chat and SOW 
A-
58 for voice.
The integration work in this SOW falls into 
two
 
principal areas: (1) exposing the chat experience on the BSC employee portal via Genesys Cloud Messaging and connecting that chat channel to the AI Agent on Sierra through the Sierra Genesys Bot Connector; and (
2
) implementing the escalation paths from the AI Agent to a live agent, including chat-to-voice callback during business hours and warm transfer with conversation context.
At a high level, Consultant will deliver: (a) an Integration Specification Document and end-to-end Solution Architecture Diagram, (b) the configured Genesys Cloud Messaging deployment on the BSC employee portal, (c) GCX Architect flows for inbound chat routing and bot connection, (d) a GCX callback flow for chat-to-voice escalation, (
e
) a warm transfer flow with live-agent context handoff, (
f
) reporting and analytics dashboards, (
g
) an end-to-end test plan and results
.
1.2
Services
. 
 Consultant shall provide the following services to BSC (the “Services”):
1.2.1
Integration Specification
.  Consultant shall produce an Integration Specification Document (the “Integration SSD”) that defines the end-to-end design for chat routing, identifying every interface between systems (BSC portal, Genesys Cloud Messaging, GCX inbound chat, Sierra Genesys Bot Connector, AI Agent on Sierra, , Sierra Genesys Audio Connector, live-agent desktop), the payloads exchanged at each interface, the routing rules, the authentication and authorization model, the escalation contracts consumed from the AI Agent, the disposition and wrap-up conventions, and the data-retention and logging behavior.
The Integration SSD will be paired with an end-to-end Solution Architecture Diagram showing the systems, the interfaces, the data and control flows for chat, the data and control flows for voice, and the escalation paths.  The Integration SSD will identify all configuration that is BSC-owned versus 
Consultant
-owned and the change-control process for each.
1.2.2
Portal Web Messaging Deployment
.
  Consultant shall configure and deploy the Genesys Cloud Messaging chat experience on the BSC employee portal.  This includes the Messenger configuration, the portal-side embed script provided to the BSC web team for 
inclusion in the portal, the authentication handshake so that the AI Agent receives the authenticated employee context (employee identifier, plan identifier, any other portal-provided context), and the launch behavior (entry points, business hours behavior, holiday behavior).
Consultant will work with the BSC Web Developer on the embed mechanics and will provide a documented embed integration package suitable for inclusion in the portal release.
1.2.3
GCX Inbound Chat Routing and Bot Connector Integration
.
  Consultant shall design and configure the GCX Architect inbound message flow that receives portal-originated chat sessions, validates the inbound payload, applies routing rules, and connects the session to the AI Agent on Sierra through the Sierra Genesys Bot Connector.  Consultant shall configure the Bot Connector integration on the GCX side, including the authentication parameters, session-initiation payload, session-update payload, and the disposition contract returned to GCX.
Consultant shall configure the GCX skill, queue and routing logic required to handle escalation from the AI Agent to live agents during business hours, including business-hours and holiday schedules, queue overflow behavior, and after-hours behavior.
1.2.
4
Chat-to-Voice Callback Configuration
.  Consultant shall configure the GCX callback functionality used to transition an employee from web chat to a voice call with a live agent during business hours when the AI Agent cannot complete the request in chat.  This includes the callback request capture in the chat session, the GCX callback queue, expected-wait-time messaging, callback retry behavior, and the live-agent screen-pop on callback delivery showing the originating chat transcript summary.
Consultant shall configure the after-hours behavior for callback requests (e.g., offer next-business-day callback windows or queue for the next business day, per BSC policy documented in the Integration SSD).
1.2.7
Warm Transfer and Live Agent Context Handoff
.  
Consultant shall configure the warm-transfer flow that hands an employee from the AI Agent to a live agent, in chat, when the AI Agent signals the need for escalation.  Consultant shall configure the live-agent screen-pop / context payload so that the receiving live agent has the conversation summary, the employee identifier, the plan identifier, the reason for escalation, and a transcript link.
Consultant shall configure the GCX disposition / wrap-up codes used to capture the outcome of the live-agent interaction following an AI Agent escalation, to support reporting in section 1.2.8 below.
Consultant will coordinate with BSC on any agent-desktop-side changes required to render the context payload; changes to BSC live-agent desktop tooling beyond consumption of the agreed context payload are out of scope.
1.2.8
Reporting, Analytics and Dashboards
. 
 Consultant shall configure 
native 
GCX reporting and at least one operational dashboard covering the AI Agent traffic for chat.
 Custom report development is not included in this scope of work.
  
1.2.9
End-to-End Integration Testing
.  
Consultant shall produce and execute an End-to-End Integration Test Plan covering all integration paths.  The test plan will cover happy paths, 
business-hours and after-hours behavior, disposition handling, escalation context handoff, and negative cases including connector failure, AI Agent timeout, and queue overflow.
Consultant will coordinate execution with the SOW 
A-
57 (chat AI Agent) workstream and will report integration defects for remediation.  BSC is responsible for performing and signing off on integration User Acceptance Testing; Consultant will provide test scripts, test data, evidence packages and defect-triage support.
1.2.10
 
Production Cutover
.  Consultant shall produce a Production Cutover Plan covering the staged rollout of portal Messaging, callback, and warm transfer.
Consultant shall support the production cutover activities defined in the cutover plan, including configuration promotion, smoke testing, and hyper-care support during the first two bus
i
ness weeks following production release.
1.2.11
 
Project Management
.  Consultant shall provide project management for Services, including but not limited to the following:
1.2.11.1
 
Serve as the primary contact for all questions and issues related to Consultant’s Services hereunder.
1.2.11.2
 
Create and maintain a project plan (the “Project Plan”) and provide a weekly status report (the “Weekly Status Report”) of Consultant’s project progress, staff management, risks, and issues, including coordination touchpoints with the SOW 57 and SOW 58 workstreams.
1.2.11.3
 
Maintain a risk and issue log and a decision log, updated weekly and reviewed in the weekly status meeting.
1.2.11.4
 
BSC will appoint a single point of contact responsible for all communications and project management among all Customer parties (staff, vendors, consultants) and for the escalation and resolution of any issues for BSC.
1.2.11.5
 
The participation and commitment of BSC’s project team during the project, including assigned tasks to BSC team members, will be a key to project success.
1.2.11.6
 
BSC will provide qualified development engineering/programming resources versed in Customer’s application(s) during any development/integration portion of this project as needed.
1.2.11.7
 
All Services, materials and communications are assumed to be delivered in English, unless otherwise specifically noted.
1.3
Consultant Personnel
.  Consultant shall
 ensure that its personnel assigned to perform services under this SOW have the necessary qualifications, competence and experience required to provide the Service and Deliverables.  If BSC, at its sole discretion, is not satisfied with the performance of any Consultant personnel, BSC shall notify Consultant and Consultant shall promptly furnish replacement personnel.  BSC 
retains the right at all times
 to end the assignment 
of any personnel Consultant provides under this SOW.
1.4
Term
.
  Consultant shall begin providing the Services under this SOW on the Effective Date and Consultant will complete all Services and provide all Deliverables no later than
 
September 30
th
, 2026
.  Unless otherwise terminated earlier pursuant to the terms of the Agreement, this SOW will terminate on completion of all Services, including final acceptance of all Deliverables.
1.5
Key BSC Roles
.  The participation and commitment of BSC’s project team will be a key to project success.  BSC
 will provide qualified business and technical resources versed in BSC’s applications and systems during the project as needed.  The following key customer roles shall be filled by BSC:
1.5.1
Project Sponsor

  The Project Sponsor shall be able to articulate the project vision, identify and provide needed resources and funding, and oversee the successful deployment and adoption of the integration.
1.5.2
Web Developer
.  The Web Developer is responsible for embedding the Genesys Cloud Messenger in the BSC employee portal.  They will participate in design sessions and serve as the point of contact for any portal-side issues.
1.5.3
IT Administrator
.  The IT Administrator is responsible for providing infrastructure and network connectivity between BSC systems, GCX and Sierra, ensuring that the network connectivity is robust, and serving as the point of contact for any infrastructure or network issues.
1.5.
4
Contact Center Operations Lead
.  BSC shall designate a Contact Center Operations Lead who will own the live-agent queues, schedules, dispositions, and wrap-up codes affected by the integration, and who will participate in the design of escalation, callback and warm-transfer behavior.
1.6

these change
 materially, Consultant may request a change to scope, schedule, and/or fees pursuant to the Agreement:
1.6

AI Agent Configuration and Knowledge

A-
57
.

Test Lead (Integration)

Executive Summary
Build a generative agent (GA) chat interface within the Blue Shield CA member portal focused exclusively on benefits support, with initial pilot launch to BSC employees who have BSC insurance. Future expansion to other lines of business and use cases will take place through 2027.
Key Scope Decisions:
• Benefits support only (excludes claims, billing, other use cases)
• BSC members who are employees as pilot group
• Member portal/Genesys integration
• Sierra.ai for managing the GA
• End of Q2 2026 target launch with BSC Employees (stretch goal, not required by the MEM team)

COMPASS
CSR Chat
User & Training Guide
Prepared by    
Stellarus
Document owner    
Product and Customer Operations / Training
Date    
August 2026
Version    
v1.1 Draft
ABOUT THIS DOCUMENT
This guide explains how authorized customer service representatives use Compass CSR Chat during live interactions. It covers session readiness, effective questions, response review, follow-up, fallback handling, responsible use, feedback, troubleshooting, and training readiness. Customer-specific access, privacy, support, and operating procedures remain authoritative for each deployment.
Contents
1. Purpose, Audience, and Document Boundaries
1.1 Intended audience
1.2 User responsibility
1.3 Document family
2. How CSR Chat Fits into the User Workflow
2.1 Standard workflow
2.2 Information and context
3. Access and Session Readiness

3.2 Verify context
4. Ask Effective Questions
4.1 Question pattern
4.2 Examples and practices
5. Review and Validate Responses
5.1 Response review
5.2 Before customer communication
6. Follow-Up and Conversation Management
7. Common User Workflows
8. When CSR Chat Cannot Answer
9. Responsible Use, Feedback, and Issue Reporting
10. Troubleshooting and Getting Help
11. Training and User Readiness
12. FAQs, Current Limitations, and Glossary
Appendix A. Practice Scenarios
Appendix B. User Quick Reference
1. Purpose, Audience, and Document Boundaries
Compass CSR Chat is an AI-powered decision-support assistant for benefit inquiries. It helps representatives retrieve and interpret plan-specific benefit information during live customer interactions. This guide establishes a safe, repeatable way to use the product without replacing customer procedures, authoritative sources, or human judgment.
Core user principle
CSR Chat supports the representative. The representative remains responsible for confirming the applicable context, reviewing the complete response, following required procedures, and communicating the final answer.
1.1 Intended audience
Authorized customer service representatives who use CSR Chat during member or provider interactions.
Supervisors, coaches, and trainers who prepare users and reinforce expected behavior.
Quality and benefit reviewers who assess answer use and provide feedback.
1.2 User responsibility
Use CSR Chat only for approved business purposes and supported benefit inquiries.
Confirm that the correct customer and plan context is active before asking a question.
Review the full response and apply required validation before communicating it.
Use an approved source or escalation path when the answer is missing, unclear, conflicting, or appears incorrect.
Protect PHI and PII according to the health plan's policies and approved product procedures.
1.3 Document family
Document
Question it answers
Authoritative content
Product Brief
Why use CSR Chat and what does it do?
Problem, value, current capabilities, use cases, journeys, and product boundaries
Implementation & Integration Guide
How is CSR Chat deployed?
Readiness, implementation phases, resources, data, authentication, integration, testing, and launch
Technical Architecture & Security Overview
How does CSR Chat work and protect data?
Architecture, data flow, storage, security controls, retention, PHI, and HIPAA assurance
User & Training Guide
How should a representative use CSR Chat?
User workflow, question quality, review, fallback, responsible use, troubleshooting, and training
Customer operating procedures
What exact steps and contacts apply here?
Launch path, roles, source precedence, PHI rules, session rules, screenshots, support, and escalation
2. How CSR Chat Fits into the User Workflow
2.1 Standard workflow
SCREENSHOT TODO
Add an approved overview screenshot of the primary CSR Chat workspace. Annotate the major regions a user needs to recognize—active context, conversation area, question entry, response area, supporting-source area when enabled, and feedback controls. Use the current production release and mask or replace all PHI, PII, customer names, member identifiers, and plan-specific data.
Stage
User action
CSR Chat role
1. Receive
Understand the customer's question and identify the applicable member, plan, benefit, and effective period in approved systems
Does not independently search for a member or determine which plan applies
2. Prepare
Open CSR Chat through the approved launch path and verify the displayed or inherited context
Receives authenticated customer and plan context from the calling application
3. Ask
Enter one clear, specific benefit question using only permitted information
Retrieves relevant information from the approved plan context
4. Review
Read the full answer, conditions, disclosures, and any displayed supporting context
Presents a structured response grounded in available benefit data
5. Resolve
Ask a focused follow-up, validate in approved sources, use another process, or escalate
Continues within permitted context or reports that the question cannot be answered
6. Communicate
Provide the customer response only after completing required review
Supports but does not replace representative judgment
7. Improve
Submit feedback when an answer is helpful, incomplete, or incorrect
Routes available feedback for quality review
2.2 Information and context
CSR Chat answers from approved benefit data associated with the plan context supplied for the request. The calling application supplies that context; CSR Chat does not select a member or determine which plan applies.
Plan identifiers determine which benefit data is available.
Effective dates may determine which plan version applies.
Available answers depend on the plans and information domains loaded and validated for the deployment.
CSR Chat is not permitted to answer unsupported questions from general knowledge.
Customer-specific rule
The health plan's operating procedure defines which member, case, plan, and effective-date context must be confirmed before a question is asked. That procedure takes precedence over general examples in this guide.
3. Access and Session Readiness
3.1 Before starting
SCREENSHOT TODO
Add screenshots of the approved launch entry point and authenticated landing state for each supported delivery model used by the customer. Show only the controls required to reach CSR Chat. Capture the release/version and environment, and do not expose identity details, internal URLs, or live customer data.
Use only the launch path, environment, and authentication method approved by the health plan. CSR Chat may be delivered through a Stellarus-hosted interface, embedded in the representative desktop, or accessed through a customer-built interface.
Readiness check
Confirm
Authorization
You are assigned an approved role and have completed required training
Authentication
You signed in through the approved health plan identity process
Environment
You are using the correct production or training environment
Customer context
The correct customer or tenant is active
Plan context
The applicable plan identifiers and effective period are present or inherited
Support path
You know the approved procedure for access, product, privacy, or answer-quality issues
3.2 Verify context
SCREENSHOT TODO
Add a close-up screenshot showing where the user confirms customer, member or case context when applicable, plan identifiers, and effective period. Label which fields are inherited versus user-selected. Use synthetic data and include a caption explaining what must be verified before asking a question.
Before asking a question, confirm the context required by the health plan's procedure. Do not assume that a previously selected member, plan, case, or effective period remains applicable.
Stop if required context is missing, unclear, or inconsistent with the customer inquiry.
Correct the context in the authoritative customer system before using CSR Chat.
Begin a new conversation when required by customer session rules or when the member, plan, effective period, or primary topic changes.
UI labels vary
Exact application URLs, buttons, field names, screenshots, and session controls depend on the selected delivery model and release. Use the current training materials approved for your deployment.
4. Ask Effective Questions
4.1 Question pattern
SCREENSHOT TODO
Add a screenshot of the question composer with a strong example question entered but not yet submitted. Annotate the entry field, submit control, any character or content guidance, and the context that makes the question specific. Use an approved benefit example with synthetic data.
A strong CSR Chat question asks for one benefit decision at a time and includes only the context needed to distinguish the service, network level, cost-share type, or effective period.
Question element
Guidance
Example
Benefit or service
Name the benefit or service precisely
Physical therapy, specialist visit, durable medical equipment
Information needed
Ask for coverage, cost sharing, limitations, or another specific detail
Is it covered? What cost sharing applies?
Network or tier
Include when the answer may differ by network level
In-network specialist
Conditions
Ask about limits, exclusions, or authorization when relevant
What limitations apply?
Effective period
Confirm the applicable plan year or effective date in the approved context
Current plan version
4.2 Examples and practices
Use case
Illustrative question
Coverage
Is physical therapy covered under this plan?
Cost sharing
What cost sharing applies to an in-network specialist visit?
Benefit conditions
What limitations apply to this durable medical equipment benefit?
Deductible relationship
Does the deductible apply before coinsurance for this benefit?
Clarification
Does that answer apply only to in-network services?
Ask one primary question at a time.
Use the health plan's approved terminology.
Include only information permitted by privacy and security policy.
Use a focused follow-up instead of combining unrelated questions.
Do not ask CSR Chat to select a plan, make a legal determination, adjudicate a claim, or answer from general knowledge.
Do not assume that a fluent or confident response is correct.
5. Review and Validate Responses
5.1 Response review
SCREENSHOT TODO
Add an annotated response-anatomy screenshot showing the main answer, plan or benefit detail, conditions and limitations, disclosure language, and supporting source or citation when enabled. The image should demonstrate what the representative must review before communicating the answer.
Response presentation varies by delivery model and customer configuration. A response may include an answer, plan details, conditions, disclosure language, and supporting context. Review every displayed element before using the response.
Review area
Question to answer
Context
Is this the correct customer, member or case context when required, plan, and effective period?
Direct answer
Does the response address the question that was actually asked?
Benefit detail
Is the benefit, service, network tier, and cost-share type correct?
Conditions
Are applicable limits, exclusions, deductible rules, or other conditions included?
Disclosure
Is required health plan or regulatory language present?
Supporting context
When displayed, is the source applicable, current, and consistent with approved records?
Completeness
Could the response be misunderstood without another detail or follow-up?
Consistency
Does the response conflict with an authoritative system, document, or procedure?
5.2 Before customer communication
Mandatory review
Do not communicate a CSR Chat response until you have reviewed it and completed every validation step required by the health plan's operating procedure.
Read the entire response, not only its first sentence.
Confirm material conditions and disclosure language.
Use an authoritative source when required by policy or when confidence is reduced.
Do not silently choose between conflicting sources.
If the response cannot be validated, use the approved fallback or escalation process.
Record or communicate information only through approved systems and channels.
6. Follow-Up and Conversation Management
SCREENSHOT TODO
Add a two-state screenshot showing a focused follow-up within the same verified context and the approved control for starting a new conversation. Annotate the visual cues that confirm whether prior context remains active. Use only synthetic conversation content.
A focused follow-up can clarify a response when it clearly refers to the same context and topic. Do not rely on conversational context when the applicable member, plan, effective period, service, or question has changed.
Situation
Recommended action
Clarify the same benefit
Ask a focused follow-up, such as whether a limitation applies to in-network services
Request a missing condition
Ask specifically about the deductible, visit limit, exclusion, or other missing detail
Change member, plan, or effective period
Start a new conversation using the procedure approved for the deployment
Change to an unrelated topic
Start a new conversation when required by customer session rules
Context is unclear
Stop, verify the authoritative context, and restart before continuing
Response conflicts with a source
Do not use a follow-up to resolve the conflict without verification; follow source-precedence and escalation procedures
Session boundaries
Conversation duration, expiration, history, and new-session controls are deployment-specific. Follow the current customer procedure and approved UI training rather than assuming that prior context persists.
7. Common User Workflows
SCREENSHOT TODO
Add a worked-example screenshot sequence for one coverage inquiry and one cost-share inquiry: verified context, submitted question, complete response, and the user's final review points. Keep each sequence short enough to scan and label it as illustrative rather than a guaranteed response format.
Workflow
Representative steps

1. Product Snapshot
Compass CSR Chat is an AI-powered decision-support assistant for health plan customer service representatives. During a live interaction, a representative asks a benefit question in natural language and receives a structured, plan-specific answer grounded in the health plan's approved benefit data.
Product promise
Help representatives reach accurate, consistent benefit information faster while keeping the representative responsible for the final customer communication.
1.1 What CSR Chat is
CSR Chat brings benefit interpretation into the representative workflow. It retrieves the plan context supplied with the request, identifies relevant benefit information, and generates an answer using that context. When the available context does not support an answer, the product is designed to say that it cannot answer rather than rely on general knowledge.
1.2 Who it serves

Technology and security teams

1.3 Product scope
The current product scope is representative-assisted benefit inquiry. Supported plan populations depend on which benefit data has been integrated and validated for the health plan. Additional domains are enabled only after their source data, rules, and validation are complete.
Agent-facing: CSR Chat supports representatives; it is not a member-facing chatbot.
Decision support: It assists with benefit questions; it is not a system of record or claims adjudication system.
Plan-grounded: It answers from approved customer context; it is not permitted to answer from general knowledge.
2. Problem and Value
2.1 The customer service challenge
Benefit questions often require representatives to move across plan documents, internal tools, and policy sources while a member or provider waits. Representatives must interpret specialized language, identify the correct plan details, and communicate required conditions consistently.

Limited visibility
Difficulty identifying recurring gaps and improvement opportunities
2.2 How CSR Chat helps
CSR Chat combines the health plan's approved benefit data with a controlled answer-generation workflow. The representative asks a question, the application retrieves relevant plan context, and the model produces a structured response for representative review. Customer-specific configuration controls terminology, presentation, and required disclosure language.
2.3 Expected outcomes
Faster access to benefit information during live interactions.
More consistent interpretation and presentation across representatives.
Greater representative confidence when handling complex benefit questions.
A repeatable validation and feedback loop for improving answer quality.
A scalable foundation for additional plans and approved information domains.
Measurement approach
Outcome targets are baselined with each health plan. Typical measures include time to answer, answer accuracy, required-disclosure compliance, representative adoption, feedback, and benefit-inquiry handle time. Results are not guaranteed and depend on implementation scope, source quality, workflow design, and adoption.

1. Purpose, Audience, and Document Boundaries

Use an authoritative source when required by policy or when confidence is reduced.
Do not silently choose between conflicting sources.
If the response cannot be validated, use the approved fallback or escalation process.
Record or communicate information only through approved systems and channels.

ABOUT THIS DOCUMENT
This guide describes how Compass CSR Chat works and what is required to implement it. It covers the solution architecture, data flows, answer accuracy and performance, data storage, system interfaces, and integrations, followed by the onboarding process, resource expectations, and dependencies.
