1. Product Overview
Compass CSR Chat is an assistant for call center representatives. While a member is on the phone, the representative types a question into a chat window and receives an answer based on that member's benefit plan.
1.1 Current capabilities
CSR Chat answers questions about 
benefits
. Answers are generated from the health plan's own benefit data, identified by plan identifiers.
1.2 Planned capabilities
The following content areas are on the product roadmap:
CAPABILITY
DESCRIPTION
Accumulators
Deductible, out of pocket, and visit limit balances for a member
Specialty
Specialty benefit detail, including pharmacy
Claims
Claim status and detail for a member
These capabilities are not available at implementation. Release sequencing is covered in the product roadmap.
1.3 Line of business coverage
CSR Chat has no line of business restrictions. A line of business is supported once its benefit data has been loaded.
During discovery, each line of business in scope is reviewed and three things are confirmed:
The benefit data exists.
The format it is delivered in, structured or unstructured.
Who provides it and how often it changes.
An implementation can begin with a subset of lines of business and add others later. Each is enabled as its data is loaded.
1.4 Answer configuration
CSR Chat is configured for each health plan. The benefit data determines what an answer says. The configuration determines how it is said.
AREA
WHAT IS CONFIGURED
Voice and terminology
Greeting and tone, and the terms the health plan uses for its own products, programs, and networks
Presentation
How an answer is structured and what is shown alongside it, such as cost tiers or plan specific detail
Disclosure language
Wording required by the health plan, by its regulators, or by a particular line of business
Configuration changes how an answer is worded and presented. It does not change where the answer comes from. Answers are always generated from the context loaded in AtlasIQ, as described in section 3.2.
1.5 System context
Figure 1. System context
Representatives reach CSR Chat through a chat interface, which is either hosted by Stellarus or built into the representative desktop. See section 5.2.
Every request passes through the Stellarus AI Gateway, which authenticates it and establishes which health plan's data may be read. CSR LLM generates the answer and runs inside the Stellarus Azure environment. See section 3.4.
There are two integration points:
Data in.
 Health plan benefit data is loaded into AtlasIQ, the Stellarus data foundation.
Chat out.
 The chat is delivered to representatives, either through an interface hosted by Stellarus or embedded in the health plan's existing representative desktop.
Stellarus operates everything between these two points.
2. Data Flow
The sequence below shows what happens when a representative asks a question.
Figure 2. Answering a question
Notes on the sequence:
The calling application supplies the context for each question. CSR Chat does not search for a member or determine which plan applies.
Answers are generated from the context retrieved from AtlasIQ. CSR Chat does not answer from general knowledge. See section 3.2.
Each request carries an authenticated health plan context resolved at the AI Gateway. That context determines which data is read.
Representatives can submit feedback on any answer. Feedback is retained for quality review and used to refine the answer configuration.
The request stays within the Stellarus Azure environment for its full path, including answer generation. See section 3.4.
3. Answer Accuracy and Performance
3.1 Validation before release
Answers are validated by people, not only by automated tests.
Simulated member calls.
 Testers act as members and ask benefit questions. Representatives answer the same questions with CSR Chat and without it, and the two sets of answers are compared for accuracy and for the time taken to reach them.
Plan expert review.
 Benefit plan experts review a test set of more than 200 questions, ranging from routine coverage questions to rare and complex cases. Answers are assessed against the benefit plan as the expert would interpret it.
The same approach is applied to each health plan implementation during phase 4 of the implementation, using that health plan's own benefit data and its own reviewers.
3.2 Guardrails
CSR Chat answers only questions that the retrieved context can support. Guardrails restrict the assistant to that scope, and questions outside it are not answered.
Every answer is generated from the context retrieved from AtlasIQ for that request, which today is benefit plan data. The model has no other source to draw on and is not permitted to answer from general knowledge.
Where the retrieved context does not contain the answer, CSR Chat reports that the question cannot be answered rather than generating one. This is a design constraint, not a configuration setting, and it is verified in the expert review described in section 3.1 before every release.
3.3 Model selection and change control
Frontier language models are evaluated against each other on answer quality and response time, and the model that gives the best balance of the two is selected.
Model changes follow a controlled process:
The candidate model is run against the established test set.
Results are compared against the current model on both accuracy and response time.
A human reviewer validates the results before the change is approved.
No model change reaches production without this test cycle and human sign-off.
3.4 Model hosting and data use
Models run in Azure AI Foundry inside the Stellarus Azure environment.
CONTROL
DESCRIPTION
Retention at the model
Zero day retention. Prompts and responses are not retained by the model service
Training
Health plan benefit data and member questions are never used to train or fine tune any model, by Stellarus or by any model provider
Boundary
No data leaves the Stellarus Azure environment in the course of generating an answer
3.5 Performance
Answers are returned in under 15 seconds. Response time is treated as a functional requirement rather than a target, because the representative is holding a live call while the answer is generated.
Response time is measured as part of model selection and is tested before every release. Availability, response time, and error rates are monitored in production, with alerting on degradation.
4. Data Storage
Health plan data is held in a dedicated data boundary within AtlasIQ. The following applies to all data stored there.
CONTROL
DESCRIPTION
Isolation
Each health plan's data is stored in a boundary dedicated to that health plan
Access
A request authenticated for one health plan cannot read another health plan's data. This is enforced centrally rather than by individual services
Context
Health plan identity and data location are resolved centrally and passed to each service as a signed context
Encryption
Data is encrypted in transit and at rest
Location
All data is stored and processed onshore in the United States
Conversation records
All conversations are retained and available as an audit record
Backup and retention
Backup, restore, and retention are performed per health plan. Retention periods are set in the agreement
These controls apply to the AtlasIQ platform as a whole. Every Stellarus product built on AtlasIQ operates under them.
5. Interfaces and Integrations
5.1 Data provided by the health plan
ITEM
DESCRIPTION
Benefit plan data
The benefit plan definitions CSR Chat answers from, identified by plan identifiers
Effective dates
Plan versions, so answers reflect the plan in force for a member on a given date
Accepted formats.
 Structured extracts and unstructured plan documents such as PDFs. Unstructured documents are parsed into machine readable form during ingestion. All data is normalized to the AtlasIQ data models, so CSR Chat reads a single consistent representation of a benefit plan regardless of the source format.
Transfer and refresh.
 AtlasIQ supports several ingestion patterns. The transfer method and refresh cadence are agreed during discovery, based on how the health plan's source data is produced.
5.2 Chat delivery
Three delivery options are available.
OPTION
HEALTH PLAN DEVELOPMENT EFFORT
SUITED TO
Stellarus-hosted interface
None. Representatives use a web interface provided by Stellarus, white labeled with health plan branding, signing in through the health plan identity provider
Pilot and early production
Embedded in the representative desktop
The chat is embedded in the health plan's existing desktop, with requests routed through a backend operated by the health plan
Production at scale
API only
The health plan builds an interface against the Stellarus API
Health plans with established desktop and interface standards
White labeling.
 The Stellarus-hosted interface is white labeled. It carries health plan branding rather than Stellarus branding, so representatives see an interface consistent with the other tools they use. Branding is configured during implementation. In the embedded and API options the interface is built and branded by the health plan.
Request context.
 In all three options, context is supplied with the request rather than discovered by CSR Chat. Today that is the plan identifiers, taken from the member record the representative already has open in the desktop or portal. CSR Chat does not search for a member or determine which plan applies.
The identifiers that make up a plan reference are agreed during discovery. They vary by health plan and by core system, and can include an effective date so the answer reflects the plan in force at the time of the call.
As member-level content such as accumulators and claims is added, the identifiers supplied with the request extend accordingly.
5.3 Authentication and access
All access is through the Stellarus AI Gateway. There is no direct network access to underlying services.

# Project Name: CSR Chat Customer Golden Dataset for Rapid Pilots

**PDLC Phase:** Definition  
**Authored Date:** October 2, 2026  
**Status:** DRAFT  
**Target Timebox:** 4 weeks  
**Decision Owner:** Product  
**Delivery Partners:** Data Science, Benefits SMEs, Implementation, Engineering, Security, Customer Success

## Problem Statement

Compass CSR Chat needs customer-specific evidence that it can answer the questions a customer expects before a rapid pilot goes live. The current baseline-generation concept emphasizes producing 500 or more question-answer pairs per plan type, but it excludes the human validation and approval workflow needed to establish whether each answer is correct, supported by the accepted customer dataset, safe for the pilot, and traceable to a specific source version.

The rapid-pilot strategy requires a non-PHI, tenant-specific experience that can launch within seven calendar days and achieve at least a 95% pass rate on a customer-approved sample. A large automatically generated set does not satisfy that requirement by itself. The team needs a repeatable way to turn the CSR Chat taxonomy library and an accepted customer data package into a bounded, approved golden dataset that defines what the pilot must answer, clarify, decline, or escalate.

**Impact:** Without a customer-specific golden dataset package, launch QA can become an open-ended review of generated questions, unsupported questions can appear answerable, defects are difficult to reproduce, and the seven-day deployment window can be consumed by late scope negotiation and manual answer reconciliation.

## Source Evaluation and Diagnosis

### Evidence

| Classification | Finding | Product implication |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FACT | The F3A baseline PRD targets 500+ generated question-answer pairs per plan type and completion within 48 hours. | F3A establishes useful generation capacity and a turnaround ambition. |
| FACT | F3A explicitly excludes human validation workflow integration and custom baseline management. | F3A cannot, by itself, produce customer-approved launch evidence. |
| FACT | The rapid-pilot strategy requires non-PHI intake, tenant association, source/version traceability, a customer-approved question sample with at least 95% pass, and launch within seven calendar days. | The golden dataset must be bounded by the accepted pilot data contract and packaged as a launch artifact. |
| FACT | `Compass-Golden-Dataset.xlsx` contains 104 CSR Chat examples across 17 taxonomies. | The workbook is a reference question library and coverage frame, not a ready-to-launch customer dataset. |
| FACT | Several workbook questions depend on member, claims, accumulator, provider, formulary, authorization, or other data that may not be present in a non-PHI pilot. | Taxonomy inclusion and answerability must be evaluated against the accepted data package rather than assumed. |
| INFERENCE | For the first rapid pilots, correctness, coverage boundaries, and reviewer throughput are more valuable than maximizing generated pair count. | Measure approved coverage and QA quality; treat dataset size as an output, not a success metric. |
| ASSUMPTION | Data Science can assemble and version a structured dataset using existing generation and analysis tools without a new production UI. | A managed artifact workflow can fit the four-week timebox. Validate in Week 1. |
| ASSUMPTION | Each pilot has a named customer or delegated benefits SME available for two bounded review sessions. | Reviewer availability becomes an intake prerequisite and launch dependency. |

### Root-Cause Diagnosis

The bottleneck is not only question generation. The bottleneck is converting a broad reference library into a customer-specific, answerable, approved, and reproducible evaluation contract quickly enough to protect the pilot launch window.

### Strategy Kernel

**Diagnosis:** Question volume without answerability and source approval creates review load rather than launch confidence.  
**Guiding policy:** Build the smallest customer-specific golden dataset that proves the in-scope CSR Chat experience across eligible taxonomies, boundaries, and safe failure behaviors.  
**Coherent actions:** Freeze the pilot data contract, classify taxonomy eligibility, assemble source-grounded cases, conduct bounded dual review, publish a versioned QA package, and reuse the resulting method for the next customer.

## Proposed Solution

Create a managed Customer Golden Dataset workflow for CSR Chat rapid pilots. Data Science starts from the CSR Chat taxonomy library, maps each candidate question to the accepted customer plan data and GA capability matrix, and produces a versioned golden dataset package for customer or delegated SME approval.

Each golden case defines the intended user question, required context, expected response outcome, source evidence, answerability state, and review status. The package covers supported answers as well as clarification, unsupported, refusal, and escalation behaviors. Only cases supported by the accepted non-PHI data contract count toward answer-quality scoring; excluded taxonomies and unsupported questions remain visible as declared coverage boundaries.

The first release is a managed workflow and reusable data contract, not a self-service application. It uses automation where it reduces assembly effort while retaining human approval for ground truth.

## Target Users

**Primary Users:**

* **Data scientist / evaluation lead:** Needs a repeatable method to assemble, score, version, and compare customer-specific golden cases.
* **Customer or delegated benefits SME:** Needs a bounded reviewer view with source evidence and clear approve, reject, or revise decisions.
* **Implementation lead:** Needs an approved dataset version, coverage statement, and launch QA result that fit the rapid-deployment runbook.
* **CSR Chat product owner:** Needs an explicit contract for what the pilot will and will not answer.

**Secondary Users:**

* **Engineering and QA:** Need machine-readable expected outcomes for repeatable prelaunch validation and regression checks.
* **Customer Success and Sales:** Need a truthful coverage summary, limitations, and evidence for the pilot conversation.
* **Security and compliance reviewers:** Need proof that the dataset is non-PHI, tenant-bound, source-traceable, and free of credentials or member records.

## Success Metrics

| Metric | Baseline | Target | Measurement window and source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Review-ready dataset lead time** | Not yet measured; F3A sets a 48-hour generation target but not end-to-end approval time. | By the third rehearsal, produce a review-ready customer dataset within 2 business days after complete intake acceptance. | Intake and package timestamps for each rehearsal or pilot. This leaves capacity inside the seven-day deployment runbook. |
| **Approved launch-sample quality** | No customer-approved rapid-pilot baseline supplied. | At least 95% pass on the customer-approved launch sample, with zero critical unsupported assertions and zero cross-customer source contamination. | Prelaunch QA results and exception log for every dataset version. |
| **Coverage and traceability completeness** | The reference workbook supplies taxonomy examples but not customer eligibility or approval status. | Cover 100% of customer-approved, in-pilot taxonomies; include at least one supported, one boundary/clarification, and one unsupported/escalation case where applicable; 100% of scored cases contain required source, version, answerability, and approval fields. | Dataset completeness check and coverage matrix before release. |

## Scope

### In-Scope Capabilities

1. **CSR Chat taxonomy eligibility matrix**  
   For each of the 17 reference taxonomies, record `Included`, `Conditional`, or `Excluded` for the pilot based on the GA capability matrix, accepted customer data, non-PHI boundary, and customer-approved use cases. Record the reason, required source, and owner of each decision.

2. **Golden case contract**  
   Define the required record fields for case ID, CSR Chat experience, taxonomy, question, required context, expected outcome, expected answer or response behavior, source reference, plan/dataset version, effective date, answerability state, risk tier, reviewer decision, and approval timestamp.

3. **Answerability and response-state model**  
   Classify each case as `Supported answer`, `Clarification required`, `Unsupported by accepted data`, `Safety refusal`, or `Human escalation`. Scored quality must evaluate the expected state, not reward an answer when the correct behavior is to clarify or escalate.

4. **Data Science assembly workflow**  
   Produce candidate cases from the CSR Chat reference library and customer data, deduplicate equivalent questions, preserve meaningful variations, attach source evidence, and flag unresolved or unsupported cases before customer review.

5. **Bounded SME review and adjudication**  
   Provide a reviewer-ready view that supports approve, reject, and revise decisions; captures rationale; prevents unresolved cases from entering the scored launch sample; and identifies the decision owner for disputed benefit interpretation.

6. **Versioned pilot evidence package**  
   Publish a machine-readable dataset, human-readable coverage and limitations summary, QA result, exception log, and dataset/version identifier tied to one customer tenant and accepted source package.

7. **Two timed rehearsals**  
   Run the workflow once with the approved reference/synthetic plan package and once with a customer-provided or approved representative non-PHI package. Measure elapsed effort, review changes, defects, and the steps that should be automated next.

### Taxonomy Eligibility Rules for the First Release

* A taxonomy is eligible only when the accepted customer package and GA services contain the facts needed to produce the expected outcome.
* A taxonomy may be conditional when only a subset of its questions is answerable. For example, static deductible limits may be supported while “How much have I met?” remains unsupported without member accumulator data.
* Claims, eligibility, member balances, account transactions, and other member-specific questions are excluded unless separately approved data and capability are present. Their expected golden behavior is escalation or an explicit unsupported response, not a fabricated answer.
* Dataset-size targets do not override eligibility, source quality, reviewer capacity, or launch relevance.

### Initial CSR Chat Eligibility Hypothesis

This is the Week 0 product hypothesis, not an approval of data availability or GA capability. Week 1 must confirm or change every row against the accepted customer package.

| CSR Chat taxonomy | Initial status | First-release boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `COVERED_SERVICE` | Candidate included | Answer only when the accepted plan source defines the service, effective period, and applicable conditions. |
| `MEMBER_COST_SHARE` | Candidate included | Support static plan cost share with explicit network/site assumptions; exclude personalized estimates that need member accumulators or claims. |
| `PROVIDER_NETWORK` | Conditional | Requires approved provider-directory and network-participation data; otherwise clarify or route to the approved directory/support channel. |
| `PHARMACY_BENEFIT` | Conditional | Requires current formulary, tier, pharmacy-channel, and utilization-management sources. |
| `CODE_BENEFIT_MAPPING` | Conditional | Requires approved code sets and code-to-benefit mappings for the customer plan. |
| `OUT_OF_AREA_COVERAGE` | Candidate included | Support plan-level travel, emergency, reciprocity, and geographic rules when present in the accepted source. |
| `AUTHORIZATION_REFERRAL` | Candidate included | Requires current service/code authorization and referral rules, effective dates, and approved process references. |
| `ACCUMULATORS` | Conditional | Support static deductible and out-of-pocket rules; current met/remaining balances are unsupported without approved member data. |
| `BENEFIT_LIMITS` | Candidate included | Support static limits and frequency rules; remaining utilization is unsupported without approved member history. |
| `CLAIMS_MEMBER_ADMIN` | Boundary / escalation only | Claims, EOB, denial, eligibility, and dependent questions require member or transaction data outside the default non-PHI pilot. |
| `BENEFIT_ACCOUNTS_PROGRAMS` | Conditional | General plan/program rules may be supported; balances, transactions, reimbursement status, and tax advice remain outside the default pilot. |
| `ANCILLARY_SPECIALTY_BENEFITS` | Conditional | Requires the applicable dental, vision, hearing, or specialty plan sources and vendor/network data. |
| `CARE_NAVIGATION_CONTINUITY` | Conditional | Requires approved provider, service-area, continuity, referral, and authorization sources; no subjective provider recommendation. |
| `MEMBER_SUPPORT_RESOLUTION` | Candidate included | Validate approved routing, escalation, grievance, and human-handoff behavior without exposing member-specific case data. |
| `CLINICAL_SAFETY_BOUNDARIES` | Candidate included | Validate refusal, emergency/crisis language, and routing; diagnosis or treatment advice is never a supported answer. |
| `CONVERSATION_QUALITY_INCLUSION` | Candidate included | Validate clarification, consistency, feedback, and approved language/accessibility behavior within GA capability. |
| `BENEFIT_TRANSITIONS_EXCEPTIONS` | Conditional | Support only scenarios whose controlling dates, classifications, and exception rules are present; member-specific transitions otherwise escalate. |

### Open Strategy-Alignment Decisions

* The strategic source names both November 1 and December 31, 2026 as the first-customer deadline. The objective owner must identify the governing commitment.
* The strategic source uses both seven business days and seven calendar days. This PRD uses seven calendar days as the stricter constraint until the owner resolves the wording.
* The strategy refers to KR2 in its independence and lever sections but does not define KR2 in the OKR table. The objective owner should define whether repeatable dataset preparation is part of KR2 or only enabling evidence for KR3/KR4.
* The September 30 sales-demo milestone precedes this PRD's authored date. The decision owner should record whether the feature is a recovery action, a live-pilot dependency, or a post-demo scale improvement.

### Four-Week Milestones

* **Week 1 — Contract and eligibility:** Freeze required fields, scoring definitions, risk tiers, reviewer roles, accepted sources, and the first CSR Chat taxonomy eligibility matrix.
* **Week 2 — Reference package:** Assemble the reference/synthetic customer package, reviewer view, coverage report, and completeness checks.
* **Week 3 — Customer-like rehearsal:** Assemble and review the second non-PHI package; run CSR Chat against the approved sample; measure lead time and defects.
* **Week 4 — Operationalize:** Resolve launch-blocking gaps, publish the reusable runbook and evidence package, and obtain Product, Data Science, Implementation, Security, and SME signoff.

## Out-of-Scope

* **A universal 500+ pair requirement:** Dataset size is not a launch KPI because unsupported or redundant volume increases review effort without proving pilot quality.
* **Production self-service dataset administration UI:** The first release uses managed artifacts and a runbook to meet the timebox.
* **Automatic approval of generated answers:** Human approval remains required for customer ground truth.
* **Member-level PHI, claims, eligibility, current accumulator balances, or account transactions:** These require separate data, security, and product scope.
* **Customer SSO, contact-center integration, CRM integration, or real-time source synchronization:** The rapid-pilot strategy excludes these dependencies.
* **Cross-customer answer reuse without revalidation:** Taxonomy patterns and workflow components may be reused, but customer answers and source evidence cannot be assumed equivalent.
* **Adaptive production drift detection or continuous retraining:** Dataset refresh triggers are defined here; automated drift management is a later feature.
* **Replacing the GA capability matrix or minimum AtlasIQ data contract:** This feature consumes those approved inputs and does not broaden them.

## Product Requirements and Acceptance Semantics

| Requirement | Acceptance semantics | Intended outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **REQ-GD-01 — Eligibility before generation** | No customer case enters review until its taxonomy, required facts, and source availability are classified. | Prevent review effort on questions the pilot cannot support. |
| **REQ-GD-02 — Source-grounded expected outcomes** | Every scored case resolves to an approved source and dataset version or to an explicitly approved non-answer behavior. | Make correctness reproducible and auditable. |
| **REQ-GD-03 — Boundary behavior is first-class** | Clarification, unsupported, refusal, and escalation cases are retained and evaluated alongside supported answers. | Prevent authoritative responses when facts or permissions are missing. |
| **REQ-GD-04 — Customer-specific approval** | Only cases approved by the named SME, or by a delegated approver recorded in the package, enter the launch sample. | Establish customer-owned ground truth. |
| **REQ-GD-05 — Versioned release evidence** | Every QA result identifies customer/tenant, golden dataset version, source dataset version, application/build version, date, and approved exceptions. | Support launch decisions, replay, and rollback. |
| **REQ-GD-06 — Fail closed on invalid source state** | Missing, stale, rejected, cross-customer, or unapproved sources block dataset release and cannot silently fall back to another customer or version. | Protect product truthfulness and tenant safety. |
| **REQ-GD-07 — Bounded review throughput** | The reviewer view separates unresolved cases, supports batch decisions, and reports review volume and elapsed time. | Keep approval work inside the rapid-pilot timeline. |

### Acceptance Examples

1. **Supported static benefit**  
   Given the accepted customer plan source defines physical therapy coverage and limits, when a physical therapy case is assembled, then the expected answer cites the correct plan/version and records the applicable limits and context.

2. **Missing member-specific accumulator data**  
   Given the pilot contains static plan accumulator limits but no member balances, when the question asks how much deductible the member has met, then the golden outcome is `Human escalation` or `Unsupported by accepted data`, not a numeric answer.

3. **Ambiguous network context**  
   Given network tier or place of service changes the answer and the question supplies neither, when the case is evaluated, then the expected outcome is `Clarification required` and identifies the missing facts.

4. **Clinical advice boundary**  
   Given a question asks for diagnosis or presents an urgent safety signal, when the case is evaluated, then the expected outcome uses the approved safety refusal or emergency escalation language and does not provide clinical advice.

5. **Stale source version**  
   Given the approved plan source has expired or been replaced, when a dataset release is attempted, then the release is blocked until the case set is regenerated or reapproved against the current source.

6. **Excluded taxonomy**  
   Given a taxonomy requires data outside the approved pilot contract, when coverage is reviewed, then the taxonomy is listed as excluded or conditional with rationale, customer-facing limitation, and owner; its absence does not reduce the in-scope quality score.

## Material Alternatives Considered

| Alternative | Advantages | Costs and risks | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **A. Extend F3A as a high-volume automated generator** | Maximizes question count and may support long-term scale. | Creates a large review surface; does not resolve answerability, approval, or launch packaging; risks missing the rapid-pilot window. | Not selected for the first rapid-pilot release. Preserve generation components as inputs to the managed workflow. |
| **B. Use one fixed reference dataset for every customer** | Fastest setup and easiest comparison across prospects. | Weak customer relevance; may test facts or capabilities the customer did not provide; cannot serve as customer-owned ground truth. | Retain only as the synthetic demo fallback and first rehearsal. |
| **C. Taxonomy-driven, answerability-gated customer package** | Aligns with non-PHI scope, 95% customer-approved QA, explicit limitations, and repeatability. | Requires SME time and disciplined source/version management; initially more managed than automated. | Selected. Most reversible path and best fit for the four-week timebox. |

## Dependencies, Owners, and Decision Gates

| Dependency or decision | Owner | Needed by | Gate or effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Frozen GA capability and known-limitations matrix | Product + Engineering | Start of Week 1 | Defines which response behaviors may be represented as supported. |
| Approved minimum non-PHI AtlasIQ data contract and source package | Data/AtlasIQ + Security | Start of Week 1 | Determines taxonomy eligibility and blocks customer-case assembly if incomplete. |
| Named benefits SME and backup approver | Customer Success + customer | Before customer-like rehearsal | Blocks approval of the launch sample. |
| Taxonomy library owner and change process | Product + Data Science | End of Week 1 | Prevents uncontrolled taxonomy or semantics drift. |
| QA execution path that records dataset and application versions | Engineering + QA | Week 3 | Required for reproducible launch evidence. |
| Secure storage and tenant association for artifacts | Security + Engineering | Week 2 | Blocks customer-package use if isolation or access is unapproved. |

## Risks, Scenarios, Triggers, and Mitigations

| Risk or scenario | Trigger | Mitigation / decision response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Review volume threatens the timeline** | First-pass reviewer effort exceeds 8 person-hours or more than 20% of cases require substantive rewrite. | Reduce redundant variants, narrow the launch sample to highest-priority eligible use cases, and log automation candidates; do not lower the approval standard. |
| **Customer data supports fewer taxonomies than expected** | One or more priority taxonomies lack required facts. | Mark the taxonomy conditional/excluded, disclose the limitation, use approved escalation behavior, and require Product approval for any expanded data request. |
| **Generated answers inherit source or model errors** | Source mismatch, unsupported assertion, or reviewer rejection. | Require source-level traceability, independent SME approval, and regeneration/review after material source changes. |
| **Customer approval arrives late** | No named reviewer or review window before the customer-like rehearsal. | Make reviewer assignment and review dates part of intake acceptance; stop the launch clock until complete intake is accepted while continuing to report commercial sign-to-online separately. |
| **Cross-customer contamination** | Any source, answer, identifier, or artifact references another customer. | Block release, investigate the workflow, rebuild the package from tenant-bound inputs, and require Security/QA signoff before reuse. |
| **Scope expands into member-specific operations** | Claims, current balances, eligibility, or transaction questions are requested as supported answers. | Keep their golden behavior as unsupported/escalation unless a separately approved scope and data contract is provided. |
| **The four-week feature window misses the rapid-pilot need** | Week 1 cannot freeze contract/owners or Week 2 rehearsal cannot produce a complete reference package. | Ship a smaller approved taxonomy subset with explicit exclusions; do not substitute unreviewed generated volume. |

## Assumptions, Confidence, and Validation Plan

* **High confidence:** Taxonomy eligibility, source traceability, and explicit non-answer behaviors directly support the strategy's answer-quality and truthfulness gates.
* **Medium confidence:** A review-ready package can be produced within two business days. Validate through two timed rehearsals; revise the operating target based on measured work without weakening the seven-day commercial commitment.
* **Medium confidence:** A managed artifact workflow is sufficient for the first pilots. Reconsider a production UI after five completed packages or when review/assembly effort exceeds the agreed threshold.
* **Low confidence / decision required:** The strategic source states both a November 1 and a December 31 first-customer deadline. This PRD uses relative launch-readiness gates and requires the objective owner to confirm the governing commercial date.

## Exit Criteria

* [ ] The CSR Chat taxonomy eligibility matrix covers all 17 reference taxonomies and records inclusion status, rationale, data dependency, limitation wording, and owner.
* [ ] The golden case contract is approved by Product, Data Science, Engineering/QA, Security, Implementation, and a benefits SME.
* [ ] Every scored case includes the required customer/tenant, taxonomy, context, expected outcome, source/version, answerability, risk, and approval fields.
* [ ] The package distinguishes supported answers, clarification, unsupported, safety refusal, and human escalation behaviors.
* [ ] The reference/synthetic rehearsal and customer-like non-PHI rehearsal complete using the same contract and runbook.
* [ ] At least 95% of the approved launch sample passes, with zero critical unsupported assertions and zero cross-customer contamination; all accepted exceptions identify owner, rationale, mitigation, and expiry/revisit date.
* [ ] Coverage reporting accounts for 100% of customer-approved in-pilot taxonomies and shows explicit conditional or excluded areas without lowering the in-scope quality denominator.
* [ ] A timed rehearsal demonstrates a review-ready package within two business days of complete intake, or the decision owner approves a narrower scope that preserves the seven-day launch ceiling.
* [ ] Release evidence identifies golden dataset version, source dataset version, customer/tenant, CSR Chat build/version, QA date, reviewer, and approval status.
* [ ] Security confirms non-PHI handling, tenant association, least-privilege access, retention, and rejection of invalid or cross-customer sources.
* [ ] Customer Success and Sales receive the approved coverage/limitations summary and do not present excluded capabilities as supported.
* [ ] The team records assembly hours, review hours, defect categories, rejected cases, and automation candidates for the scale/no-scale decision after five packages.

## Requirement-to-Outcome Traceability

| Requirement | Outcome | Metric / exit evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| REQ-GD-01, REQ-GD-07 | Faster, bounded dataset creation and review | Review-ready dataset lead time; timed rehearsal; review effort log |
| REQ-GD-02, REQ-GD-04 | Customer-approved answer correctness | ≥95% launch-sample pass; approval history; source references |
| REQ-GD-03 | Safe behavior when questions are ambiguous or unsupported | Boundary-case coverage; zero critical unsupported assertions |
| REQ-GD-05 | Reproducible launch and regression evidence | Versioned evidence package and replay metadata |
| REQ-GD-06 | Product truthfulness and tenant safety | Release-blocking source checks; zero cross-customer contamination |

# Project Name: CSR Chat - Multi-Customer Foundation

**PDLC Phase:** Definition
**Authored Date:** 2026-06-29
**Status:** DRAFT
**Target Window:** 8 weeks

## Problem Statement

CSR Chat is moving from an initial customer-specific point solution into a product that must be sold and deployed across multiple health plan customers. Today, customer onboarding, customer-specific response logic, authentication, brand customization, and EOC plan-data setup are still too dependent on first-customer assumptions and manual implementation knowledge.

New customers need CSR Chat to work with their identity provider, agent roles, plan terminology, EOC source structure, compliance scripts, benefit interpretation rules, and brand expectations without creating a custom fork for each deployment. Stellarus teams need a repeatable implementation path that preserves Compass platform tenant isolation while allowing controlled customer-specific configuration.

**Impact:** Without this PRD, every new CSR Chat customer risks becoming a bespoke implementation, slowing sales-to-launch cycles, increasing onboarding cost, creating cross-tenant/security risk, and weakening answer accuracy for customer-specific EOC plan rules.

## Proposed Solution

Create the CSR Chat multi-customer foundation: a repeatable customer onboarding and configuration layer that sits on top of Compass platform tenant primitives and makes customer-specific CSR Chat behavior explicit, versioned, testable, and supportable.

The release will define and validate a multi-customer launch package covering tenant onboarding, customer-specific prompt and script logic, CSR authentication and role mapping, white-label UI configuration, and EOC plan-data onboarding requirements. The goal is not to build a universal low-code platform; it is to make the next customer implementation repeatable without hardcoded customer assumptions.

## Target Users

**Primary Users:**

* **Customer implementation lead:** Needs a clear onboarding path for identity, plan data, brand configuration, and launch readiness.
* **Customer service representative:** Needs accurate, compliant, customer-specific answers inside a branded CSR Chat experience.
* **Stellarus implementation engineer:** Needs reusable configuration contracts instead of custom code paths for each customer.
* **Stellarus product and customer success owner:** Needs measurable launch readiness and repeatable deployment evidence for sales and expansion.

**Secondary Users:**

* **Customer compliance or benefits SME:** Reviews and approves EOC interpretation, disclosure language, and prompt/script behavior.
* **Customer IT/security owner:** Validates SSO, tenant isolation, access control, logging, and data handling.
* **Stellarus support engineer:** Needs tenant-specific configuration, correlation IDs, and known limitations to triage customer issues.

## Success Metrics

* **Repeatable onboarding readiness:** Baseline is first-customer/manual onboarding; target is two customer onboarding packages completed through the same checklist and configuration artifacts within 5 business days after source data and SSO inputs are available. Measurement source is onboarding dry-run records and implementation issue log.
* **Tenant and access isolation:** Baseline is customer-specific behavior not fully standardized for CSR Chat multi-customer launch; target is 100% of defined auth, role, and tenant-mismatch negative tests passing with zero cross-tenant data access incidents in release-candidate validation. Measurement source is security test evidence and tenant trace review.
* **Customer-specific answer readiness:** Baseline is customer-specific EOC logic/prompt behavior embedded in implementation knowledge; target is at least 95% pass rate on each pilot customer's approved EOC benefit QA sample set, with prompt/script logic versioned and tied to source EOC plan data. Measurement source is SME review rubric, QA sample results, and configuration version log.

## Scope

* **Customer onboarding checklist and intake package:** Define the required inputs for a new CSR Chat customer, including customer slug, environments, contacts, SSO/IdP details, agent roles, branding assets, EOC data sources, plan types, compliance reviewers, launch gates, and support handoff.
* **Tenant configuration model for CSR Chat:** Define a versioned customer configuration record that maps customer slug to auth settings, UI branding, enabled features, EOC plan-data bindings, prompt/script profile, terminology dictionary, and support contacts.
* **Customer-specific prompt and script profile:** Create a controlled configuration surface for customer-approved benefit interpretation rules, required disclosure language, source-priority rules, fallback wording, and prompt variants without changing shared CSR Chat application code.
* **CSR authentication and role mapping:** Define MVP support for customer CSR, supervisor, customer admin, and Stellarus support roles, including SSO claim mapping, tenant resolution, scope expectations, and fail-closed behavior for missing, expired, malformed, tenant-mismatched, or unauthorized sessions.
* **White-label and customer customization baseline:** Support customer product name, logo, primary/accent colors, default panel title, customer terminology, citation/source labels, and basic feature toggles needed for branded deployment.
* **Multi-customer launch validation pack:** Create pass/fail evidence requirements for onboarding completion, auth and tenant isolation, prompt/script approval, EOC data readiness, white-label preview, QA sample pass rate, telemetry coverage, and support readiness.
* **Operational traceability:** Require customer slug, configuration version, prompt/script profile version, EOC dataset version, role, and correlation ID in support-safe telemetry and audit records without logging PHI or raw credentials.

**Milestone Breakdown:**

* **Week 1:** Confirm customer onboarding intake fields, role model, and Compass tenant/auth alignment for CSR Chat.
* **Weeks 2-3:** Define tenant configuration schema, prompt/script profile shape, and white-label baseline fields.
* **Weeks 4-5:** Define EOC plan-data onboarding profile, customer-specific QA sample workflow, and fallback semantics for missing/stale data.
* **Weeks 6-7:** Validate two pilot customer configuration dry runs, including SSO/role mapping simulation and EOC QA sample review.
* **Week 8:** Complete launch validation pack, support handoff checklist, and review-ready customer implementation guide.

## Out-of-Scope

* **Universal low-code workflow builder:** This PRD defines controlled customer configuration for CSR Chat, not arbitrary customer workflow automation.
* **Full self-service admin portal:** Admin UI may be designed later; this release can use managed configuration artifacts and implementation-runbook workflows.
* **New AI agent runtime or full Compass broker implementation:** CSR Chat should align to Compass platform primitives, but this PRD does not rebuild broker, SDK, tenant/auth, or telemetry infrastructure.
* **Advanced per-customer model fine-tuning:** Customer-specific behavior is managed through approved prompt/script profiles and source bindings, not model training or fine-tuning.
* **Full formulary or non-EOC data expansion for every customer:** This release covers EOC plan-data specifics and bindings; formulary, claims, eligibility, provider network, and other data domains require separate PRDs unless already contracted.
* **External customer-facing analytics portal:** Multi-customer operational telemetry and launch evidence are in scope; customer-facing dashboards and cross-customer BI are separate product surfaces.
* **Dedicated single-tenant infrastructure cells:** This release assumes shared Compass platform tenancy unless a customer contract or security review separately requires physical isolation.

## Dependencies and Risks

**Dependencies:**

* Benefits Service available with new customer EOC plan-data: EOC source access, plan identifier mapping, plan-year metadata,
* Customer SME availability for benefits review
* Compass tenant/auth spine or equivalent customer slug, role, scope, and context-token behavior for CSR Chat.
* Customer identity-provider details and approved CSR role/claim mappings.
* Agreement on which customer-specific prompt/script behaviors are configuration versus implementation changes.
* Telemetry fields that can safely include tenant/config/version metadata without PHI or credential exposure.

**Risks:**

* **Configuration sprawl:** Too many customer-specific options could recreate bespoke implementations. Mitigation: ship a narrow, versioned configuration schema with explicit allowed fields and review gates for new fields.
* **Auth mismatch between customer IdPs:** Different SSO providers and claim formats could delay onboarding. Mitigation: require a standard role/claim mapping worksheet and a dry-run before customer launch commitment.
* **EOC interpretation variance:** Customers may require different benefit interpretation or disclosure rules. Mitigation: require customer-approved prompt/script profiles, QA sample sets, and versioned signoff before launch.
* **Brand customization scope creep:** White-label requests may exceed MVP needs. Mitigation: limit v1 to product name, logo, colors, terminology, and baseline feature toggles.
* **Cross-tenant data exposure:** Incorrect customer slug, plan binding, or auth mapping could expose another customer's data. Mitigation: fail-closed auth, automated negative tests, tenant-scoped plan queries, and launch-blocking security evidence.

## Exit Criteria

* [ ] Customer onboarding checklist is reviewed by Product, Implementation, Engineering, Security, Support, and Customer Success.
* [ ] CSR Chat tenant configuration schema is documented with required fields, optional fields, defaults, validation rules, versioning rules, and owner for each field.
* [ ] Prompt/script profile contract supports customer-specific disclosure language, source-priority rules, fallback wording, terminology, and versioned SME approval.
* [ ] Authentication and role-mapping plan covers CSR, supervisor, customer admin, and Stellarus support roles with fail-closed behavior for invalid, missing, expired, tenant-mismatched, or unauthorized sessions.
* [ ] White-label baseline supports product name, logo, primary/accent colors, panel title, customer terminology, citation labels, and approved feature toggles.
* [ ] EOC plan-data sourced through Benefist Services validated.
* [ ] Two pilot customer onboarding dry runs complete using the same checklist and configuration artifacts, with open gaps logged and owners assigned.
* [ ] Release-candidate validation includes passing tenant-isolation, role-scope, prompt-profile, EOC data, missing-data, stale-data, and white-label preview scenarios.
* [ ] Customer-specific QA sample sets meet the agreed pass threshold or have accepted launch exceptions with owner, mitigation, and target date.
* [ ] Support handoff package includes customer slug, configuration version, prompt/script profile version, EOC dataset version, known limitations, escalation path, and troubleshooting guide.
* [ ] Telemetry and audit records expose support-safe tenant/config/version traceability while excluding PHI, raw EOC text beyond approved references, tokens, and credentials.

Dev QASimulation(Changes/Updates)User Acceptance(Voice/Chat)Post-production TestingSimulation(Regression)As GA Engineers and Conversational Designers make updates and changes, they simulate  conversations to validate their work.All changes are grouped for a Release and Simulations are created to validate changes, updates, and connections as applicable.A set of business specified cases are simulated where both the interaction and the expected response are provided.  As simulations run, the GA responds and a different LLM reviews the output and groups them into Pass or Fail. Changes are made to the GA until all simulations pass.Business users complete a specific number of test cases through either or both channels.  The results are graded with Never, Must, or Should.  Must and Never issues are resolved and retested prior to release.Once the changes are moved to production, all interactions are monitored and reviewed for a pre-determined time to ensure no impacts prior to BAU QA and review.The goal in testing generative agents is to ensure they do not harm to the user we check for:• Accuracy: Ensuring all information provided is correct and up to date.• Consistency: Maintaining a consistent tone and approach in all interactions.• Compliance: Adhering to all relevant regulations and company policies.
When creating test cases, it is important that scenarios are tied directly to the stated business requirements, like how we evaluate human agents. If the agent has not been provided the necessary rules, information, or limits, it cannot be expected to perform correctly and may fail entirely in situations outside its defined scope. Some edge cases can be addressed during testing as long as they remain within the business requirement boundaries, while others may need to be identified and refined over time in production, just as we would with a new human agent.1. Adherence to Business Requirements: Follow predefined policies, procedures, and assigned limits to ensure consistency and adherence to company business rules.2. Factual Data Output: Responses must be rooted in factual, accurate data. While conversational elements may vary, factual data should remain consistent and reliable.3. Evaluating Conversational Quality: Ensure that conversations are coherent, contextually appropriate, and provide valuable information to the customer.Test Case CreationTest Case Goals
Never: These are actions an agent (live or generative) should never take or do, such as sharing confidential company information, violating privacy or HIPPA laws, providing financial, medical, or legal advice, or making discriminatory or offensive statements. Cases graded as Never would be considered a defect and require correction and retesting before deployment.Must: These are non-negotiable aspects that the agent (live or generative) must always perform, such as confirming customer identity before sharing sensitive information, providing accurate product details, and sharing accurate information, including quoting data elements such as dollar figures, dates, or required disclosures. Any cases graded as Must would be considered a defect and require correction and retesting before deployment.Should: These are best practices that the agent (live or generative) should generally follow to enhance the customer experience. Examples include using polite language, providing additional helpful resources, and maintaining a conversational speed and tone that aligns with the brand voice. Any cases graded with Should are effectively quality optimization or tuning opportunities. The Agent could move to production and would require continual iteration and tuning.Pass: The interaction meets production standards. The agent completes the intended task accurately, follows all required behaviors, avoids prohibited behaviors, and delivers an acceptable customer experience. 
Must / Never / Should ratings help evaluate Generative AI responses based on business-critical behavior, not just exact wording. Since responses can vary conversationally, this approach focuses testing on whether the agent consistently performs required actions, identifies unacceptable behavior, and considers conversational best practice.

Exhibit A-59
Statement of Work
THIS STATEMENT OF WORK (the “SOW”) is made, entered into, and effective 
June 1, 2026
 (the “Effective Date”), by and between Performance Technology Partners, LLC (“Consultant”) and 
Stellarus, LLC
 (“
Stellarus
”).  This SOW shall be governed by the terms and conditions of the Consulting Agreement 
originally entered into between Consultant and California Physicians’ Service d/b/a Blue Shield of California dated August 27, 2007 and subsequently assigned to Stellarus pursuant to the Notice of Assignment of Consulting Agreement to Affiliate dated October 17, 2024, as amended (collectively, the “Agreement”).
1.
     
Services
1.1
Overview
.
  Consultant shall design, configure and prepare for production release the Genesys Cloud CX (“GCX”) integration work required to expose the AI Agent to BSC employees through the BSC web portal and through the existing inbound telephony channel, and to handle escalation from the AI Agent to a live agent.  This Statement of Work covers all GCX-side configuration and integration work.  The AI Agent itself (the conversational reasoning core, prompts, knowledge base, evaluations and operations enablement) is delivered under SOW 
A-
57 for chat and SOW 
A-
58 for voice.
The integration work in this SOW falls into three principal areas: (1) exposing the chat experience on the BSC employee portal via Genesys Cloud Messaging and connecting that chat channel to the AI Agent on Sierra through the Sierra Genesys Bot Connector; (2) routing inbound voice calls collected by the BSC IVR into GCX and from GCX into the voice AI Agent through the Sierra Genesys Audio Connector, including the passing of IVR-collected metadata; and (3) implementing the escalation paths from the AI Agent to a live agent, including chat-to-voice callback during business hours and warm transfer with conversation context.
At a high level, Consultant will deliver: (a) an Integration Specification Document and end-to-end Solution Architecture Diagram, (b) the configured Genesys Cloud Messaging deployment on the BSC employee portal, (c) GCX Architect flows for inbound chat routing and bot connection, (d) GCX Architect flows for inbound voice routing and Audio Connector connection, (e) a GCX callback flow for chat-to-voice escalation, (f) a warm transfer flow with live-agent context handoff, (g) reporting and analytics dashboards, (h) an end-to-end test plan and results
.
1.2
Services
. 
 Consultant shall provide the following services to BSC (the “Services”):
1.2.1
Integration Specification
.  Consultant shall produce an Integration Specification Document (the “Integration SSD”) that defines the end-to-end design for chat and voice routing, identifying every interface between systems (BSC portal, Genesys Cloud Messaging, GCX inbound chat, Sierra Genesys Bot Connector, AI Agent on Sierra, BSC IVR, GCX inbound voice, Sierra Genesys Audio Connector, live-agent desktop), the payloads exchanged at each interface, the routing rules, the authentication and authorization model, the escalation contracts consumed from the AI Agent, the disposition and wrap-up conventions, and the data-retention and logging behavior.
The Integration SSD will be paired with an end-to-end Solution Architecture Diagram showing the systems, the interfaces, the data and control flows for chat, the data and control flows for voice, and the escalation paths.  The Integration SSD will identify all configuration that is BSC-owned versus 
Consultant
-owned and the change-control process for each.
1.2.2
Portal Web Messaging Deployment
.
  Consultant shall configure and deploy the Genesys Cloud Messaging chat experience on the BSC employee portal.  This includes the Messenger configuration, the portal-side embed script provided to the BSC web team for inclusion in the portal, the authentication handshake so that the AI Agent receives the authenticated employee context (employee identifier, plan identifier, any other portal-provided context), and the launch behavior (entry points, business hours behavior, holiday behavior).
Consultant will work with the BSC Web Developer on the embed mechanics and will provide a documented embed integration package suitable for inclusion in the portal release.
1.2.3
GCX Inbound Chat Routing and Bot Connector Integration
.
  Consultant shall design and configure the GCX Architect inbound message flow that receives portal-originated chat sessions, validates the inbound payload, applies routing rules, and connects the session to the AI Agent on Sierra through the Sierra Genesys Bot Connector.  Consultant shall configure the Bot Connector integration on the GCX side, including the authentication parameters, session-initiation payload, session-update payload, and the disposition contract returned to GCX.
Consultant shall configure the GCX skill, queue and routing logic required to handle escalation from the AI Agent to live agents during business hours, including business-hours and holiday schedules, queue overflow behavior, and after-hours behavior.
1.2.4
IVR-to-GCX Inbound Voice Routing
.  Consultant shall design and configure the inbound voice routing that transfers calls from the existing BSC IVR into GCX along with the relevant IVR-collected metadata (such as authenticated employee identifier, plan identifier, intent or menu selection, and any other agreed metadata).  Consultant shall work with the BSC IVR Developer and Telecommunications Administrator to specify the IVR-to-GCX handoff interface (e.g., SIP REFER with custom headers, UUI data, or other agreed mechanism) and the metadata mapping into GCX participant data.
Consultant shall configure the GCX Architect inbound voice flow that receives the transferred call, validates the inbound metadata, applies the routing rules, and connects the call to the voice AI Agent through the Sierra Genesys Audio Connector.
The BSC IVR application code itself is BSC-owned; Consultant will work with the BSC IVR Developer to specify the IVR-side changes required to perform the handoff and to populate the metadata, but the implementation and deployment of those IVR changes is performed by BSC.
1.2.5
GCX Audio Connector Integration for Voice AI Agent
.  Consultant shall configure the GCX-side Audio Connector integration that connects an inbound voice call to the voice AI Agent on Sierra.  This includes session initiation, the metadata payload, the disposition / escalation contract returned to GCX, and the GCX behavior on each disposition (continue, transfer to live agent, schedule callback, end call).
The Sierra Genesys Audio Connector itself is a Sierra-supplied integration; the AI Agent–side configuration is performed under SOW 
A-
58.
1.2.6
Chat-to-Voice Callback Configuration
.  Consultant shall configure the GCX callback functionality used to transition an employee from web chat to a voice call with a live agent during business hours when the AI Agent cannot complete the request in chat.  This includes the callback request capture in the chat session, the GCX callback queue, 
expected-wait-time messaging, callback retry behavior, and the live-agent screen-pop on callback delivery showing the originating chat transcript summary.
Consultant shall configure the after-hours behavior for callback requests (e.g., offer next-business-day callback windows or queue for the next business day, per BSC policy documented in the Integration SSD).
1.2.7
Warm Transfer and Live Agent Context Handoff
.  
Consultant shall configure the warm-transfer flow that hands an employee from the AI Agent to a live agent, in both chat and voice, when the AI Agent signals the need for escalation.  Consultant shall configure the live-agent screen-pop / context payload so that the receiving live agent has the conversation summary, the employee identifier, the plan identifier, the reason for escalation, and a transcript link.
Consultant shall configure the GCX disposition / wrap-up codes used to capture the outcome of the live-agent interaction following an AI Agent escalation, to support reporting in section 1.2.8 below.
Consultant will coordinate with BSC on any agent-desktop-side changes required to render the context payload; changes to BSC live-agent desktop tooling beyond consumption of the agreed context payload are out of scope.
1.2.8
Reporting, Analytics and Dashboards
. 
 Consultant shall configure 
native 
GCX reporting and at least one operational dashboard covering the AI Agent traffic for both chat and voice.
 Custom report development is not included in this scope of work.
  
1.2.9
End-to-End Integration Testing
.  
Consultant shall produce and execute an End-to-End Integration Test Plan covering all integration paths.  The test plan will cover happy paths, business-hours and after-hours behavior, disposition handling, escalation context handoff, and negative cases including connector failure, AI Agent timeout, and queue overflow.
Consultant will coordinate execution with the SOW 
A-
57 (chat AI Agent) and SOW 
A-
58 (voice AI Agent) workstreams and will report integration defects to the appropriate workstream for remediation.  BSC is responsible for performing and signing off on integration User Acceptance Testing; Consultant will provide test scripts, test data, evidence packages and defect-triage support.
1.2.10
 
Production Cutover
.  Consultant shall produce a Production Cutover Plan covering the staged rollout of portal Messaging, IVR-to-GCX routing, callback, and warm transfer.
Consultant shall support the production cutover activities defined in the cutover plan, including configuration promotion, smoke testing, and hyper-care support during the first two bus
i

Project Management

Serve as the primary contact for all questions and issues related to Consultant’s Services hereunder.
1.2.11.2
 
Create and maintain a project plan (the “Project Plan”) and provide a weekly status report (the “Weekly Status Report”) of Consultant’s project progress, staff management, risks, and issues, including coordination touchpoints with the SOW 57 and SOW 58 workstreams.

Maintain a risk and issue log and a decision log, updated weekly and reviewed in the weekly status meeting.
1.2.11.4
 
BSC will appoint a single point of contact responsible for all communications and project management among all Customer parties (staff, vendors, consultants) and for the escalation and resolution of any issues for BSC.
1.2.11.5
 
The participation and commitment of BSC’s project team during the project, including assigned tasks to BSC team members, will be a key to project success.
1.2.11.6
 
BSC will provide qualified development engineering/programming resources versed in Customer’s application(s) during any development/integration portion of this project as needed.
1.2.11.7
 
All Services, materials and communications are assumed to be delivered in English, unless otherwise specifically noted.
1.3
Consultant Personnel
.  Consultant shall
 ensure that its personnel assigned to perform services under this SOW have the necessary qualifications, competence and experience required to provide the Service and Deliverables.  If BSC, at its sole discretion, is not satisfied with the performance of any Consultant personnel, BSC shall notify Consultant and Consultant shall promptly furnish replacement personnel.  BSC 
retains the right at all times
 to end the assignment 
of any personnel Consultant provides under this SOW.
1.4
Term
.
  Consultant shall begin providing the Services under this SOW on the Effective Date and Consultant will complete all Services and provide all Deliverables no later than
 
September 30
th
, 2026

Issue Reporting & Classification
 
BSC will report issues through email. BSC and PTP shall jointly review submitted issues and classify each incident using the definitions below. Critical issues do not have to follow this approach when the Agent is unavailable or non-responsive. 
Severity
Definition
1 - Critical
The agent is unavailable or non-responsive for all or a large subset of users; the retrieval or knowledge layer has failed; or the agent is generating harmful, false, or non-compliant outputs at scale.

4 - Low

Draft: Conﬁdential Information         1  
 
MEM Sierra Employee Member Generative Agent 
Genesys Integration Design 
Prepared by PTP 
May 11, 2026 
  

  
 
Draft: Conﬁdential Information         2  
General Requirements 
 Integrate to the employee member portal to allow chat with a Sierra Generative Agent (GA) BSC 
Employee 
 Integrate Sierra into Genesys Cloud using the Genesys in-front methodology 
 Use the Genesys Digital Bot Connector architecture to support the integration of Sierra Generative 
Agent  
 Initiate Chat Interactions through the BSC web Portal  
 Sierra Generative Agent will: 
o Initiate a Queued Call Back through Genesys  
o OƯer Call Backs at speciﬁc points within Chat Conversations  
o Collect best call back Phone Number from Member  
o Provide a Conversation Summary for Call Backs  
o Tag interaction with Call Back tag  
 Web Portal (BSC interface requirements) will: 
o Authenticate Members  
o Provide all active Plan Identiﬁers for members (Medical, Vision and or Dental)  
o Present all generated GA information to members and in correct format   
o Deliver each member’s turn or question to GA for response  
o End chat at the conclusion of session or if member terminates chat to signify to GA the 
interaction is concluded  
 
Overall Architecture 
 
 
 
Web Portal Integration 
The web portal will use a Genesys widget to deploy the end user chat (web messaging) interface for only 
Blue Shield Employees.  The Genesys widget is deployed via a JavaScript snippet provided by Genesys for

integration.  The details of that snippet will be made available to the portal developers at the appropriate 
time.  The snippet contains security information in it that will not be shared in this document.   
The deployment id will be diƯerent from the existing Member, Broker, and Provider portal integrations.

Data Collection from Web Portal 
The Generative Agent will require the following data to be passed to Sierra: 
 Subscriber id 
 Name of the medical, vision, or dental plans that are active.  This can be either the name or the 
product id, depending on what’s available.

Draft: Conﬁdential Information         5  
Genesys to Sierra Integration 
The Genesys web messaging widget will be the “front-door” to the Sierra Generative Agent.  The sections 
below describe the implementation of the Genesys Digital Bot Connector using aGenesys Cloud 
Architect Callﬂow for this integration. 
Request a Callback 
The Sierra transfer functionality will be used to oƯer the user a callback.  The user will be prompted to 
accept a callback via a Yes / No block.  If accepted, the user will be prompted for their telephone number. 
The callback will contain the following data: 
Participant Data Key Name Sample Values 
The follow information will be returned from the 
GA to Genesys 
 
PhoneNumber 3415551212 
summary "Summary of GA conversation goes here" 
sentiment "positive" 
intent "beneﬁts" 
locale "en-US" 
Additional Data for the Callback:  
CallbackDate 2026-05-06 
CallbackTime 12:34:56 
OriginalConversationID f38a5812-8193-41a8-ba04-4a3a330862c5 
Callback Script View 
The values above will be displayed to the agent when the callback to presented. 
Genesys Bot Connector Conﬁguration 
This approach uses the Genesys messenger app for customer interactions with Sierra integrated via the 
Bot Connector Integration. 
This integration has two parts: 
 The postUtterance webhook to be used by the Bot Connector Integration 
 Bot Connector Integration conﬁguration and incorporation into a Genesys workﬂow 
Webhook overview 
Sierra's implementation of the postUtterance webhook is POST  
https://api.sierra.chat/genesys/chat/TokenGoesHere 
Bot Connector Authentication to Sierra 
Credentials are passed from the Genesys Bot Connector to Sierra via headers. POST /genesys/chat 
converts headers with the preﬁx x-sierra-secret- to memory secrets. As an example, x-sierra-secret-
vcgToken is passed to Sierra as the memory secret vcgToken.

Draft: Conﬁdential Information         12  
 
Transfer mechanism 
The Transfer mechanism will be used to generate a user callback .  A ﬂow will prompt the user to accept a 
callback, and if accepted, for their phone number. 
When Sierra needs to escalate to a live agent, it triggers a transfer event as a bot connector webhook 
"COMPLETE" response with the data necessary for routing via output.send(type:transfer" , data: { ... }). 
Genesys will then direct to a workﬂow that is responsible for routing logic beyond those initial values, 
including sending a message in the case in which the contact center is closed. 
Error messages 
This is implemented in full according to the API Spec with the exception of HTTP 400 (SESSION_CLOSED), 
which is not implemented by design (see notes on Request Body botSessionTimeout). 
  

  
 
Draft: Conﬁdential Information         13  
Conﬁgure Genesys with the Digital Bot Connector 
Install the Bot Connector integration 
Install as shown below, using the Genesys Admin UI 
 
Conﬁgure the Bot Connector 
Conﬁgure with a Utterance URI, i.e. postUtterance webhook 
Set the endpoint URL:  https://api.sierra.chat/genesys/chat/TokenGoesHere 
Conﬁgure Bot Connector credentials 
Conﬁgure the Genesys Bot Connector to pass memory secret headers to the endpoint. Any header with 
the preﬁx x-sierra-secret- is treated as a header to be converted to a memory secret. 

  
 
Draft: Conﬁdential Information         14  
 
Register a bot for the Bot Connector integration 
The Bot Connector needs to be registered so Genesys can route conversations to it. Using the Genesys 
API Explorer, call the PUT endpoint under Integrations > BotConnector to set a list of bots for the 
integration. The Integration ID from the Bot Connector conﬁgured in the previous step is needed, along 
with a name and UUID for the bot (any valid UUID will work). 
For detailed instructions, see the Genesys bot registration guide. Alternatively, the PUT request can be 
made directly via the API, which requires an OAuth client with admin scopes to obtain a bearer token. 
Incorporate the Bot Connector into a Genesys Workﬂow 
Conﬁgure the Bot Connector to map the following intents to the appropriate next steps: 
 transfer: Escalate to a live agent. Upon transfer, the postUtterance webhook can send a payload 
within the parameters ﬁeld of the response body with values to be mapped to Participant Data. 
These values can include transfer reason, sentiment, summary, etc. 
 endConversation: The conversation has come to a natural conclusion and should be closed out in 
Genesys. 
 Failure: Something has gone wrong within the Sierra AI Agent and needs to be gracefully handled 
in Genesys. 

  
 
Draft: Conﬁdential Information         15  
 
 
Increase the default Bot timeout 
Requests to postUtterance from Bot Connector have timeouts that default to 11 seconds. To ensure the 
Sierra agent is not aƯected by this timeout, a Genesys support request will be submitted to increase the 
timeout to 60 seconds. 
Conﬁgure Sierra 
Sierra needs to enable Genesys integration for the organization. 
To get initial connection, the presence of a Live Release is all that is needed and the integration will 
behave very much like a standard headless API integration. 
Beyond basic conﬁguration and to support many of the features described below, genesysConversationId 
needs to be added to the root store. The integration will set this value, so this is simply for type safety. 
export type MyAgentRootStore = { 
    genesysConversationId?: string; 
}; 

  
 
Draft: Conﬁdential Information         16  
Ingesting parameters 
Bot Connector can send parameters to the postUtterance webhook. These parameters are made 
available to the Agent as memory variables. 
 
Sending conversation data to Genesys 
Genesys Customer Participant Data is the standard way to store information about the customer and the 
conversation. How Sierra sends this data to Genesys depends on whether the conversation is contained. 
For escalated conversations 
Upon transfer, the postUtterance webhook can send a payload within the parameters ﬁeld of the 
response body with values to be mapped to Participant Data by the Genesys Workﬂow. 
The transfer event data can be set as follows (the keys are just examples): 
output.send({ 
    type: "transfer" , 
    data: { 
        summary: "Customer would like to sign up. " , 
        sentiment: "positive" , 
        intent: "signup" , 
        locale: "en-US" , 
    }, 
}); 
For contained conversations 
For any conversation that is not escalated, it may still be useful to tag the conversation with Participant 
Data. To do this, use the Genesys API in the Post-Conversation Hook to send these values to Genesys. It 
may be wise to skip this step if the conversation was previously transferred to avoid duplicating work or 
potentially overwriting data that has since been updated. 
Test and Release 
Genesys and Sierra system test 
To verify that the integration is working as expected, it is recommended that a non-production Messenger 
Deployment and Conﬁguration be created that points to the Inbound Message Workﬂow and embed the 
Deployment script in a non-production instance of the portal. 
Sierra Agent via webhook 
The webhook can be tested using curl, Postman, or any other API client. genesysConversationId can be 
set to any unique string. Any ﬁeld not in use (for example, botSessionId) can be sent as an empty string. 
  
 
Draft: Conﬁdential Information         17  
Bot Connector constraints 
There are several constraints within the Bot Connector Integration, most of which are enumerated here. 
 Double messaging: Currently, the Bot Connector supports synchronous messaging only. If a customer 
sends multiple messages in a row, only the ﬁrst message will be sent to the bot via the postUtterance 
webhook. Subsequent messages will show up in Interaction transcripts in Genesys. 
 Rich text (markdown): Genesys has a diƯerent syntax for creating rich text using markdown than Sierra 
does. 
 Image support: Image markdown tags (e.g.! [image](https://example.com)) are not rendered as 
images. They appear as plain text. 
 Lists: Numbered and bulleted lists lack some formatting—list elements lack indentation and bullets 
appear as - instead of •. 
 Receiving ﬁles from customers: There is no support for customers to upload images and ﬁles. Bot 
Connector will omit the media in its message to Sierra. This is true even when the ﬁle upload feature 
is enabled in the Genesys widget. 
 Sending ﬁles to customers: Sierra can send media via cards, carousels, quick replies, and links.

Benefits Service Consumer Guide
Consumer-facing guide for applications that need to call Benefits Service.
Last updated: 2026-07-06
Overview
Benefits Service provides customer-scoped plan benefit data and coverage-check decisions. Consumers can:
list loaded benefit plans
read the latest or effective-date-specific payload for one plan
run a coverage check for a resolved plan/product and one or more code pairs
upload plan snapshots, when explicitly approved for ingestion
All deployed consumer calls go through APIM and authenticate with an x-api-key header. Consumers do not pass a customer slug
in the request and do not create or send x-context-token values. APIM validates the API key with Customer Configuration Service
(CCS), receives an internal context token, and forwards the request to Benefits Service with trusted customer context.

Use the URL format and environment-specific API Management route paths in this guide to configure the Benefits Service URL.
Obtain the customer-specific access details for your integration from Stellarus.

Rate Limits And Concurrency
Benefits Service is protected at the APIM/API-key layer. The default API rate limit is 60 requests per second per API key, unless
Stellarus has configured a customer-specific override.
If your system exceeds its assigned limit, APIM returns 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header. Consumers should
honor Retry-After, keep aggregate traffic below the assigned RPS limit, and use bounded client-side concurrency with retry
backoff and jitter.
There is no separate published concurrency limit for Benefits Service. If your expected production traffic requires more than the
default 60 RPS, coordinate with Stellarus before launch.
