Overview
. 
Consultant shall implement an artificial intelligence agent (the “AI Agent”) on the Sierra platform to assist BSC employees through web chat with questions about their health insurance plan benefits while they are logged in to the BSC website.
Employees will interact with the AI Agent through the BSC website using Genesys Cloud CX (“GCX”) web chat. GCX web chat will be integrated into the website, and GCX will route employee chat interactions to the Sierra platform through the Sierra Genesys Bot Connector integration. GCX will manage the interactions so that, if the AI Agent is unable to fully assist an employee, GCX callback can be used to transition the employee from web chat to voice and route the callback to live agents during business hours. When live agents are engaged, they will be provided with context from the interaction.
The implementation is limited to BSC employees and to questions related to BSC employee health insurance plans. The number of plans included in scope is limited to 8.
Services
. Consultant shall provide the following services to BSC (the “Services”):
Specification
.
  
Consultant will provide analysis services to specify the behavioral and technical requirements for the solution and the evaluations required to validate the solution before release. The primary deliverable for this work will be a Solution Specification Document (the “SSD”).
The SSD is intended to serve as the primary reference for solution behavior, evaluation, change management, and release readiness. The SSD will define the solution in terms of behaviors that the AI Agent must perform, must not perform, should perform, or should not perform. Behaviors classified as musts, and their associated evaluations, are critical and must satisfy their associated evaluations before production release unless otherwise agreed. Behaviors classified as shoulds, and their associated evaluations, guide solution quality but may be deferred as agreed.
Consultant will start with the business use cases or user stories and decompose them into one or more behaviors as needed to support solution configuration, evaluation, and release decisions. For each behavior, the SSD will document one or more evaluations used to validate the behavior. The SSD will also identify the knowledge sources and dependencies for the solution.
When
 a stakeholder identifies a desired behavior, an undesired behavior, or a change to a previously defined behavior, the SSD will be reviewed to determine whether the behavior is already specified, whether the existing evaluation remains appropriate, or whether the SSD should be updated to reflect the revised behavior and associated evaluation.

Interaction Management
.  
Consultant will configure GCX and facilitate the integrations between the AI Agent and GCX and between the BSC website and GCX.  
If the AI Agent cannot assist an employee,

 callback

 to transition the employee from web chat to voice and route the callback to live agents during business hours

maintain participant data, routing, monitoring, and reporting while 
employees interact with both

AI Agent
 in web chat and the live agents in voice.
Testing
.  
Consultant shall test the AI Agent based on the behaviors and evaluations documented in the SSD. The evaluations documented in the SSD will be implemented as simulations in the Sierra platform and executed before each release. Evaluations associated with must behaviors will be implemented as critical simulations and are required for release readiness unless otherwise agreed. Evaluations associated with should behaviors will be implemented as non-critical simulations and will be used to assess solution quality and support release decisions. If an evaluation fails, Consultant may update the AI Agent configuration
 
and execute the simulations again. If needed, the SSD may also be updated to reflect revised behaviors or evaluations before additional testing is performed. BSC is responsible for acceptance testing during the test phase of the project.

The initial implementation will focus on a text-based chat experience designed to support members with plan-related questions and self-service needs. 
The primary use case for the solution is member benefits look-up across Employee Medical, Specialty, and Pharmacy plans. Exhibit A-57
Statement of Work
THIS STATEMENT OF WORK (the “SOW”) is made, entered into, and effective 
June 1, 2026
 (the “Effective Date”), by and between Performance Technology Partners, LLC (“Consultant”) and 
Stellarus, LLC
 (“
Stellarus
”).  This SOW shall be governed by the terms and conditions of the Consulting Agreement 
originally entered into between Consultant and California Physicians’ Service d/b/a Blue Shield of California dated August 27, 2007 and subsequently assigned to Stellarus pursuant to the Notice of Assignment of Consulting Agreement to Affiliate dated October 17, 2024, as amended (collectively, the “Agreement”).
1.
Services
1.1
Overview
.
  Consultant shall design, configure, evaluate and prepare for production release an artificial intelligence agent (the “AI Agent”) on the Sierra platform that assists BSC employees, via web chat, with questions about their employer-sponsored health insurance plan benefits while they are authenticated on the BSC website.
  This Statement of Work covers the conversational AI Agent for the chat modality only.  Voice adaptation of the same AI Agent and the Genesys Cloud CX integration work that exposes the AI Agent on the portal and routes inbound voice traffic are addressed in separate Statements of Work (SOW 
A-
58 and SOW 
A-
59, respectively).
The AI Agent is intended to provide grounded, 
knowledge based
 responses, follow defined conversation policies, escalate gracefully to a live agent when out of scope or low-confidence, and produce consistent, auditable conversation outcomes.  The implementation is limited to BSC employees and to questions related to BSC employee health insurance plans.  The number of plans included in scope is limited to 
twelve 
(
12
).
At a high level, Consultant will deliver: (a) a detailed Solution Specification Document, (b) a fully configured Sierra workspace for the chat AI Agent (system prompts, persona, conversation policies, tools, guardrails, routing logic), (c) a curated knowledge base spanning the 
twelve 
in-scope plans
,
 (d) a comprehensive evaluation/simulation suite covering critical and non-critical behaviors, (e) test execution results, and (f) operations enablement so that BSC can sustain and extend the AI Agent post-release.
1.2
Services
.  Consultant shall provide the following services to BSC (the “Services”):
1.2.1
Discovery and Solution Specification
.  Consultant shall conduct discovery workshops with BSC business and technical stakeholders to define the in-scope use cases, the expected conversational behaviors, the evaluations used to validate those behaviors, and the success criteria for production release.  The primary deliverable from this activity is the Solution Specification Document (the “SSD”).
The SSD will serve as the primary reference for solution behavior, evaluation, change management, and release readiness.  The SSD will define the solution in terms of behaviors that the AI Agent must perform, must not perform, should perform, or should not perform.  Behaviors classified as “musts”, and their associated evaluations, are critical and must satisfy their associated evaluations before production release unless otherwise agreed.  Behaviors classified as “
shoulds
”, and their associated evaluations, guide solution quality but may be deferred as agreed.
Consultant will start with the business use cases or user stories supplied by BSC and decompose them into one or more behaviors as needed to support solution configuration, evaluation, and release decisions.  For each behavior the SSD will document one or 
more evaluations used to validate the behavior, the data and knowledge sources required, the escalation/refusal logic, and the expected conversational outcome.  The SSD will also identify the knowledge sources and dependencies for the solution and any open questions that must be resolved before build.
When a stakeholder identifies a desired behavior, an undesired behavior, or a change to a previously defined behavior, the SSD will be reviewed to determine whether the behavior is already specified, whether the existing evaluation remains appropriate, or whether the SSD should be updated to reflect the revised behavior and associated evaluation.
1.2.2  
Advisory and Education
.  Throughout the engagement, Consultant's Engagement Lead, supported by the Solution Architect and other Consultant subject
 
matter experts, shall provide ongoing advisory and education services to 
Stellarus’ 
technical resources and 
BSC’s 
business leaders.  The intent of these services is to elevate 
the 
collective understanding of generative agent architecture, design patterns, operational characteristics, and deployment considerations so that stakeholders can make informed decisions during this engagement and remain capable of 
maintaining
 the solution after Consultant's involvement concludes.
 
Advisory and education activities will be tailored to the audience and may include
:
(a) 
Working 
sessions and deep dives on generative agent architecture on the Sierra platform, alternatives considered and the trade-offs that informed key architectural decisions, retrieval and grounding patterns, evaluation and simulation methodology, 
and 
integration patterns with contact-center platforms
.
(b) 
Executive
 briefings on deployment expectations, 
the 
operational and organizational implications of placing a generative agent into production,
 and
 industry 
best practices
 drawn from Consultant's experience 
with similar 
engagements
.
(c) 
Practical
 guidance on the risk model for generative agents in healthcare contexts, including grounding, refusal and escalation patterns, audit and logging considerations, model-drift and knowledge-drift considerations, and 
ongoing tuning requirements.
These services will be 
integrated throughout the
 engagement rather than performed in a separate 
phase, and
 will be delivered through a combination of working sessions, executive briefings, 
and 
architecture review sessions.  Consultant will work with BSC to identify
 appropriate
 
audiences
 topics 
on an ongoing basis.
1.2.
3
Conversation and Behavior Design
.  Consultant shall design the chat conversational experience for the AI Agent across the in-scope plan-benefits use cases.  This includes the AI Agent persona, tone and voice for written chat, opening and closing turns, intent acknowledgment patterns, disambiguation strategies, multi-turn information gathering, refusal and disclaimer language, and the escalation hand-off language used when the AI Agent transitions an employee to a live agent.
 
Consultant will define and document the conversational guardrails the AI Agent must enforce (e.g., refusal to provide individualized medical, legal or claims-determination advice; refusal to disclose Protected Health Information (PHI) outside of authenticated, in-context use; refusal to discuss plans outside the in-scope 
twelve 
(
12
); refusal to speculate beyond grounded knowledge).  These guardrails will be enumerated in the SSD as “must not” behaviors and will each have one or more associated evaluations.
1.2.
4
Knowledge Base Engineering
.  Consultant shall ingest, normalize and curate the source materials required to ground the AI Agent for the 
twelve 
(
12
) in-scope plans.  Sources may include Summary Plan Descriptions, Evidence of Coverage documents, benefit summaries, plan FAQs, and other plan-administration materials provided by BSC.  For each source document, Consultant will perform extraction (text, tables, structured fields), normalization, chunking, and conversion into knowledge articles structured for retrieval and use by the AI Agent.
Consultant will produce a 
Knowledge
-to-Behavior Traceability Matrix that maps each documented behavior in the SSD to the source documents and knowledge articles supporting it, so that BSC can audit grounding coverage and identify gaps.
Consultant will define and document the cadence and mechanics for refreshing the knowledge base when source documents change (e.g., annual open enrollment plan updates) and will train designated BSC staff in the refresh process as part of knowledge transfer.
 
Consultant 
will 
process
 
approximately twenty (20) 
source documents 
in JSON and PDF format as provided
 by BSC. These sources
 with be ingested into the Sierra workspace and decomposed 
for use by the generative agent, resulting in approximately 
35
0 unique knowledge
 articles.
1.2.
5
AI Agent Configuration on Sierra
.  Consultant shall stand up and configure the Sierra workspace for the AI Agent.  This includes environment setup aligned to BSC change-management requirements, agent persona and system prompt authoring, conversation policy configuration, tool and function registration, retrieval configuration, output formatting, low-confidence handling, fallback behavior, and per-plan branching where required by plan-specific behavior differences.
Consultant will configure the AI Agent to operate within the conversational guardrails defined in section 1.2.2 above, including PHI handling rules, refusal patterns, and the escalation hand-off contract that will be consumed by the Genesys Cloud CX integration delivered under SOW 
A-
59.
Configuration artifacts (prompts, policy definitions, tool registrations) will be 
created
 in the Sierra workspace and exported as part of the Configured Sierra Workspace deliverable so that BSC has a snapshot of the as-built configuration.
1.2.
6
Backend Tool and Function Integration
.  If the AI Agent needs to call BSC web services to retrieve member-specific or plan-specific data in real time, Consultant will develop the integration between the AI Agent and those web services, including request/response handling, error handling, timeout behavior, and circuit-breaker behavior so that web service failures do not produce ungrounded or unsafe responses.
BSC is responsible for documenting and providing the web services in advance of the build phase
, including authentication mechanisms, request/response schemas, sandbox/test endpoints, and representative test data.  
1.2.
7
Evaluation and Simulation Engineering
.  Consultant shall implement, in the Sierra platform, the evaluations documented in the SSD as automated simulations executable against the AI Agent.  Evaluations associated with “must” behaviors will be implemented as critical simulations and are required for release readiness unless otherwise agreed.  Evaluations associated with “should” behaviors will be implemented as non-critical simulations and will be used to assess solution quality and to support release decisions.
The simulation suite will include, at a minimum: (a) grounding evaluations that confirm responses are sourced to the knowledge base, (b) refusal evaluations for out-of-scope and unsafe requests, (c) escalation evaluations that confirm the AI Agent triggers hand-off correctly, (d) tone and clarity evaluations, and (e) per-plan behavior evaluations covering plan-specific differences across the 
twelve 
(
12
) in-scope plans.
Consultant will run the full suite before each release, triage failures, update configuration or knowledge as needed, and re-execute until release criteria are met.  Simulation definitions and results will be exported and provided to BSC as part of each Test Execution Report.
 The initial release is anticipated to include approximately 400 
simulations. Each additional release will generate additional 
simulations, and
 also include the prior simulation set as a regression test to e
nsure 
accuracy
, safety, and groundedness are preserved with each iteration.
1.2.
8
Pre-Production Testing
.  In addition to the automated simulation suite, Consultant shall support a structured pre-production testing phase including a User Acceptance Testing (UAT) cycle with BSC business stakeholders.  Consultant will triage defects, propose remediations, implement remediations to the AI Agent configuration or knowledge base, and re-test.
Consultant will also support an optional limited pilot with a small population of BSC employees prior to broad release, if BSC elects to pilot.  Pilot scope, population, and entry/exit criteria will be defined jointly during specification.
BSC is responsible for performing and signing off on User Acceptance Testing.  Consultant will provide test scripts, defect-triage support and remediation during this phase.
 
Acceptance is based on 100% pass rate for critical scenarios, characterized as “must do” and “must not do” with 95% accuracy for other scenarios as measured by 
the Sierra instrumentation tools
, in alignment with the process for other implementations at BSC.
Target first-token latency ≤ 2 seconds for chat, ≤ 1.5 seconds for voice; end-of-turn target ≤ 6 seconds chat, ≤ 4 seconds voice. 
Targets assume nominal performance of the Sierra platform, 
GCX, 
the underlying LLM inference layer, and BSC-provided web services
.
1.2.
9
Knowledge Transfer and Enablement
.  Consultant shall create 
an
 Operations Guide (the “Operations Guide”) that describes how to configure, evaluate, improve, and operate the AI Agent in production, and shall conduct live knowledge-transfer sessions with the BSC operations team.  The goal of knowledge transfer is to ensure that BSC can independently improve existing use cases, add new use cases, refresh the knowledge base, and operate the simulation suite as part of ongoing change management.
Knowledge-transfer sessions will be scheduled during the testing phase and will be recorded.  Topics will 
include:
 Sierra workspace administration, prompt and policy change management, knowledge-
base
 authoring and refresh, evaluation authoring, simulation execution and triage, 
and 
release-readiness procedures.
1.2.
10 
Release Readiness
,
 
Production Cutover Support
, and Hypercare
.  Consultant shall produce a Production Release Readiness Report documenting the state of all critical simulations, outstanding defects, residual risks, recommended go/no-go decision, and the cutover plan.  Consultant shall support the production cutover activities defined in the cutover plan, including configuration promotion, smoke testing, and hyper-care support
.
1.2.
10
.1  
Consultant will provide 
hypercare
 support for a period of 2 business weeks following the production release of the Deliverables under this SOW (the "Hypercare Period"). The Hypercare Period may be extended at BSC's request through a written change order at scope and fees to be agreed by the parties.
1.2.

WHAT:
 AI-powered chatbot integrated in the Member Portal and Mobile App, delivering and always-available, natural language self-service experience that aligns with evolving industry standards. This not only reduces support costs but also strengthens our position as a digitally forward, member-centric health insurance provider.
WHY:
 As digital expectations and costs in healthcare rise, it mandates seamless, self-service support comparable to other industries and competitors. Continuing to rely heavily on call centers for routine queries limits our ability to meet these expectations, inflates operating costs and risks eroding member satisfaction and loyalty. 
Strategic and competitive advantage for BSC in a rapid AI adoption landscape
Contact center call containment and resulting cost savings

Overview
. 
Consultant shall implement an artificial intelligence agent (the “AI Agent”) on the Sierra platform to assist BSC employees through web chat with questions about their health insurance plan benefits while they are logged in to the BSC website.
Employees will interact with the AI Agent through the BSC website using Genesys Cloud CX (“GCX”) web chat. GCX web chat will be integrated into the website, and GCX will route employee chat interactions to the Sierra platform through the Sierra Genesys Bot Connector integration. GCX will manage the interactions so that, if the AI Agent is unable to fully assist an employee, GCX callback can be used to transition the employee from web chat to voice and route the callback to live agents during business hours. When live agents are engaged, they will be provided with context from the interaction.
The implementation is limited to BSC employees and to questions related to BSC employee health insurance plans. The number of plans included in scope is limited to 8.
Services
. Consultant shall provide the following services to BSC (the “Services”):
Specification
.
  
Consultant will provide analysis services to specify the behavioral and technical requirements for the solution and the evaluations required to validate the solution before release. The primary deliverable for this work will be a Solution Specification Document (the “SSD”).
The SSD is intended to serve as the primary reference for solution behavior, evaluation, change management, and release readiness. The SSD will define the solution in terms of behaviors that the AI Agent must perform, must not perform, should perform, or should not perform. Behaviors classified as musts, and their associated evaluations, are critical and must satisfy their associated evaluations before production release unless otherwise agreed. Behaviors classified as 
shoulds
, and their associated evaluations, guide solution quality but may be deferred as agreed.
Consultant will start with the business use cases or user stories and decompose them into one or more behaviors as needed to support solution configuration, evaluation, and release decisions. For each behavior, the SSD will document one or more evaluations used to validate the behavior. The SSD will also identify the knowledge sources and dependencies for the solution.
When
 a stakeholder identifies a desired behavior, an undesired behavior, or a change to a previously defined behavior, the SSD will be reviewed to determine whether the behavior is already specified, whether the existing evaluation remains appropriate, or whether the SSD should be updated to reflect the revised behavior and associated evaluation.

**Benefits Quoting via Sierra** is a member‑facing conversational AI that resolves routine benefit questions through voice and digital self‑service, reducing live‑agent demand while delivering fast, accurate, and accessible answers at scale

**Product:** Sierra AI – Benefits Quoting Agent

**Primary End Users:** Members

**Economic Buyers:** Member Experience, Digital Experience, and Contact Center C‑suite

**Interaction Modes:** Voice, chat, and digital messaging (omnichannel)

Product Description

**Benefits Quoting via Sierra is a member‑facing conversational AI designed to resolve routine benefit inquiries through self‑service across voice and digital channels.** It enables members to ask natural‑language questions about their benefits and receive immediate, policy‑grounded responses without requiring live agent intervention.

Sierra is optimized for **containment, accessibility, and scalability** by handling high‑volume, lower‑complexity benefit questions while escalating edge cases to live agents when needed. By resolving common inquiries upfront, Sierra reduces inbound call volume, shortens wait times, and lowers cost‑to‑serve, while improving member satisfaction.

During pilots, Sierra demonstrated strong performance in self‑service containment and issue resolution, validating its role as the front door of the AI‑Driven Member Advocacy Hub.

Strategic Value

* **Digital containment:** Deflects a meaningful share of benefit inquiries from live agents
* **Always‑on access:** 24/7 availability across voice and digital channels
* **Cost efficiency:** Lower marginal cost per resolved inquiry compared to agent‑assisted interactions
* **Experience lift:** Faster answers and reduced friction improve member satisfaction

Exhibit A-57
Statement of Work
THIS STATEMENT OF WORK (the “SOW”) is made, entered into, and effective 
June 1, 2026
 (the “Effective Date”), by and between Performance Technology Partners, LLC (“Consultant”) and 
Stellarus, LLC
 (“
Stellarus
”).  This SOW shall be governed by the terms and conditions of the Consulting Agreement 
originally entered into between Consultant and California Physicians’ Service d/b/a Blue Shield of California dated August 27, 2007 and subsequently assigned to Stellarus pursuant to the Notice of Assignment of Consulting Agreement to Affiliate dated October 17, 2024, as amended (collectively, the “Agreement”).
1.
Services
1.1
Overview
.
  Consultant shall design, configure, evaluate and prepare for production release an artificial intelligence agent (the “AI Agent”) on the Sierra platform that assists BSC employees, via web chat, with questions about their employer-sponsored health insurance plan benefits while they are authenticated on the BSC website.
  This Statement of Work covers the conversational AI Agent for the chat modality only.  Voice adaptation of the same AI Agent and the Genesys Cloud CX integration work that exposes the AI Agent on the portal and routes inbound voice traffic are addressed in separate Statements of Work (SOW 
A-
58 and SOW 
A-
59, respectively).
The AI Agent is intended to provide grounded, 
knowledge based
 responses, follow defined conversation policies, escalate gracefully to a live agent when out of scope or low-confidence, and produce consistent, auditable conversation outcomes.  The implementation is limited to BSC employees and to questions related to BSC employee health insurance plans.  The number of plans included in scope is limited to 
twelve 
(
12
).
At a high level, Consultant will deliver: (a) a detailed Solution Specification Document, (b) a fully configured Sierra workspace for the chat AI Agent (system prompts, persona, conversation policies, tools, guardrails, routing logic), (c) a curated knowledge base spanning the 
twelve 
in-scope plans
,
 (d) a comprehensive evaluation/simulation suite covering critical and non-critical behaviors, (e) test execution results, and (f) operations enablement so that BSC can sustain and extend the AI Agent post-release.
1.2
Services
.  Consultant shall provide the following services to BSC (the “Services”):
1.2.1
Discovery and Solution Specification
.  Consultant shall conduct discovery workshops with BSC business and technical stakeholders to define the in-scope use cases, the expected conversational behaviors, the evaluations used to validate those behaviors, and the success criteria for production release.  The primary deliverable from this activity is the Solution Specification Document (the “SSD”).
The SSD will serve as the primary reference for solution behavior, evaluation, change management, and release readiness.  The SSD will define the solution in terms of behaviors that the AI Agent must perform, must not perform, should perform, or should not perform.  Behaviors classified as “musts”, and their associated evaluations, are critical and must satisfy their associated evaluations before production release unless otherwise agreed.  Behaviors classified as “
shoulds
”, and their associated evaluations, guide solution quality but may be deferred as agreed.
Consultant will start with the business use cases or user stories supplied by BSC and decompose them into one or more behaviors as needed to support solution configuration, evaluation, and release decisions.  For each behavior the SSD will document one or 
more evaluations used to validate the behavior, the data and knowledge sources required, the escalation/refusal logic, and the expected conversational outcome.  The SSD will also identify the knowledge sources and dependencies for the solution and any open questions that must be resolved before build.
When a stakeholder identifies a desired behavior, an undesired behavior, or a change to a previously defined behavior, the SSD will be reviewed to determine whether the behavior is already specified, whether the existing evaluation remains appropriate, or whether the SSD should be updated to reflect the revised behavior and associated evaluation.
1.2.2  
Advisory and Education
.  Throughout the engagement, Consultant's Engagement Lead, supported by the Solution Architect and other Consultant subject
 
matter experts, shall provide ongoing advisory and education services to 
Stellarus’ 
technical resources and 
BSC’s 
business leaders.  The intent of these services is to elevate 
the 
collective understanding of generative agent architecture, design patterns, operational characteristics, and deployment considerations so that stakeholders can make informed decisions during this engagement and remain capable of 
maintaining
 the solution after Consultant's involvement concludes.
 
Advisory and education activities will be tailored to the audience and may include
:
(a) 
Working 
sessions and deep dives on generative agent architecture on the Sierra platform, alternatives considered and the trade-offs that informed key architectural decisions, retrieval and grounding patterns, evaluation and simulation methodology, 
and 
integration patterns with contact-center platforms
.
(b) 
Executive
 briefings on deployment expectations, 
the 
operational and organizational implications of placing a generative agent into production,
 and
 industry 
best practices
 drawn from Consultant's experience 
with similar 
engagements
.
(c) 
Practical
 guidance on the risk model for generative agents in healthcare contexts, including grounding, refusal and escalation patterns, audit and logging considerations, model-drift and knowledge-drift considerations, and 
ongoing tuning requirements.
These services will be 
integrated throughout the
 engagement rather than performed in a separate 
phase, and
 will be delivered through a combination of working sessions, executive briefings, 
and 
architecture review sessions.  Consultant will work with BSC to identify
 appropriate
 
audiences
 topics 
on an ongoing basis.
1.2.
3
Conversation and Behavior Design
.  Consultant shall design the chat conversational experience for the AI Agent across the in-scope plan-benefits use cases.  This includes the AI Agent persona, tone and voice for written chat, opening and closing turns, intent acknowledgment patterns, disambiguation strategies, multi-turn information gathering, refusal and disclaimer language, and the escalation hand-off language used when the AI Agent transitions an employee to a live agent.
 
Consultant will define and document the conversational guardrails the AI Agent must enforce (e.g., refusal to provide individualized medical, legal or claims-determination advice; refusal to disclose Protected Health Information (PHI) outside of authenticated, in-context use; refusal to discuss plans outside the in-scope 
twelve 
(
12
); refusal to speculate beyond grounded knowledge).  These guardrails will be enumerated in the SSD as “must not” behaviors and will each have one or more associated evaluations.
1.2.
4
Knowledge Base Engineering
.  Consultant shall ingest, normalize and curate the source materials required to ground the AI Agent for the 
twelve 
(
12
) in-scope plans.  Sources may include Summary Plan Descriptions, Evidence of Coverage documents, benefit summaries, plan FAQs, and other plan-administration materials provided by BSC.  For each source document, Consultant will perform extraction (text, tables, structured fields), normalization, chunking, and conversion into knowledge articles structured for retrieval and use by the AI Agent.
Consultant will produce a 
Knowledge
-to-Behavior Traceability Matrix that maps each documented behavior in the SSD to the source documents and knowledge articles supporting it, so that BSC can audit grounding coverage and identify gaps.
Consultant will define and document the cadence and mechanics for refreshing the knowledge base when source documents change (e.g., annual open enrollment plan updates) and will train designated BSC staff in the refresh process as part of knowledge transfer.
 
Consultant 
will 
process
 
approximately twenty (20) 
source documents 
in JSON and PDF format as provided
 by BSC. These sources
 with be ingested into the Sierra workspace and decomposed 
for use by the generative agent, resulting in approximately 
35
0 unique knowledge
 articles.
1.2.
5
AI Agent Configuration on Sierra
.  Consultant shall stand up and configure the Sierra workspace for the AI Agent.  This includes environment setup aligned to BSC change-management requirements, agent persona and system prompt authoring, conversation policy configuration, tool and function registration, retrieval configuration, output formatting, low-confidence handling, fallback behavior, and per-plan branching where required by plan-specific behavior differences.
Consultant will configure the AI Agent to operate within the conversational guardrails defined in section 1.2.2 above, including PHI handling rules, refusal patterns, and the escalation hand-off contract that will be consumed by the Genesys Cloud CX integration delivered under SOW 
A-
59.
Configuration artifacts (prompts, policy definitions, tool registrations) will be 
created
 in the Sierra workspace and exported as part of the Configured Sierra Workspace deliverable so that BSC has a snapshot of the as-built configuration.
1.2.
6
Backend Tool and Function Integration
.  If the AI Agent needs to call BSC web services to retrieve member-specific or plan-specific data in real time, Consultant will develop the integration between the AI Agent and those web services, including request/response handling, error handling, timeout behavior, and circuit-breaker behavior so that web service failures do not produce ungrounded or unsafe responses.
BSC is responsible for documenting and providing the web services in advance of the build phase
, including authentication mechanisms, request/response schemas, sandbox/test endpoints, and representative test data.  
1.2.
7
Evaluation and Simulation Engineering
.  Consultant shall implement, in the Sierra platform, the evaluations documented in the SSD as automated simulations executable against the AI Agent.  Evaluations associated with “must” behaviors will be implemented as critical simulations and are required for release readiness unless otherwise agreed.  Evaluations associated with “should” behaviors will be implemented as non-critical simulations and will be used to assess solution quality and to support release decisions.
The simulation suite will include, at a minimum: (a) grounding evaluations that confirm responses are sourced to the knowledge base, (b) refusal evaluations for out-of-scope and unsafe requests, (c) escalation evaluations that confirm the AI Agent triggers hand-off correctly, (d) tone and clarity evaluations, and (e) per-plan behavior evaluations covering plan-specific differences across the 
twelve 
(
12
) in-scope plans.
Consultant will run the full suite before each release, triage failures, update configuration or knowledge as needed, and re-execute until release criteria are met.  Simulation definitions and results will be exported and provided to BSC as part of each Test Execution Report.
 The initial release is anticipated to include approximately 400 
simulations. Each additional release will generate additional 
simulations, and
 also include the prior simulation set as a regression test to e
nsure 
accuracy
, safety, and groundedness are preserved with each iteration.
1.2.
8
Pre-Production Testing
.  In addition to the automated simulation suite, Consultant shall support a structured pre-production testing phase including a User Acceptance Testing (UAT) cycle with BSC business stakeholders.  Consultant will triage defects, propose remediations, implement remediations to the AI Agent configuration or knowledge base, and re-test.
Consultant will also support an optional limited pilot with a small population of BSC employees prior to broad release, if BSC elects to pilot.  Pilot scope, population, and entry/exit criteria will be defined jointly during specification.
BSC is responsible for performing and signing off on User Acceptance Testing.  Consultant will provide test scripts, defect-triage support and remediation during this phase.
 
Acceptance is based on 100% pass rate for critical scenarios, characterized as “must do” and “must not do” with 95% accuracy for other scenarios as measured by 
the Sierra instrumentation tools
, in alignment with the process for other implementations at BSC.
Target first-token latency ≤ 2 seconds for chat, ≤ 1.5 seconds for voice; end-of-turn target ≤ 6 seconds chat, ≤ 4 seconds voice. 
Targets assume nominal performance of the Sierra platform, 
GCX, 
the underlying LLM inference layer, and BSC-provided web services
.
1.2.
9
Knowledge Transfer and Enablement
.  Consultant shall create 
an
 Operations Guide (the “Operations Guide”) that describes how to configure, evaluate, improve, and operate the AI Agent in production, and shall conduct live knowledge-transfer sessions with the BSC operations team.  The goal of knowledge transfer is to ensure that BSC can independently improve existing use cases, add new use cases, refresh the knowledge base, and operate the simulation suite as part of ongoing change management.
Knowledge-transfer sessions will be scheduled during the testing phase and will be recorded.  Topics will 
include:
 Sierra workspace administration, prompt and policy change management, knowledge-
base
 authoring and refresh, evaluation authoring, simulation execution and triage, 
and 
release-readiness procedures.
1.2.
10 
Release Readiness
,
 
Production Cutover Support
, and Hypercare
.  Consultant shall produce a Production Release Readiness Report documenting the state of all critical simulations, outstanding defects, residual risks, recommended go/no-go decision, and the cutover plan.  Consultant shall support the production cutover activities defined in the cutover plan, including configuration promotion, smoke testing, and hyper-care support
.
1.2.
10
.1  
Consultant will provide 
hypercare
 support for a period of 2 business weeks following the production release of the Deliverables under this SOW (the "Hypercare Period"). The Hypercare Period may be extended at BSC's request through a written change order at scope and fees to be agreed by the parties.
1.2.
10
.2  
Hypercare support will be provided during BSC business hours, Monday through Friday excluding BSC-observed holidays, with on-call engineering response for Severity 1 (Critical) incidents outside of business hours. All other severity levels are worked during business hours.
1.2.
10
.3  
BSC will report issues through a jointly
 
agreed channel (designated email alias, shared messaging channel, or ticketing tool) confirmed during cutover planning. The Engagement Lead and Project Manager will serve as primary points of escalation for BSC.
 Solution performance will be monitored through a combination of establish
ed
 reporting
 dashboards within Sierra
 and GCX
, 
survey 
results
, 
manual review of session 
transcripts
 by Consultant and BSC
, and 
qualitative feedback from contact center representative
s
.
1.2.
10
.4  
Issues identified during the Hypercare Period will be classified jointly by BSC and Consultant using the following definitions:
Severity
Definition
1 - Critical
The agent is unavailable or non-responsive for all or a large subset of users; the retrieval or knowledge layer has failed; or the agent is generating harmful, false, or non-compliant outputs at scale.
2 - High
A core agent capability is significantly impaired including persistent retrieval failures, inability to complete a primary use case, or systematic hallucination on a defined topic
.
3 - Medium
Agent behavior is degraded in a limited or non-core way, including inconsistent grounding or stale knowledge content, and a workaround exists or the issue occurs only under specific conditions.
4 - Low
Minor issue, knowledge base content correction, prompt or instruction adjustment, or non-urgent refinement of an existing agent behavior.
1.2.
10
.5  
Consultant commits to the following acknowledgment, working, and communication commitments during the Hypercare Period:
Severity
Initial Response
Working C
ommitment
Status Updates

Within 1 business hour

 backlog and worked during business hours based on impact

10

6
  
The parties acknowledge that the time required to resolve an issue with the AI Agent and the associated integrations is driven by the root cause, complexity, and dependency on third-party platforms (including Sierra and Genesys Cloud CX), BSC IT infrastructure, and BSC-provided web services. Consultant commits to the acknowledgment, working
 commitment
, and status
 
update c
adence
 
above
, and 
does not commit to a specific resolution deadline
. For each open issue, Consultant will maintain 
open communication and
 proactively escalate to the Engagement Lead and the BSC Operations Owner when the estimate changes materially or when root cause is identified to lie outside Consultant's scope of work.
  
Where the root cause of an issue is determined to lie within a third-party platform (Sierra, Genesys Cloud CX), BSC IT infrastructure, or BSC-provided web services, Consultant's responsibility during 
hypercare
 is limited to triage, root-cause identification, coordination with the responsible party, ongoing communication with BSC
.
1.2.
10
.
7
  
Hypercare is limited to defect remediation against the Deliverables accepted under this SOW. The following are expressly out of scope of 
hypercare
 and, if requested, will be handled through written change orders:
New use cases, new intents, new conversation flows, or new behaviors not documented in the SSD
New plans or material revisions to in-scope plans during the Hypercare Period
New integrations, or material changes to in-scope integrations
Routine or scheduled knowledge-
base
 refresh (including annual open enrollment updates)
Knowledge updates resulting from changes to BSC source materials provided after acceptance
Performance tuning beyond the targets documented in the SSD
Enhancement requests of any classification
 
 
1.2.
11 
Post Production
 Support & Optimization
. 
At the conclusion of the hypercar period,
 Consultant will continue working alongside BSC for an additional four business week
s
, shifting focus from incident response to tuning, optimization, monitoring, and collaborative operational support. During 
this 
period
, Consultant will refine AI Agent configuration 
based on observed conversation patterns, update knowledge articles where production data reveals gaps, monitor performance against the targets defined in the SSD, address residual issues, and partner with the BSC team on day-to-day operational questions and 
management
 of the solution. The intent is 
to 
capture insights
 from 
early 
production traffic and to support a confident transition of full operational ownership to BSC at the conclusion of the period. The parties will operate as a single working team throughout, 
collaborating to identify and prioritize 
improvement opportunities
. 
This 
post production
 support period is not a managed service, and a
ny continued Consultant involvement beyond th
e 
post production
 support period 
will be addressed under a separate Statement of Work.
1.2.1
2
 
Project Management
.  Consultant shall provide project management for Services, including but not limited to the following:
1.2.1
2
.1
  
Serve as the primary contact for all questions and issues related to Consultant’s Services 
   
hereunder.
1.2.1
2
.2
  
Create and maintain a project plan (the “Project Plan”) and provide a weekly status report (the “Weekly Status Report”) of Consultant’s project progress, staff management, risks, and issues.
1.2.1
2
.3
  
Maintain a risk and issue log and a decision log, updated weekly and reviewed in the weekly status meeting.
1.2.1
2
.4
  
BSC will appoint a single point of contact responsible for all communications and project management among all Customer parties (staff, vendors, consultants) and for the escalation and resolution of any issues for BSC.
1.2.1
2
.5
  
The participation and commitment of BSC’s project team during the project, including assigned tasks to BSC team members, will be a key to project success.
1.2.1
2
.6
  
BSC will provide qualified development engineering/programming resources versed in Customer’s application(s) during any development/integration portion of this project as needed.
1.2.1
2
.7
  
All Services, materials and communications are assumed to be delivered in English, unless otherwise specifically noted.
1.3
Consultant Personnel
.  Consultant shall ensure that its personnel assigned to perform services under this SOW have the necessary qualifications, competence and experience required to provide the Service and Deliverables.  If BSC, at its sole discretion, is not satisfied with the performance of any Consultant personnel, BSC shall notify Consultant and Consultant shall promptly furnish replacement personnel.  BSC 
retains the right at all times
 to end the assignment of any personnel Consultant provides under this SOW.
1.4
Term
.  Consultant shall begin providing the Services under this SOW on the Effective Date and Consultant will complete all Services and provide all Deliverables no later than 
September 30
, 2026
.  Unless otherwise terminated earlier pursuant to the terms of the Agreement, this SOW will terminate on completion of all Services, including final acceptance of all Deliverables.
1.5
Key BSC Roles
.  The participation and commitment of 
BSC's
 project team will be a key to project success.  BSC will provide qualified business and technical resources versed in BSC’s 
applications and systems during the project as needed.  The following key customer roles shall be filled by BSC:
1.5.1
Project Sponsor
.  The Project Sponsor shall be able to articulate the project vision, identify and provide needed resources and funding, and oversee the successful deployment and adoption of the solution.
1.5.2
Benefits Subject Matter Experts
.  BSC shall provide one or more Benefits SMEs with deep knowledge of the 
twelve 
(
12
) in-scope health plans.  Benefits SMEs are responsible for validating knowledge-article accuracy, answering interpretive questions during build, and signing off on plan-specific behaviors.
1.5.3
Compliance and Privacy Reviewer
.  BSC shall provide a Compliance and Privacy Reviewer responsible for reviewing AI Agent disclaimer and refusal language, PHI handling rules, retention and logging configuration, and any other compliance-relevant aspects of the AI Agent prior to production release.
1.5.4
Web Services Developer
.  The Web Services Developer is responsible for documenting and providing any BSC web services
, which 
may
 
be
 used by the AI Agent
 to interact with systems at BSC
.  They will also participate in design sessions, provide the web services documentation as part of design, and serve as the point of contact for any web service changes or issues.
1.5.5
IT Administrator
.  The IT Administrator is responsible for providing infrastructure and network connectivity between the AI Agent and other systems at BSC, ensuring that the network connectivity is robust, and serving as the point of contact for any infrastructure or network issues.
1.5.6
Operations Owner
.  BSC shall designate an Operations Owner who will be the recipient of knowledge transfer, the maintainer of the Operations Guide post-release, and the operational owner of the AI Agent thereafter.
1.6
Assumptions and Dependencies
.  This SOW is predicated on the following assumptions and dependencies.  If any of 
these change
 materially, Consultant may request a change to scope, schedule, and/or fees pursuant to the Agreement:
1.6.1
Plan Scope
.  The number of in-scope BSC employee health plans is limited to 
twelve
 (

# 🧩 Project Name: Compass Performance Dashboard

**PDLC Phase:** Define
**Authored Date:** March 18, 2026
**Status:** DRAFT

## 🎯 Problem Statement

Stellarus operations and engineering teams lack real-time visibility into the operational performance of Compass and the business impact across customer deployments, creating blind spots in service quality monitoring, cost optimization, and continuous improvement planning. Without comprehensive performance analytics, teams cannot proactively identify service degradation, optimize resource allocation, or demonstrate ROI to stakeholders across multiple lines of business.

**Impact:** Risk of undetected service issues affecting customer operations and end-user experience; inability to optimize operational costs across deployments; lack of data-driven insights for future release planning and multi-customer expansion strategies.

## 💡 Proposed Solution

Create a comprehensive, real-time Performance Analytics Dashboard that provides operational teams with actionable insights into Compass and the performance across response times, usage patterns, accuracy metrics, and cost efficiency. The dashboard will integrate with existing telemetry and provide both real-time monitoring and historical trending capabilities.

## 👥 Target Users

**Customer Authenticated Users (Customer-Facing Metrics Only):**

* **Customer Operations Teams:** Need visibility into their deployment's performance, uptime, and service quality metrics
* **Customer IT Leadership:** Require service level monitoring and performance trending for their specific Compass instance
* **Customer Success Managers:** Need usage analytics and accuracy metrics to demonstrate value and identify optimization opportunities

**Stellarus Authenticated Users (Full Internal + Customer Metrics):**

* **Stellarus Operations Team:** Need comprehensive system health monitoring and alerting across all customer deployments
* **Stellarus Product Managers:** Require usage analytics and accuracy trends across all customers to inform future release roadmap
* **Stellarus Customer Success Leadership:** Need business impact metrics to measure ROI and service quality improvements across customer base
* **Stellarus Technical Support:** Need diagnostic data to troubleshoot customer-reported issues across all deployments
* **Stellarus Finance Team:** Require cost tracking and efficiency metrics for budget planning and pricing optimization
* **Stellarus Sales Engineering:** Need performance metrics to support customer expansion discussions and new customer onboarding

## ✅ Success Metrics

How will we measure success in reporting accurate system and product health? Include 2–3 quantifiable KPIs focused on data trust and reliability.

* **Data Accuracy & Reliability:** Achieve <1% variance between dashboard metrics and source system data across all performance indicators, validated through weekly automated reconciliation checks
* **System Health Detection Accuracy:** Dashboard correctly identifies and reports 100% of known system issues within 2 minutes of occurrence, with zero false positive alerts during 30-day measurement period
* **Cross-System Data Integrity:** Maintain 99.9% data freshness SLA with all telemetry sources feeding dashboard metrics no more than 30 seconds behind real-time, measured continuously across all customer deployments

## 📦 Scope

**Performance Metrics Implementation:**

**Customer-Facing Metrics (Visible to Customer Authenticated Users):**

* **Response Time Analytics:** Real-time and historical tracking for customer's deployment (Min, Max, Avg, Median, Standard Deviation)
* **Usage Analytics:** Session counting and trending for customer's instance by Day/Week/Month/Quarter
* **Session Quality Metrics:** Questions per session analytics for customer's deployment
* **Application Health Dashboard:** System uptime and availability trending for customer's instance
* **Quality Assurance:** Question accuracy rate monitoring with confidence scoring for customer's deployment
* **Product Pipeline Analytics:** Total plan products successfully ingested with historical tracking; product update frequency by Day/Week/Month/Quarter; product ingest failure rate percentage with trending and alerting capabilities

**Internal + Customer Metrics (Stellarus Users Only):**

* **Cost Management:** Per-question and per-session cost tracking with trend analysis and forecasting across all customers
* **Infrastructure Monitoring:** API error rate tracking, resource utilization, and capacity planning metrics
* **Business Intelligence:** Revenue per customer, churn risk indicators, and expansion opportunity analysis

**Dashboard Features:**

* **Multi-Tenant Authentication:** Role-based access control with customer vs Stellarus user authentication and authorization
* **Contextual Data Views:** Automatic data filtering based on authenticated user role and customer assignment
* **Real-time Data Visualization:** Live updating charts and KPI cards with last-updated timestamps
* **Historical Trending:** 7-day, 30-day, 90-day views with YoY comparison capabilities where applicable
* **Role-Based Alerting:** Configurable thresholds for key metrics with customer-specific vs global notification capabilities
* **Secure Data Export:** CSV/Excel export functionality with appropriate data filtering based on user permissions

## 🚫 Out-of-Scope

**Explicitly excluded from this iteration:**

###### Cross Customer Analytics:

* **Cross-Customer Analytics:** Aggregated performance metrics across all customer deployments with customer segmentation
* **Cross-Customer Data Sharing:** Customer users will not see aggregated data or metrics from other customer deployments

###### General Scope:

* **End-User Level Analytics:** Individual end-user usage patterns and PII-related metrics (requires additional privacy governance per customer)
* **Advanced AI/ML Insights:** Predictive analytics, anomaly detection algorithms, or machine learning-powered recommendations
* **Customer-Specific System Integration:** Customer proprietary system correlation or external health monitoring integrations
* **White-Label Customization:** Customer-branded dashboard themes or custom UI modifications
* **Advanced RBAC:** Granular permissions beyond customer vs Stellarus user roles (department-level, project-level access)

## ⚠️ Risks & Dependencies

**High-Risk Technical Dependencies:**

* **Customer SSO Integration Complexity:** Each customer deployment may require unique SSO configuration (SAML, OAuth2, LDAP) with varying identity provider implementations, potentially extending authentication integration timeline by 2-4 weeks per customer type
* **Data Isolation Architecture:** Multi-tenant data segregation requires bulletproof customer boundary enforcement at database, API, and UI layers; single misconfiguration could result in data leakage incident requiring immediate system shutdown
* **Compass Telemetry System Dependencies:** Dashboard relies on existing Compass telemetry infrastructure for real-time metrics; any telemetry system outages or schema changes will directly impact dashboard data accuracy and availability

**Medium-Risk Integration Dependencies:**

* **Authentication System Dependencies:** Integration with Stellarus internal identity management system for employee access; changes to corporate authentication policies or system upgrades could break internal user access
* **Customer Onboarding Process:** New customer provisioning requires coordination between Customer Success, IT Security, and Engineering teams; manual steps in onboarding process create risk of access delays or misconfigurations
* **Third-Party Monitoring Tools:** Chart visualization and real-time data refresh depend on integrated monitoring stack; vendor API changes or service outages could impact dashboard functionality

**Business & Operational Risks:**

* **Customer Data Privacy Compliance:** Multi-tenant architecture must comply with varying customer data residency and privacy requirements (GDPR, HIPAA, SOC2); compliance violations could result in customer contract breaches
* **Performance at Scale:** Dashboard performance degradation as customer count increases; inadequate load testing could result in system slowdowns affecting all customers during peak usage
* **Security Audit Timeline:** Required security review for multi-tenant data access may extend launch timeline if vulnerabilities are discovered requiring architectural changes

**Risk Mitigation Strategies:**

* Implement phased rollout starting with pilot customers having standard SSO configurations
* Establish automated testing for data isolation boundaries with continuous monitoring
* Create fallback data sources and graceful degradation for telemetry system dependencies
* Develop comprehensive security testing protocol and schedule security review early in development cycle

## 🏁 Definition of Done

**Functional Completion Criteria:**

* **Authentication System Validation** : Multi-tenant authentication system tested successfully beteween customer and Stellarus SSO integrations. Evidence: Test execution report with pass/fail results, error logs, and performance metrics.
* **Customer Dashboard Functionality** : Customer-facing metrics dashboard validated with 100% successful data filtering tests for 10 representative customer datasets. Evidence: Test cases execution results, screenshots of filtered vs unfiltered data views, data validation report.
* **Internal Dashboard Functionality** : Full internal dashboard tested with 100% access to all metric categories and cross-customer data views for Stellarus authenticated users. Evidence: Feature checklist validation, role-based access matrix verification, test user validation results.
* **Role-Based Access Controls** : Data access permissions tested across 20 user scenarios with 0 unauthorized access incidents. Evidence: Penetration testing report, access control matrix validation, security audit findings.
* **Historical Data Visualization** : Time range selection (7/30/90 days) validated with accurate data retrieval from source systems with <1% variance. Evidence: Data accuracy validation report, automated test suite results, cross-system data comparison.
* **Alerting System Validation** : Role-based alerts tested for 10 threshold scenarios with 100% delivery success rate. Evidence: Alert delivery logs, notification testing results, escalation workflow validation.
* **Data Export Security** : CSV export functionality tested with permissions-based filtering validated across 15 user scenarios. Evidence: Export test results, data filtering validation, permissions audit report.

**Quality and Performance Gates:**

* **Performance Benchmarks** : Dashboard load time ≤3 seconds validated across 100 test scenarios with 95% success rate. Evidence: Performance testing report, load time metrics dashboard, optimization recommendations.
* **Uptime Requirements** : 99.9% uptime target with comprehensive monitoring and alerting system deployed. Evidence: Monitoring dashboard configuration, SLA tracking setup, incident response procedures.
* **Data Accuracy Validation** : Cross-system data validation automated testing with <1% variance tolerance across all metric categories. Evidence: Data validation test suite, variance analysis report, discrepancy tracking system.
* **Security Compliance** : Security review passed with 0 high-severity findings and multi-tenant data segregation validated. Evidence: Security audit report, penetration testing results, compliance certification.
* **Integration Testing** : Customer SSO and Stellarus authentication integration tested with 100% success rate across target authentication providers. Evidence: Integration test results, authentication flow validation, error handling verification.

**Business Readiness:**

* **Training Completion** : Operations team training completed with 100% stakeholder certification and documented competency validation. Evidence: Training completion certificates, competency assessment results, stakeholder sign-off documentation.
* **Documentation Delivery** : Complete documentation package delivered including user guides (≥90% user satisfaction score), admin procedures (validated by operations team), and troubleshooting playbooks (tested against 10 common issues). Evidence: Documentation review approval, user feedback survey results, troubleshooting validation report.
* **Success Metrics Foundation** : Baseline metrics established with automated tracking implementation and first 48-hour operational validation completed. Evidence: Metrics dashboard validation, baseline measurement report, automated tracking verification results.

## 📋 Linear Development Issues

*Following the Linear Method, these issues are written as actionable, scoped technical tasks rather than user stories.*

### Project: Dashboard Foundation & Data Layer

#### [CPD-01] Scaffold Next.js Application and CI/CD Pipeline
**Context:** A foundational repository is required to establish the frontend tooling, routing, and deployment processes so parallel engineering can begin.
**Scope:**
- Initialize Next.js 14+ (App Router) with TypeScript and Tailwind CSS.
- Setup Prettier, ESLint, and Husky pre-commit hooks.
- Configure GitHub Actions pipeline to run tests, lint checks, and deploy a skeleton build to the staging environment.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Repository is accessible and runs locally without errors.
- Pushing to `main` triggers a successful CI/CD deployment to staging.

#### [CPD-02] Implement Databricks & MLflow Connection Utilities
**Context:** The dashboard requires backend access to real-time performance telemetry housed in Databricks and MLflow.
**Scope:**
- Implement server-side client wrappers utilizing the Databricks SQL Connector and MLflow REST APIs.
- Establish a caching layer (e.g., node-cache or Redis) with a 30-second TTL to support real-time polling without overloading the data stores.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Utility methods successfully return raw performance data from both Databricks and MLflow.
- Repeated requests within the 30-second TTL correctly serve data from the cache.

#### [CPD-03] Implement Multi-Tenant Authentication (NextAuth)
**Context:** We need to authenticate two separate groups: Customer Operations (via their respective SSO) and Internal Stellarus users.
**Scope:**
- Configure `NextAuth.js` with SAML/OAuth2 providers for customers and internal corporate providers for Stellarus.
- Map and append custom claims to the JWT session: `role` (customer | stellarus) and `tenant_id`.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Users are successfully redirected to their respective SSO log-in and securely authenticated.
- The application session exposes accurate `tenant_id` and `role` properties.

#### [CPD-04] Enforce Tenant Data Isolation Middleware
**Context:** Misconfigured API routes risk leaking data across customer bounds. Isolation must be handled systematically before data is fetched.
**Scope:**
- Create a Next.js server-side utility/middleware that intercepts data fetches and injects `WHERE tenant_id = ?` into Databricks queries.
- Reject any cross-tenant query request automatically unless the user has the `stellarus` role.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Customer API requests explicitly return only data scoped to their `tenant_id`.
- Test coverage confirms requests for arbitrary tenant IDs by customer roles return a 403 Forbidden.

### Project: Customer-Facing Analytics

#### [CPD-05] Build Real-Time KPI Cards Component
**Context:** Users need an at-a-glance visualization of core health metrics at the top of the dashboard.
**Scope:**
- Build the reusable `<KpiCard />` React component.
- Implement SWR/React Query hooks to poll the backend data endpoints every 30 seconds.
- Implement frontend logic to calculate the (↑/↓) change from a 7-day trailing average.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- 6 KPI cards render accurately according to the wireframes.
- Values auto-refresh on screen without page reloads.
- Components render loading skeleton states during data fetches.

#### [CPD-06] Develop Response Time & Health Distribution Charts
**Context:** Deep-dive line charts are needed to evaluate historical application performance.
**Scope:**
- Integrate charting library (e.g., Recharts or Chart.js).
- Build the "Response Time Distribution" line chart charting Min/Max/Avg/Median/StdDev.
- Build the "Application Health" multi-line chart charting Uptime % and Error Rates.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Charts handle 1000+ data points cleanly without UI lag.
- Tooltips on hover expose the exact timestamps and metric values.
- Time Range toggles (7/30/90 Days) dynamically update the chart data.

#### [CPD-07] Implement Session & Product Pipeline Analytics
**Context:** Dashboards require visibility into customer usage patterns and product pipeline ingestion success metrics.
**Scope:**
- Build the "Session Analytics" bar chart and "Questions per Session" histogram.
- Develop the dual-chart interface for Product Pipeline analytics (Success vs Failure rates).
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Data automatically groups into daily/weekly/monthly buckets based on the selected time range.
- Numerical axes format cleanly (e.g., 1.2K instead of 1200).

### Project: Internal Stellarus Analytics

#### [CPD-08] Build Internal Cost Management Dashboard
**Context:** The Stellarus finance and operations teams require a view to monitor infrastructure cost efficiency.
**Scope:**
- Build a stacked bar chart mapping Cost per Question vs. Cost per Session.
- Implement the aggregation logic across all tenants (Internal access only).
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Logged in `stellarus` users can view the global, cross-tenant Cost Analysis chart.
- Requests from `customer` users to this view/API immediately return 403 Forbidden.

#### [CPD-09] Build Business Intelligence Module (Churn & Growth)
**Context:** We must automatically flag at-risk and high-growth accounts based on their telemetry data.
**Scope:**
- Write the backend Databricks queries that calculate relative session velocity across a 30-day window.
- Render a tabulated "Customer Health" data table summarizing Revenue, Usage Deltas, and Risk Scores.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Customers with >25% drop in sessions are explicitly highlighted as "Churn Risk".
- Table allows sorting by Risk Score and Expansion Opportunity.

### Project: Alerting & Exporting

#### [CPD-10] Implement Secure CSV Data Export Endpoint
**Context:** Operations personnel require raw data extracts for use in external compliance/reporting tools.
**Scope:**
- Build an API endpoint `/api/export` that generates a streamed CSV from the telemetry queries.
- Strictly enforce the existing Data Isolation logic within the export generation.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Download button successfully yields a well-formatted CSV matching the user's dashboard view.
- Customer CSV exports never contain rows belonging to another `tenant_id`.

#### [CPD-11] Build Custom Alert Configuration UI
**Context:** Teams need to be notified when performance degrades past customized thresholds.
**Scope:**
- Build a settings UI form allowing users to select a metric, an operator (>, <), and a threshold value.
- Provide a multi-select for Notification preferences (Email, UI, Slack).
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Configurations persist to the database.
- Users can edit, disable, or delete existing alert thresholds.

#### [CPD-12] Implement Background Alert Evaluation Worker
**Context:** Alert rules need to run constantly without depending on an active browser session.
**Scope:**
- Build a standalone Node.js cron/worker that polls the Databricks/MLflow data layer every 2 minutes.
- If threshold logic is breached, generate a database alert record and trigger the appropriate email/Slack integrations.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Deliberately spiked data in the staging environment triggers an alert notification within the 2-minute SLA.
- Triggered alerts surface on the Dashboard's UI footer.

# 🧩 Project Name: Baseline Question-Answer Generation

**PDLC Phase:** Define
**Authored Date:** April 1, 2026
**Status:** DRAFT

## 🎯 Problem Statement

The Compass platform requires automated baseline "ground-truth" generation to scale beyond manual Q&A pair creation for thousands of customer plans. Manual baseline creation cannot meet the coverage requirements for comprehensive conversational AI accuracy across diverse plan types and benefit categories, creating a bottleneck for customer deployment and ongoing quality management.

**Impact:** Without automated baseline generation foundation, customer deployment will require unsustainable manual effort and cannot achieve the discovery accuracy needed for reliable member support workflows.

## 💡 Proposed Solution

Implement core AI-powered question extraction engine that automatically generates baseline question-answer pairs ("Ground Truths") from plan documents, establishing the foundational capability for automated discovery. The solution processes plan data from customer integration and creates structured Q&A pairs that serve as the basis for quality measurement and validation workflows.

## 👥 Target Users

**Primary Users:**

* **Customer Representavies:** Need automated baseline generation to allow human Q&A validation over creation effort and improve plan coverage
* **Compass AI Platform:** Requires baseline question-answer pairs for conversational accuracy and response quality

**Secondary Users:**

* **Product Engineering Teams:** Need baseline generation foundation for F3B benchmarking and F3C validation features

## ✅ Success Metrics

- **Generation Output:** Produce 500+ baseline question-answer pairs per plan type through automated extraction (Baseline: Manual creation only)
- **Plan Coverage:** Achieve automated baseline generation for 100% of customer plan types integrated (Baseline: 0% automated coverage)
- **Processing Efficiency:** Complete baseline generation for entire plan portfolio within 48 hours of plan data updates (Measurement Window: Weekly monitoring)

## 📦 Scope

What's included in this release?

- AI-powered question extraction engine that processes plan documents and identifies relevant question patterns
- Baseline question-answer pair generation system producing structured Q&A content
- Plan document processing pipeline integrating with F1A plan data foundation
- Basic quality scoring for generated baseline relevance and completeness
- Question categorization by benefit type and plan coverage areas
- Generated content formatting compatible with downstream validation processes

## 🚫 Out-of-Scope

What's explicitly out of scope?

- Advanced quality benchmarking and accuracy measurement frameworks
- Human validation workflow integration and approval processes
- Cross-customer baseline learning and pattern recognition
- Real-time baseline updates during live conversations
- Adaptive Baseline automation and drift detection
- Custom baseline editing and management interfaces

## 🏁 Exit Criteria

Task list of statements that define when implementation of this PRD would be considered complete.

* [ ] AI-powered question extraction engine successfully processes plan documents from customer plan data integration
* [ ] Baseline generation system produces 500+ question-answer pairs per plan type for all BSC plan types
* [ ] Generated Q&A pairs cover key benefit categories with appropriate question variety and depth
* [ ] Basic quality scoring evaluates generated baseline relevance and completeness with consistent criteria
* [ ] Question categorization accurately organizes baselines by benefit type and coverage area

Based on comprehensive UX evaluation of the current Mira interface (powered by Minerva APIs), this document proposes **six focused Feature PRDs** that address critical usability barriers while advancing strategic cost optimization and agent adoption objectives. **Strategic Imperative:** UX improvements are not optional enhancements—they are critical enablers of cost optimization through increased adoption, reduced training overhead, decreased support costs, and elimination of redundant tool usage.

- **Training Costs:** Intuitive, low-code UI reduces onboarding time by 50% and eliminates recurring training overhead

## PRD Structure

### PRD-1: Low-Code/No-Code UI Platform Foundation & Configuration Framework

### Problem Statement

Current Mira UI creates adoption barriers through fixed positioning, full-screen takeovers, and inflexible interface patterns that disrupt agent workflows during live calls. Each customer deployment requires custom development, creating unsustainable costs and slow deployment cycles. Agents need a contextual, adaptable interface that integrates seamlessly with existing workflows while enabling customer-specific branding, layout, and configuration without engineering effort.

### Strategic Alignment

- **Cost Impact:**

  - Eliminate custom UI development costs (estimated 50% reduction in per-customer deployment costs)
  - Reduce training overhead by 50% through intuitive, self-service configuration
  - Decrease support costs by 40% through better workflow integration
  - Enable rapid multi-customer scaling supporting cost-per-query optimization through volume
- **Adoption Driver:** Flexible, contextual interface increases agent confidence and sustained usage, directly supporting >90% adoption target
- **Quality Enabler:** Better workflow integration reduces misquoting risk and maintains >98% accuracy standards

### Success Metrics (Measurable)

- **Workflow Disruption:** Reduce agent workflow disruption by 60% (measured via user session analysis and time-to-task metrics)
- **Configuration Adoption:** >80% of customers utilize white-label customization within 30 days of deployment
- **Agent Preference:** Interface customization adoption >80% within 30 days of agent access
- **Support Reduction:** Support tickets for UI-related issues reduced by 50% compared to Mira baseline
- **Deployment Speed:** Customer deployment time reduced from weeks to days (target: 3-day deployment cycle)

- Collapsible/expandable states with discoverable affordances (tooltips, first-run coachmarks)
- Multiple docking positions: right-sidebar (default), left-sidebar, bottom-panel, floating
- Picture-in-picture mode for minimal footprint during non-query states

**White-Label Configuration:**

- Customer-defined default position, size, and docking behavior
- Agent-level override capabilities with workspace preference saving
- Responsive layout adaptation based on customer application constraints

#### B. White-Label Branding & Theming Framework

**Enables:** Customer-specific branding without code changes, supporting multi-tenant deployment model
